def_en: to cause something to happen in a violent and often uncontrolled way
prep_trap: 專用於固定高分慣用語：wreak havoc on（對環境、健康或經濟造成浩劫/嚴重破壞，注意 w 不發音，介詞配 on）！
example: Extreme weather events such as super typhoons can wreak havoc on coastal cities and infrastructure.

def_zh: 招致；意味著（災難或麻煩）；一段時間（名詞）
def_en: to have something, usually something bad, as a result
prep_trap: 議論文地道高分搭配：spell disaster for / spell trouble for（對…意味著災難，如對小店或生態系統帶來厄運）。
example: Reclaiming the natural wetland would spell disaster for migratory birds and marine ecosystems.

def_zh: 轉化為（實際成果或行動）；翻譯
def_en: to change something into a new form, especially to turn ideas into actions or results
prep_trap: 在議論文中，translate into 是極高分的論證片語，解作「轉化為/帶來（某種實際結果）」（put theory into practice and translate ideas into action）。
example: Environmental awareness alone means nothing unless it translates into concrete daily actions.

def_zh: 以…達到高潮；最終以…告終（必配介詞 in）
def_en: if an event or series of events culminates in something, it ends with it, having developed until it reaches this point
prep_trap: Paper 3 介紹大型活動壓軸環節或 Paper 2 敘事高分動詞：必須搭配介詞 in（The Music Week will culminate in a grand finale concert）。
example: The five-day English Festival will culminate in an inter-class drama competition on Friday afternoon.

def_zh: 使變得；使處於（某種不利狀態，如無家可歸或過時）
def_en: to cause someone or something to be in a particular state
prep_trap: 替換 make + sb/sth + adj. 的滿分正式動詞！結構為 render + 賓語 + 形容詞（render low-skilled workers jobless / render traditional skills obsolete）。
example: Rapid automation and artificial intelligence may render many repetitive clerical jobs obsolete in future.

def_zh: 使享有…的權利；使有資格獲得（優惠或福利）
def_en: to give someone the right to do or have something
prep_trap: Paper 3 會員福利與社會保障題必考：被動結構 be entitled to（享有…的權利，注意 to 是介詞，後接名詞或 V-ing）！
example: Senior citizens holding a JoyYou Card are entitled to two-dollar public transport fares.

def_zh: 賦權；使具備能力與自信去自主行動
def_en: to give someone official authority or the freedom to do something, or to make someone stronger and more confident
prep_trap: 弱勢社群、青年發展及教育題極高分動詞：結構為 empower sb to do sth（賦予某人能力與自信去做某事）。
example: Providing free vocational training empowers low-income single mothers to become financially independent.

def_zh: 使能夠；使得以
def_en: to make someone able to do something, or to make something possible
prep_trap: 替換 let / make sb can do（Chinglish 病句！）的最安全動詞：結構永遠是 enable sb to do sth！
example: Online learning platforms enable students to review recorded lectures at their own pace.

def_zh: 容許；讓；使有可能
def_en: to give permission for someone to do something, or to not prevent something from happening
prep_trap: 注意與 let 的語法分別：let sb do sth（不加 to），但 allow 有人作受詞時必須加 to（allow sb to do sth）；若無受詞直接接動作，則用 V-ing（We do not allow smoking）。
example: Flexible working hours allow working parents to spend more time caring for their children.

def_zh: 准許；允許（動詞）；許可證（名詞）
def_en: to allow something, or an official document that allows you to do something
prep_trap: 過去式須雙寫 tt（permitted）；戶外活動通告極常用獨立分詞結構：weather permitting（如天氣許可）。
example: Weather permitting, the graduation photo-taking session will be held on the school lawn.

def_zh: 迫使；強迫（不得不做某事）
def_en: to force someone to do something
prep_trap: 原形單 l（com-pel），過去式及現在分詞必須雙寫 ll（compelled / compelling）！句型：compel sb to do sth；此外形容詞 compelling 解作「極具說服力的/引人入勝的（compelling reason/evidence）」。
example: Skyrocketing living costs have compelled many elderly citizens to continue working after retirement.

def_zh: 使負有義務；迫使（依法或依責任必須做）
def_en: to force someone to do something, or to make it necessary for someone to do something
prep_trap: 最常用被動結構：be obliged to do sth（有義務/被迫做某事，名詞為 moral obligation 道德責任）。
example: Under the new ordinance, employers are legally obliged to provide safe working equipment.

def_zh: 強制規定；下令要求；授權
def_en: to give official permission for something to happen, or to order someone to do something
prep_trap: 形容詞 mandatory 的動詞形：常寫 The law mandates that... 或 mandate companies to reduce emissions。
example: The new environmental policy mandates that all large restaurants separate their daily food waste.

def_zh: 克制；避免；切勿（做某種不當行為，公眾告示常用）
def_en: to avoid doing or stop yourself from doing something
prep_trap: Paper 3 守則與通告禮貌禁止某行為的滿分句型：Please refrain from eating or drinking（請勿飲食，必須配介詞 from + V-ing）！
example: Audience members are kindly requested to refrain from taking flash photographs during the concert.

def_zh: 戒除；避免（煙酒或不健康習慣）；棄權（投票）
def_en: to not do something, especially something enjoyable that you think might be bad, or to choose not to vote
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，與 refrain 一樣必須搭配介詞 from（abstain from alcohol and tobacco 戒煙戒酒）。
example: Doctors strongly advise pregnant women to completely abstain from alcohol and smoking.

def_zh: 避免；避開；防止
def_en: to stay away from someone or something, or prevent something from happening
prep_trap: DSE 基礎必考動詞陷阱：avoid 後面若接動詞，永遠只能接動名詞 V-ing（avoid staying up late），絕對不可接 to do！
example: To maintain good health, citizens should avoid eating deep-fried and processed foods regularly.

def_zh: 逃避（責任、法律制裁或稅款）
def_en: to avoid or escape from someone or something, especially duty or tax
prep_trap: 及物動詞，專門搭配「不道德或非法地逃避責任」（evade responsibility / evade legal liability / tax evasion 逃稅）。
example: Anonymous internet users should not be allowed to evade legal responsibility for cyberbullying others.

def_zh: 推卸；逃避（責任、義務或工作）
def_en: to avoid work, duties, or responsibilities, especially if they are difficult or unpleasant
prep_trap: DSE 批評政府、企業或家長推卸責任的精準及物動詞：shirk one's responsibility / duty。
example: Parents cannot shirk their responsibility for teaching moral values by relying entirely on schools.

def_zh: 依賴；依靠；仰賴（必配 on/upon）
def_en: to need a particular thing or the help and support of someone or something in order to continue, to work correctly, or to succeed
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，第三人稱單數為 relies，過去式為 relied；必須搭配介詞 on/upon（rely heavily on fossil fuels）；名詞為 over-reliance on（過度依賴…）。
example: Over-reliance on artificial intelligence tools may weaken students' independent thinking and writing skills.

def_zh: 訴諸於；被迫採取（不良或最後手段，必配介詞 to）；度假勝地
def_en: to do something that you do not want to do because you cannot find any other way of achieving something
prep_trap: DSE 必考高分介詞陷阱！resort to 中的 to 是介詞，專門指走投無路下「訴諸某種負面手段」，後接名詞或動名詞 V-ing（resort to violence / resort to stealing / as a last resort 作為最後手段）！
example: Desperate teenagers facing financial trouble should seek help rather than resorting to illegal jobs.

def_zh: 向…求助（turn to）；對…視而不見（turn a blind eye to）
def_en: to go to someone or something for help, or to ignore something that you know is wrong
prep_trap: 兩大必背片語（當中的 to 皆為介詞）：1. turn to sb for help（向某人求助）；2. turn a blind eye to（對某問題視若無睹）。
collocations: turn to social workers for help
example: Society must no longer turn a blind eye to the plight of homeless people.

def_zh: 應付；處理；承受（壓力或逆境，必配 with）
def_en: to deal successfully with a difficult situation
prep_trap: DSE 萬年病句重災區！cope 是不及物動詞，後面必須加介詞 with（cope with academic stress），千萬不可直接寫 cope the problem（那是用 tackle / handle）！
example: Schools should organize mental health workshops to teach students how to cope with stress.

def_zh: 學業的；學術的；大學學者
def_en: relating to schools, colleges, and universities, or connected with studying and thinking, not with practical skills
prep_trap: 注意拼法為 ac-a-dem-ic（切勿與 academy 混淆詞性）；DSE 教育題最高頻搭配：academic performance（學業成績）、academic pressure（學業壓力）。
example: Excessive parental expectations often place immense academic pressure on secondary school students in Hong Kong.

def_zh: 全人的；全面的；整體的（發展或教育）
def_en: dealing with or treating the whole of something or someone and not just a part
prep_trap: DSE 教育題滿分詞彙（替換 all-round development）：注意開頭沒有 w（ho-lis-tic，雖與 whole 意思相近但拼法不同）！
example: Extracurricular activities play a vital role in fostering the holistic development of young people.

def_zh: 職業導向的；職業訓練的
def_en: providing skills and education that prepare you for a job
prep_trap: 注意開頭是 vo-ca-（與意為「假期的」vacation 差一個字母 o！）；常指職業訓練局（VTC）類型的專業技能課程（vocational training）。
example: Vocational training programmes provide practical alternative pathways for students who are less academically inclined.

def_zh: 教學法的；教育學的
def_en: relating to the methods and theory of teaching
prep_trap: 教育議論題進階詞：用來修飾教學方法或工具（pedagogical approach / value）。
example: Field trips have great pedagogical value because they allow students to learn outside classrooms.

def_zh: 死記硬背；機械式背誦
def_en: learning something in order to be able to repeat it from memory, rather than in order to understand it
prep_trap: 批評香港傳統填鴨式教育必備詞！固定搭配為 rote learning / rote memorization，或 learn by rote（死記硬背）。
example: Traditional rote learning stifles students' creativity and fails to develop their critical thinking skills.

def_zh: 填鴨式教育；過度餵飼式的教導
def_en: giving someone so much help or information that they do not need to think for themselves
prep_trap: 注意中間有連字號（spoon-feeding）；作動詞時過去式為 spoon-fed（Children are spoon-fed by helicopter parents）。
example: Instead of spoon-feeding students with model answers, teachers should encourage independent inquiry and discussion.

def_zh: 臨時抱佛腳（應付考試）；把…塞進；密集補習
def_en: to try to learn a lot very quickly before an exam, or to force a lot of things into a small space
prep_trap: 過去式及現在分詞必須雙寫 mm（crammed / cramming）！為考試臨時抱佛腳介詞用 cram for an exam；補習社亦可稱 cram school。
example: Staying up all night to cram for an examination is both stressful and ineffective.

def_zh: 抄襲；剽竊（功課、論文或創作）
def_en: the process or practice of using another person's ideas or work and pretending that it is your own
prep_trap: AI 與學術誠信題必考名詞（不可數）：動詞為 plagiarize；犯抄襲罪用 commit plagiarism。
example: Copy-pasting essays generated by artificial intelligence without proper citation is a form of plagiarism.

def_zh: 素養；識字能力；對某領域的認知能力
def_en: the ability to read and write, or knowledge of a particular subject
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 現代議題三大神級搭配：digital literacy（數碼素養）、media literacy（傳媒素養）、financial literacy（理財素養）。
example: Schools should teach financial literacy so that teenagers learn how to save money wisely.

def_zh: 精通；熟練程度；造詣（尤指語言或技能）
def_en: great skill, ability, and experience in doing something
prep_trap: 替換 language level / ability 的高分不可數名詞（形容詞為 proficient）：在某語言的造詣介詞用 proficiency in English。
example: Reading English newspapers daily is an effective way to improve one's language proficiency.

def_zh: 能力；勝任力；才幹
def_en: the ability to do something well
prep_trap: 注意字尾是 -ence（形容詞為 competent 能幹的），切勿與意為「競爭」的 competition 或「競爭力」的 competitiveness 混淆！
example: Group projects help students develop communication competence and leadership skills needed in the workplace.

def_zh: 競爭力
def_en: the ability of a person, company, or city to compete successfully with others
prep_trap: DSE 生涯規劃與香港發展題必備不可數名詞！提升個人或城市的競爭力：enhance one's competitiveness in the job market。
example: Mastering trilingual skills can greatly enhance graduates' competitiveness in the global job market.

def_zh: 潛能；潛力（不可數名詞）；潛在的（形容詞）
def_en: someone's or something's ability to develop, achieve, or succeed, or possible when the necessary conditions exist
prep_trap: 作名詞「潛能」時是不可數名詞，千萬不可加 -s（不可寫 potentials）！發揮潛能搭配動詞 unleash / realize / fulfil one's full potential。
example: Summer talent shows provide a stage for shy students to unleash their artistic potential.

def_zh: 創造力；創意
def_en: the ability to produce or use original and unusual ideas
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（切勿把形容詞 creative 當名詞用！）；激發創意用 stimulate/spark creativity，扼殺創意用 stifle creativity。
example: Visual arts and drama lessons stimulate students' creativity and encourage them to think outside the box.

def_zh: 好奇心；求知慾
def_en: an eager wish to know or learn about something
prep_trap: 注意形容詞是 curious（有 u），但變名詞時去 u 加 -ity（cu-ri-os-i-ty，中間沒有 u）！出於好奇固定搭配為 out of curiosity。
example: Some rebellious teenagers try smoking or vaping simply out of curiosity and peer influence.

def_zh: 眼界；視野（常作複數）；地平線
def_en: the limit of your desires, knowledge, or interests, or the line where the sky meets the earth
prep_trap: DSE 作文第一高頻片語 broaden one's horizons：指抽象「眼界/視野」時，horizon 永遠必須加 -s 用複數！
example: Participating in overseas study tours can broaden students' horizons and foster global citizenship.

def_zh: 視角；觀點；看待事物的角度
def_en: a particular way of considering something
prep_trap: 注意開頭是 per- 而非 pre-（per-spec-tive）；從某個角度來看，介詞搭配為 from a different perspective / from the perspective of parents。
example: Debating teaches students to examine controversial social issues from multiple perspectives.

def_zh: 心態；思維模式；觀念
def_en: a person's way of thinking and their opinions
prep_trap: 一字連寫，替換 attitude 的高分詞：常見搭配 positive mindset（積極心態）、growth mindset（成長型思維）。
example: Students with a growth mindset view exam failures as valuable opportunities to learn and improve.

def_zh: 抗逆力；心理韌性；復原力
def_en: the ability to be happy, successful, etc. again after something difficult or bad has happened
prep_trap: DSE 青少年心理題必背王牌詞！（形容詞為 resilient 具抗逆力的）：培養抗逆力用 build / foster resilience。
collocations: resilience in the face of adversity
example: Adventure training camps help teenagers build mental resilience so they can bounce back from setbacks.

def_zh: 毅力；堅持不懈；恆心
def_en: continued effort to do or achieve something, even when this is difficult or takes a long time
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意字尾是 -ance 而非 -ence（per-se-ver-ance）！運動與勵志題必備。
example: Running a full marathon requires not only physical stamina but also extraordinary mental perseverance.

def_zh: 堅毅；勇氣與毅力
def_en: courage and determination despite difficulty
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，現代教育心理學極推崇的短小精悍高分詞（grit and determination 堅毅與決心）。
example: Overcoming physical disabilities to win a Paralympic medal requires immense grit and determination.

def_zh: 自律；自我克制
def_en: the ability to make yourself do things you know you should do even when you do not want to
prep_trap: 極高頻拼錯字！discipline 中間有 sc（dis-ci-pline），千萬不可漏寫 c！不可數名詞。
example: Online learning at home requires a high degree of self-discipline and time management skills.

def_zh: 自主權；獨立自主
def_en: the ability to make your own decisions without being controlled by anyone else
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（形容詞為 autonomous 自主的）：給予青少年適度自主權用 grant teenagers greater autonomy。
example: Parents should grant older teenagers greater autonomy in choosing their own university electives.

def_zh: 獨立；自立；自主
def_en: the ability to live your life without being helped or influenced by other people
prep_trap: 極高頻拼錯字！全字後半段全是 e，沒有 a（in-de-pend-ence，形容詞為 independent）！培養獨立性用 foster independence。
example: Going on an overseas exchange trip without parents helps teenagers develop a sense of independence.

def_zh: 自尊；自信心；自我價值感
def_en: belief and confidence in your own ability and value
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，含連字號（self-esteem）：提升自尊用 boost self-esteem，自卑則是 low self-esteem。
example: Praising children for their effort rather than just grades helps build healthy self-esteem.

def_zh: 融洽關係；互信默契（尤指師生、親子或同事之間）
def_en: a good understanding of someone and an ability to communicate well with them
prep_trap: 法文借詞，字尾 t 不發音（rap-port，讀 /ræˈpɔːr/）；與某人建立融洽關係固定搭配為 build/establish a good rapport with sb。
example: Chatting casually during lunch breaks helps teachers build a strong rapport with their students.

def_zh: 同儕情誼；團隊友情與互信
def_en: a feeling of friendliness towards people that you work or share an experience with
prep_trap: 校園營會及運動隊伍題衝 5* 亮點詞：指隊友間並肩作戰的深厚情誼（foster camaraderie among teammates）。
example: Overcoming tough obstacle courses together at the camp fostered a strong sense of camaraderie.

def_zh: 凝聚力；團結一致
def_en: the situation when the members of a group or society are united
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（形容詞為 cohesive 有凝聚力的）：班級凝聚力為 class cohesion，社會凝聚力為 social cohesion。
example: Inter-class singing contests are a wonderful way to strengthen class cohesion and team spirit.

def_zh: 歸屬感（a sense of belonging）；個人財物（複數 belongings）
def_en: a feeling of being happy and comfortable as part of a particular group
prep_trap: DSE 必考單複數差異！1. 單數不可數：a sense of belonging to the school（對學校的歸屬感，介詞必用 to！）；2. 複數加 -s：personal belongings（個人隨身財物）。
example: Wearing the school uniform helps cultivate a strong sense of belonging to the school.

def_zh: 同輩；同齡人；同儕
def_en: a person who is the same age or has the same social position or the same abilities as other people in a group
prep_trap: 替換 friends / classmates 的核心詞：指「同儕（壓力/學習/支持）」作定語時用單數（peer pressure / peer learning）；指「同輩們」作名詞時加 -s（compare oneself with peers）。
example: Peer tutoring programmes allow senior students to help junior peers overcome academic difficulties.

def_zh: 青春期；青少年時期
def_en: the period of time in a person's life when they are developing into an adult
prep_trap: 注意中間有 sc（ad-o-les-cence）：adolescence 是不可數名詞「青春期」（during adolescence），而 adolescent 則是可數名詞「青少年（= teenager）」或形容詞！
example: During adolescence, young people often experience rapid emotional changes and seek peer recognition.

def_zh: 青少年（名詞）；青春期的（形容詞）
def_en: a young person who is developing into an adult
prep_trap: 替換過於重複的 teenagers / young people 的絕佳正式同義詞！注意中間有 sc（ad-o-les-cent）。
example: Parents need to show extra patience and empathy when communicating with rebellious adolescents.

def_zh: 少年的；未成年人的（常配犯罪問題）
def_en: relating to a young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult
prep_trap: 法律與社會問題專用詞（不可泛指一般好學生）：固定搭配 juvenile delinquency（青少年犯罪）及 juvenile offenders（少年犯）。
example: Lack of parental care and negative peer influence are major causes of juvenile delinquency.

def_zh: （尤指青少年的）違法行為；不良行為；犯罪
def_en: behaviour, especially of a young person, that is illegal or not acceptable to most people
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意中間是 -lin-quen-cy（有 q）；少年罪犯為 juvenile delinquent。
example: Evening outreach social workers play a key role in steering youths away from delinquency.

def_zh: 反叛的；叛逆的；難管教的
def_en: unwilling to obey rules or accept normal standards of behaviour, dress, etc.
prep_trap: 注意雙寫 ll（re-bel-lious，名詞為 rebellion 叛逆）；常用於形容處於反叛期的青少年。
example: Harsh scolding and physical punishment will only make teenagers more rebellious and distant.

def_zh: 衝動的；一時興起行事的（不顧後果）
def_en: showing behaviour in which you do things suddenly without any planning and without considering the effects they may have
prep_trap: 網購題（衝動消費 impulsive buying）及青少年心理題必備形容詞；一時衝動固定用 on impulse。
example: Flash sales and credit cards often tempt young consumers into impulsive buying online.

def_zh: （因年幼或涉世未深而）易受影響的；易被左右心智的
def_en: easily influenced by other people, especially because you are young
prep_trap: DSE 傳媒、廣告與青少年題衝 5* 神級形容詞！由 impression + -able 構成（impressionable youths 易受影響的青少年）。
example: Strict regulations are needed to protect impressionable children from misleading online gambling advertisements.

def_zh: 脆弱的；易受傷害的；弱勢的（必配介詞 to）
def_en: able to be easily physically, emotionally, or mentally hurt, influenced, or attacked
prep_trap: 注意開頭是 vul-ner-（有 l 及 r）！必考介詞搭配：be vulnerable to（易受…傷害/影響，如 vulnerable to cyberbullying / heatstroke，to 是介詞）！此外 the vulnerable / vulnerable groups 指「弱勢社群」。
example: Elderly people living alone are particularly vulnerable to telephone deception and extreme weather.

def_zh: 易受影響的；易患（某疾病）的（必配介詞 to）
def_en: easily influenced or harmed by something
prep_trap: 注意中間有 sc（sus-cep-ti-ble），字尾是 -ible；與 vulnerable 一樣，後面必須加介詞 to（susceptible to peer pressure / infectious diseases）！
example: Children with weak immune systems are highly susceptible to seasonal influenza and colds.

def_zh: 易於發生（不良事情）的；有…傾向的（必配 to）
def_en: likely to suffer from an illness or show a particular negative characteristic
prep_trap: DSE 必考介詞陷阱！be prone to 中的 to 是介詞（但常也可接原形動詞或名詞），最穩陣用法是接名詞或動名詞 V-ing（be prone to anxiety / making mistakes，专门接負面事物）！
example: Teenagers who spend excessive time on social media are more prone to anxiety.

def_zh: 對…上癮的；沉迷於…的（必配介詞 to）
def_en: unable to stop taking drugs, or doing something as a habit
prep_trap: DSE 科技題頭號介詞陷阱！be/become/get addicted to 中的 to 是介詞，後面必須接名詞或 V-ing（be addicted to playing mobile games），絕對不可寫 addicted to play！
example: Many secondary students have become addicted to scrolling through short videos late at night.

def_zh: 過分著迷於…的；對…耿耿於懷的（必配 with）
def_en: unable to stop thinking about something; too interested in or worried about something
prep_trap: 必考介詞搭配：addicted 配 to，但 obsessed 卻必須配介詞 with（be obsessed with getting 'likes' / body shape）！注意中間雙寫 ss（ob-sessed）。
example: Some young girls become unhealthy obsessed with slimming down to look like celebrities.

def_zh: 全神貫注於…的；心事重重的（以致忽略其他事，配 with）
def_en: thinking or worrying about something too much
prep_trap: 注意雙寫 cc（pre-oc-cu-pied）；必須搭配介詞 with（be preoccupied with work / smartphones）。
example: Diners nowadays are often too preoccupied with their smartphones to talk to family members.

def_zh: 疏離的；感到被排斥或格格不入的
def_en: feeling that you have no connection with the people around you
prep_trap: 内含 alien（外星人/異客）：名詞為 alienation（疏離感 social alienation）；與家人或社會疏離配介詞 from（feel alienated from family）。
example: New immigrant students may initially feel alienated from local classmates due to language barriers.

def_zh: 孤立的；與世隔絕的；個別的（個案）
def_en: feeling unhappy because of not seeing or talking to other people, or happening only once
prep_trap: 名詞為 social isolation（社交孤立）：長者或沉迷網絡者與社會脫節用 feel socially isolated from the community。
example: Hidden youths who lock themselves in their bedrooms for months become completely socially isolated.

def_zh: 性格內向的；羞怯寡言的
def_en: shy, quiet, and preferring to spend time alone rather than often being with other people
prep_trap: 名詞為 introvert（內向的人），形容詞為 introverted；反義詞則是 extroverted（外向的）。
example: Online discussion forums allow introverted students to express their views without feeling nervous.

def_zh: 性格外向的；活潑好交際的
def_en: energetic and enjoying being with other people
prep_trap: 替換 outgoing 的進階詞（名詞為 extrovert 外向者）：注意開頭是 ex-tro-。
example: Drama clubs and leadership camps naturally appeal to outgoing and extroverted secondary students.

def_zh: 有同理心的；善解人意的
def_en: having the ability to imagine how someone else feels
prep_trap: 由名詞 empathy 衍生：對某人有同理心搭配介詞 towards（be empathetic towards the needy）。
example: Visiting elderly homes regularly helps young people become more caring and empathetic towards seniors.

def_zh: 好學好問的；求知慾強的
def_en: wanting to discover as much as you can about things
prep_trap: 替換 curious 的高分正面形容詞（內含 quiz 提問字根）：an inquisitive mind（求知若渴的頭腦）。
example: Good science teachers always welcome tough questions from students with an inquisitive mind.

def_zh: 勤奮的；用功的；刻苦的
def_en: careful and using a lot of effort in your work or studies
prep_trap: 替換 hardworking 的首選高分形容詞！注意中間是 i，字尾是 -gent（dil-i-gent，名詞為 diligence 勤勉）。
example: Through diligent revision and regular practice, Sarah improved her English grade from Level 2 to 4.

def_zh: 盡責的；一絲不苟的；認真負責的
def_en: putting a lot of effort into your work
prep_trap: 推薦信或人物描寫衝 5* 形容詞！注意中間包含 science 去 e 加 -tious（con-sci-en-tious），切勿與意為「清醒/有意識的」conscious 混淆！
example: As a conscientious prefect, Alvin always arrives at school early to maintain order.

def_zh: 細心的；一絲不苟的；周密的（計劃或籌備）
def_en: very careful and with great attention to every detail
prep_trap: 替換 very careful 的高分詞：常用於讚賞活動籌備周密（meticulous planning）或工作極為細心。
example: Thanks to the committee's meticulous planning, the fiftieth anniversary banquet ran smoothly without any hitches.

def_zh: 足智多謀的；善於隨機應變解決問題的
def_en: skilled at solving problems and making decisions on your own
prep_trap: 注意形容「人」時，resourceful 解作「懂得靈活應變想辦法解決問題的」（而非解作富有資源！）。
example: Camping in the wild trains teenagers to become more independent and resourceful when facing difficulties.

def_zh: 多才多藝的（人）；多功能的（場地或工具）
def_en: able to change easily from one activity to another or able to be used for many different purposes
prep_trap: 注意拼法為 ver-sa-tile；形容人解「多才多藝」，形容設施或科技則解「多用途」。
example: Employers nowadays prefer versatile graduates who possess both technical knowledge and strong soft skills.

def_zh: 有能力的；能勝任的；稱職的
def_en: able to do something well
prep_trap: 注意字尾是 -tent（e），在某領域有能力搭配介詞 in 或 at（competent in handling emergencies）。
example: Having served as the club secretary for two years, Mary is highly competent in organizing events.

def_zh: 精通的；熟練的（尤指外語或電腦技能）
def_en: skilled and experienced
prep_trap: 替換 good at 的滿分形容詞！後面必須搭配介詞 in 或 at（be proficient in both written and spoken English）。
example: Applicants for the tourist ambassador post must be proficient in Putonghua and English.

def_zh: 充滿熱忱的；酷愛的；熱情的（必配 about）
def_en: having very strong feelings or emotions about something
prep_trap: 自薦信（Job Application Letter）必備！對某事充滿熱誠，後面介詞必須用 about（be passionate about environmental protection）！
example: I am writing to apply for the post of volunteer tutor because I am passionate about teaching children.

def_zh: 熱心的；滿腔熱忱的；踴躍的
def_en: showing enthusiasm
prep_trap: 注意中間是 -thu-si-as-tic（名詞為 enthusiasm 熱誠）；對某活動熱心投入介詞必須用 about（be enthusiastic about joining）。
example: The charity book sale received an overwhelmingly enthusiastic response from teachers and students alike.

def_zh: 冷漠的；無動於衷的；漠不關心的
def_en: showing no interest or energy and unwilling to take action, especially over something important
prep_trap: enthusiastic 的反義詞（名詞為 apathy 冷漠）：批評公眾或青少年對社會事務冷漠的高分詞，配介詞 towards/about。
example: Civic education is essential to prevent young people from becoming apathetic towards social issues.

def_zh: 漠不關心的；不以為然的；冷淡的（必配介詞 to）
def_en: not thinking about or interested in someone or something
prep_trap: DSE 閱讀與寫作常考陷阱！indifferent 絕對不是解作「不相同的（那是 different）」！它解作「冷漠不關心的」，且後面必須配介詞 to（be indifferent to the suffering of others）！
example: As responsible citizens, we should never remain indifferent to the suffering of the homeless.

def_zh: 不情願的；勉强的；猶豫不決的（不願做某事）
def_en: not willing to do something and therefore slow to do it
prep_trap: 替換 unwilling / don't want to 的高分形容詞！注意字尾是 -tant（a），句型為 be reluctant to do sth（不願意做某事）。
example: Many troubled teenagers are reluctant to seek help from school social workers due to embarrassment.

def_zh: 猶豫的；躊躇的；吞吞吐吐的
def_en: if you are hesitant, you do not do something immediately or quickly because you are nervous or not certain
prep_trap: 動詞為 hesitate（without hesitation 毫不猶豫地）；形容詞句型為 be hesitant to do sth 或 be hesitant about V-ing。
example: Students who lack confidence are often hesitant to speak English in front of classmates.

def_zh: 憂慮的；擔心不安的（對即將發生的未知事物，如公開試或新環境）
def_en: feeling worried about something that you are going to do or that is going to happen
prep_trap: 替換 worried / nervous 的高分心理形容詞：對未來某事感到擔憂，介詞必須用 about（feel apprehensive about the upcoming DSE）。
example: It is completely natural for Secondary Six students to feel apprehensive about the public examinations.

def_zh: 焦慮的；憂心忡忡的；急切的
def_en: worried and nervous
prep_trap: 注意拼法為 anx-ious（名詞為 anxiety 焦慮，中間有 e：anx-i-e-ty）！為某事感到焦慮介詞用 anxious about。
example: Practising deep breathing exercises before entering the exam hall can help calm anxious nerves.

def_zh: 不堪重負的；被（壓力、功課或情緒）壓得喘不過氣的
def_en: feeling sudden strong emotion, or having too much of something to deal with
prep_trap: DSE 描寫學業與工作壓力必背詞！注意中間有 h（o-ver-whelmed）；被繁重功課壓垮用 feel overwhelmed by/with heavy workloads。
example: Many junior form students feel overwhelmed by the sudden increase in subjects and homework.

def_zh: 感到挫敗的；沮喪的；洩氣的
def_en: feeling annoyed or less confident because you cannot achieve what you want
prep_trap: 注意第一個 r 不可漏寫（frus-trat-ed，切勿拼成 fustrated）！形容「人感到挫敗」用 -ed（feel frustrated with/by），形容「事情令人氣餒」用 -ing（frustrating）。
example: Students easily feel frustrated when their hard work does not immediately lead to higher grades.

def_zh: 灰心的；氣餒的；喪失信心的
def_en: having lost confidence, hope, and energy
prep_trap: 内含 heart（心）：對某結果感到灰心用 feel disheartened by repeated failures。
example: Even if you fail a mock test, you should not feel disheartened or give up.

def_zh: 士氣低落的；鬥志受挫的
def_en: having lost your confidence, enthusiasm, and hope
prep_trap: 源自 morale（士氣）：指因持續批評或失敗而令團隊或學生失去鬥志。
example: Constant harsh criticism from parents can leave children feeling completely demoralized and worthless.

def_zh: 困惑的；百思不得其解的；迷惘的
def_en: confused, because something is difficult to understand or solve
prep_trap: 替換 confused 的高分詞：對某事感到困惑用 feel perplexed by/about。
example: Many Secondary Three students feel perplexed about which elective subjects to choose for DSE.

def_zh: 不知所措的；迷茫困惑的
def_en: confused and uncertain
prep_trap: 比 confused 語氣更強，常形容面對過多選擇或巨變時手足無措（be bewildered by a wide array of choices）。
example: Elderly citizens often feel bewildered by complicated smartphone interfaces and electronic payment systems.

def_zh: 進退兩難的困境；左右為難的抉擇
def_en: a situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two different things you could do
prep_trap: 注意單 l 雙 mm（di-lem-ma）！處於進退兩難的局面固定搭配：be in a dilemma / face a moral dilemma。
example: Working mothers often face a painful dilemma between career advancement and caring for young children.

def_zh: 困境；窘境；尷尬艱難的處境
def_en: an unpleasant situation that is difficult to get out of
prep_trap: 替換 difficult situation 的高分可數名詞（pre-dic-a-ment）：尤指財政或生活上的窘境。
example: The government has set up an emergency fund to help unemployed workers out of their financial predicament.

def_zh: 苦況；悲慘境況（尤指弱勢社群或瀕危動物）
def_en: an unpleasant condition, especially a serious, sad, or difficult one
prep_trap: DSE 弱勢社群與動物權益題必背神字！固定以單數形式 the plight of... 出現（如 the plight of cage-home residents 籠屋居民的苦況）。
example: The photo exhibition aims to raise public awareness of the plight of homeless people.

def_zh: 逆境；厄運；重重困難
def_en: a difficult or unlucky situation or event
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 勵志與心理題必背黃金片語：in the face of adversity（面對逆境時） / overcome adversity（克服逆境）！
example: Maintaining a positive attitude enables us to stay strong in the face of adversity.

def_zh: 挫折；阻滯；倒退
def_en: something that happens that delays or prevents a process from developing
prep_trap: 可數名詞（一字連寫，常加 -s 作 setbacks）：遭遇挫折搭配動詞 suffer / experience / encounter a temporary setback。
example: Students should treat a poor exam result as a temporary setback rather than permanent failure.

def_zh: 障礙；絆腳石；難關
def_en: something that blocks you so that movement, going forward, or action is prevented or made more difficult
prep_trap: 注意拼法為 ob-sta-cle；成為某事的障礙，後面介詞必須用 to（an obstacle to success）！克服障礙用 overcome obstacles。
example: Physical disability should never be seen as an insurmountable obstacle to achieving one's dreams.

def_zh: 難關；跨欄；障礙
def_en: a problem that you have to deal with before you can make progress, or a frame to jump over in a race
prep_trap: 原指田徑跨欄，寫作中常比喻人生或計劃中需逐一跨越的「難關」（overcome/clear the first hurdle）。
example: Passing the written test is only the first hurdle for applicants seeking this scholarship.

def_zh: 障礙；壁壘；隔閡（如語言或文化隔閡）
def_en: anything that prevents people from being together or understanding each other, or a fence/wall
prep_trap: 注意雙寫 rr（bar-ri-er）；DSE 必背兩大搭配：language barrier（語言障礙）、break down cultural barriers（打破文化隔閡）；此外 barrier-free facilities 指「無障礙設施」。
example: Music and sports have the magical power to break down cultural and language barriers.

def_zh: 瓶頸（阻礙發展或流程的關鍵卡點）；交通樽頸位
def_en: a problem that delays progress, or a narrow road where traffic slows down
prep_trap: 一字連寫（bot-tle-neck）：常用於指土地不足或人手短缺成為香港發展的「瓶頸」。
example: A severe shortage of land and talent remains a major bottleneck for innovation development.

def_zh: 缺點；短處；不足之處
def_en: a fault or a failure to reach a particular standard
prep_trap: 可數名詞，一字連寫，常以複數形式 shortcomings 出現（替換 weaknesses / bad points）。
example: Self-reflection helps students recognize their own shortcomings and make continuous improvements in their studies.

def_zh: 缺陷；漏洞；瑕疵（制度、性格或論點上的）
def_en: a fault, mistake, or weakness, especially one that happens while something is being planned or made
prep_trap: 可數名詞，批評現行制度或教育制度有漏洞用 a fatal flaw in the system；形容詞 flawed 解作「有缺陷的（a flawed argument）」，flawless 則是「完美無瑕的」。
example: The tragic case exposed serious flaws in the current child protection reporting mechanism.

def_zh: 隱患；潛在陷阱；容易犯的錯誤
def_en: a likely mistake or problem in a situation
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常作複數 pitfalls（avoid the pitfalls of online shopping 避開網購的陷阱）。
example: Financial workshops teach young adults how to avoid the common pitfalls of credit card debt.

def_zh: 弊端；缺點；不利條件
def_en: a disadvantage or the negative part of a situation
prep_trap: 替換 disadvantage 的第一高頻可數名詞！一字連寫（draw-back），某事物的弊端介詞用 a major drawback of。
example: One major drawback of electric vehicles is the long charging time required for batteries.

def_zh: 優點；長處；價值（常作複數 merits）
def_en: the quality of being good and deserving praise
prep_trap: 替換 advantages and disadvantages 的高分對稱詞組：merits and demerits（優點與缺點）；此外校規中的「記優點/記缺點」亦稱 merits and demerits。
example: Before implementing the four-day work week, companies must carefully weigh its merits and demerits.

def_zh: 競爭優勢（competitive edge）；邊緣
def_en: an advantage over other people
prep_trap: DSE 職場與升學題必背黃金片語：give sb a competitive edge over others（令某人比其他人更具競爭優勢，介詞配 over）！
example: Proficiency in coding and data analysis gives university graduates a distinct competitive edge.

def_zh: 寶貴資產；有利條件；不可多得的人才
def_en: a useful or valuable quality, skill, or person
prep_trap: 注意雙寫 ss，單寫 t（as-set）：在推薦信或議論文中，讚揚人才或健康是寶貴資產用 a valuable asset to the company/society。
example: Good physical and mental health is the most valuable asset a person can possess.

def_zh: 催化劑；促成變革的推動力
def_en: an event or person that causes great change
prep_trap: 原為化學名詞，在議論文中比喻「促進正面改變或成長的催化劑」，後面介詞配 for（act as a catalyst for positive change）。
example: Hosting the international sports games acted as a catalyst for upgrading the city's infrastructure.

def_zh: 基石；基礎；最重要支柱
def_en: something of great importance that everything else depends on
prep_trap: 一字連寫，DSE 論述法治、教育或家庭重要性的滿分比喻詞：Education is the cornerstone of a prosperous society。
example: Mutual trust and honest communication form the cornerstone of a happy and harmonious family.

def_zh: 踏腳石；跳板（固定配 stepping stone）
def_en: an event or experience that helps you achieve something else
prep_trap: 專用於固定片語 a stepping stone to/towards future success（通往未來成功的踏腳石，形容實習、兼職或副學士課程）。
example: Summer internships serve as an important stepping stone for students entering the competitive business world.

def_zh: 雙刃的；有利亦有弊的（固定配 sword）
def_en: having two opposing effects, both good and bad
prep_trap: DSE 科技與社交媒體題開篇萬用金句：Artificial intelligence is a double-edged sword（是一把雙刃劍，注意 edged 必須有 -d）！
example: Social media is a double-edged sword that connects friends globally while breeding cyberbullying.

def_zh: 無處不在的；隨處可見的（尤指智能手機、AI 或塑膠）
def_en: seeming to be everywhere
prep_trap: 科技題首段引入背景的 5** 詞彙！開頭 u 發 /juː/ 音（u-biq-ui-tous）：Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life。
example: In the digital era, smartphones and wireless internet have become ubiquitous in our daily lives.

def_zh: 普遍的；盛行的；常見的（尤指不良現象或疾病）
def_en: existing very commonly or happening often
prep_trap: 替換 common 的第一高分形容詞！注意中間是 a，字尾是 -lent（prev-a-lent，名詞為 prevalence 普及程度），在某群體中普遍配介詞 among/in。
example: Myopia and poor posture have become increasingly prevalent among primary school children in Hong Kong.

def_zh: 無孔不入的；滲透各處的；普遍存在的（影響或風氣）
def_en: present or noticeable in every part of a thing or place
prep_trap: 注意開頭是 per-（per-va-sive）；常用於形容廣告、物質主義或科技對生活的廣泛滲透（the pervasive influence of social media）。
example: The pervasive influence of consumerism often misleads teenagers into equating luxury goods with happiness.

def_zh: 猖獗的；氾濫失控的（只用於犯罪、欺凌、假新聞或疾病等壞事）
def_en: of something bad: getting worse quickly and in an uncontrolled way
prep_trap: 絕對只可修飾負面事物（如 rampant cyberbullying / online scams / piracy），千萬不可用來形容正面風氣！
example: Stricter laws must be enacted to combat rampant telephone and online scams targeting retirees.

def_zh: 不可或缺的；絕對必要的
def_en: something or someone that is indispensable is so good or important that you could not manage without it, him, or her
prep_trap: 替換 very important 的頂級形容詞！注意中間是 -pen-sa-ble（是 a 而非 i）！必考搭配：play an indispensable role in / be indispensable to modern life。
example: Smartphones have become an indispensable part of modern urban life for communication and payment.

def_zh: 不可或缺的；作為整體一部分的（必配 to）
def_en: necessary and important as a part of a whole
prep_trap: 固定搭配：an integral part of（…不可或缺的一部分，如 Physical education is an integral part of holistic education）。
example: Moral and civic education is an integral part of the secondary school curriculum.

def_zh: 至關重要的；高於一切的；首要的
def_en: more important than anything else
prep_trap: DSE 議論文強調安全或健康高於一切的黃金句型：be of paramount importance（至關重要 = be extremely important）！
example: Ensuring passenger safety is always of paramount importance in the public transport system.

def_zh: 急切的；勢在必行的；極重要的
def_en: extremely important or urgent
prep_trap: 建議段及結論段呼籲行動的滿分句型：It is imperative for the government to... 或 It is imperative that we take immediate action。
example: It is imperative for the government to accelerate public housing construction for grassroots families.

def_zh: 迫切的；緊迫的；燃眉之急的（問題或需要）
def_en: urgent or needing to be dealt with immediately
prep_trap: 修飾社會問題或需求的高分定語（a pressing social issue / a pressing need for...）。
example: Waste management has become one of the most pressing environmental issues facing Hong Kong today.

def_zh: 迫在眉睫的；即將來臨的（常指危險、風暴或考試）
def_en: coming or likely to happen very soon
prep_trap: 注意雙寫 mm（im-mi-nent），切勿與意為「著名的」eminent（單 m，e 開頭）混淆！
example: With our landfills reaching full capacity soon, a serious waste crisis is imminent.

def_zh: 不可避免的；必然發生的
def_en: certain to happen and unable to be avoided or prevented
prep_trap: 副詞 inevitably（無可避免地）是 DSE 因果推論句的最佳增分修飾語（This will inevitably lead to...）。
example: An ageing population will inevitably place a heavy financial burden on the public healthcare system.

def_zh: 不可逆轉的；無法挽回的（生態破壞或身體損害）
def_en: not possible to change; impossible to return to a previous condition
prep_trap: 注意雙寫 rr，字尾是 -ible（ir-re-vers-i-ble）：環保與健康題必備（cause irreversible damage to marine ecosystems）。
example: Reclaiming natural wetlands for housing will cause irreversible damage to valuable wildlife habitats.

def_zh: 有害的；不利的（必配介詞 to）
def_en: causing harm or damage
prep_trap: 替換 bad for / harmful to 的第一高分形容詞！注意中間是 i（det-ri-men-tal），後面必須搭配介詞 to（be detrimental to physical and mental health / have a detrimental effect on）！
example: Chronic sleep deprivation is highly detrimental to teenagers' physical growth and emotional stability.

def_zh: 不利的；負面的；有害的（影響、反應或天氣）
def_en: having a negative or harmful effect on something
prep_trap: 替換 negative effects 的最佳定語！注意拼法為 ad-verse（切勿與意為「反感的」averse 混淆）：have an adverse effect/impact on。
example: Violent video games can have an adverse impact on young children's behaviour and values.

def_zh: 有益的；有利的（必配介詞 to）
def_en: helpful, useful, or good
prep_trap: 替換 good for 的標準正式詞：注意中間是 e 及 i（ben-e-fi-cial），後面必須配介詞 to（be beneficial to students' all-round development）。
example: Participating in team sports is highly beneficial to both physical fitness and interpersonal skills.

def_zh: 有助於…的；有利於促成…的（必配介詞 to）
def_en: providing the right conditions for something good to happen or exist
prep_trap: DSE 衝 5* 必備形容詞！專門形容「某種環境、氣氛或政策有利於某事的發展」，結構為 be conducive to + 名詞/V-ing（a quiet environment conducive to learning，to 是介詞）！
example: Playing soft background music in the library creates a relaxing atmosphere conducive to reading.

def_zh: 起重要作用/幫助的（必配介詞 in）；樂器的
def_en: important in helping to make something happen
prep_trap: 替換 play an important role in 的高分句型：be instrumental in V-ing（在促成某事上起關鍵作用，介詞必須用 in）！
example: Supportive teachers are instrumental in helping shy students build confidence and overcome challenges.

def_zh: 關鍵的；樞紐性的；中樞的
def_en: central and important
prep_trap: 替換 play an important role 的黃金搭配：play a pivotal role in（在…中扮演關鍵角色，注意拼法為 piv-ot-al）。
example: Parents play a pivotal role in shaping young children's eating habits and moral values.

def_zh: 至關重要的；決定性的
def_en: extremely important or necessary
prep_trap: 注意字尾是 -cial（cru-cial）；對某事至關重要介詞用 be crucial to/for。
example: Time management skills are crucial for senior students preparing for the public examinations.

def_zh: 極其重要的；維持生命所必需的
def_en: necessary for the success or continued existence of something; extremely important
prep_trap: 常用句型：It is vital for students to get enough sleep / be of vital importance。
example: Getting at least eight hours of quality sleep every night is vital for adolescent growth.

def_zh: 顯著的；重大的；別具意義的
def_en: important or noticeable
prep_trap: 注意字尾是 -cant（a），名詞為 significance（重要性）；在數據報告中形容顯著增減（a significant increase in）。
example: There has been a significant increase in the number of people using electronic payment systems.

def_zh: 大量的；可觀的；實質的（金額、數量或進展）
def_en: large in size, value, or importance
prep_trap: 替換 a lot of / big（修飾金額、數量或進步）的高分形容詞：a substantial amount of money / make substantial progress。
example: The government has invested a substantial amount of funding in promoting innovation and technology.

def_zh: 相當大的；相當多的（壓力、時間或開支）
def_en: large or of noticeable importance
prep_trap: 極易與 considerate（體貼別人的）混淆！considerable 解作「數量或程度相當大的」（under considerable pressure 承受相當大的壓力）！
example: Fresh graduates face considerable difficulty in finding a stable job during an economic recession.

def_zh: 體貼的；為他人著想的；有公德心的
def_en: kind and helpful; caring about other people's feelings and needs
prep_trap: 與 considerable（大量的）完全不同！considerate 專門形容「人為他人著想、有公德心」（be considerate towards other passengers）。
example: Public transport passengers should be considerate and offer their seats to people in need.

def_zh: 巨大的；極大的（壓力、努力或成就）
def_en: very great in amount or level, or extremely good
prep_trap: 注意首音節是 tre-，中間是 -men-dous；常搭配 pressure / effort / potential。
example: Putting tremendous academic pressure on young children may backfire and destroy their interest in learning.

def_zh: 極大的；無比的（壓力、滿足感或好處）
def_en: extremely large in size or degree
prep_trap: 注意雙寫 mm，字尾是 -se（im-mense）；常搭配抽象名詞如 immense pressure / an immense sense of satisfaction。
example: Helping underprivileged children improve their grades brings volunteer tutors an immense sense of satisfaction.

def_zh: 深遠的；深刻的（影響、改變或體會）
def_en: felt or experienced very strongly or in an extreme way
prep_trap: DSE 作文替換 deep / big impact 的滿分搭配：have a profound impact on（對…產生深遠影響）！
example: The invention of the Internet has had a profound impact on human communication and education.

def_zh: 影響深遠的；廣泛的（後果或影響）
def_en: something far-reaching has a great influence on many people or things
prep_trap: 必須加連字號（far-reaching）：專門用來修飾 consequences / implications / impact。
example: Global warming will have far-reaching consequences for food security and coastal cities worldwide.

def_zh: 微不足道的；可忽略不計的（影響、成效或成本）
def_en: too slight or small in amount to be of importance
prep_trap: significant 的反義詞（與 neglect 同源，字尾為 -ible）：駁論段用來指出某項表面措施成效微乎其微（The effect of the fifty-cent plastic bag levy has become negligible）。
example: A small fine of fifty dollars has a negligible deterrent effect on wealthy illegal parkers.

def_zh: 瑣碎的；微不足道的；雞毛蒜皮的（小事）
def_en: having little value or importance
prep_trap: 人際關係題常用詞：為雞毛蒜皮的小事爭吵用 quarrel over trivial matters。
example: Family members should learn to forgive each other instead of arguing over trivial household matters.

def_zh: 膚淺的；表面的；治標不治本的
def_en: never thinking about things that are serious or important, or only on the surface
prep_trap: 批評網絡交友、外貌主義或表面功夫的高分詞：superficial online friendships（流於表面的網友關係）。
example: Having thousands of followers on social media often brings only superficial friendships rather than genuine care.

def_zh: 從眾心理；順從；一致遵循（規範或潮流）
def_en: behaviour that follows the usual standards that are expected by a group or society
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（源自動詞 conform）：分析青少年為何盲目跟風的精準心理學詞彙（herd mentality and conformity 羊群與從眾心理）。
example: Blind conformity to internet trends can cause young people to lose their unique personal identity.

def_zh: 網絡欺凌
def_en: the activity of using the internet to harm or frighten another person, especially by sending them unpleasant messages
prep_trap: 絕對不可數名詞（一字連寫，切勿加 -s）！網絡欺凌的受害者為 victims of cyberbullying，欺凌者為 cyberbullies。
example: Schools should organize regular seminars to educate students on the devastating consequences of cyberbullying.

def_zh: 騷擾；困擾；欺凌侵擾
def_en: behaviour that annoys or upsets someone
prep_trap: 極高頻拼錯字！單寫 r、雙寫 ss（har-ass-ment），且為不可數名詞（online harassment 網上騷擾）。
example: Victims of online harassment should block the offenders immediately and report the case to teachers.

def_zh: 恐嚇；威嚇；脅迫
def_en: the action of frightening or threatening someone, usually in order to persuade them to do something that you want them to do
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（動詞為 intimidate 恐嚇，形容詞 intimidating 解作「令人畏懼/望而生畏的」）。
example: Every student has the right to study in a safe campus environment free from intimidation.

def_zh: 排擠；孤立；杯葛（某同學或成員）
def_en: to avoid speaking to or dealing with someone, often as a punishment or out of dislike
prep_trap: 校園關係性欺凌（杯葛排擠同學）的 5** 精準動詞！最常用被動結構：be ostracized by classmates（被同學排擠）。
example: Many teenagers conform to group behaviour simply out of fear of being ostracized by peers.

def_zh: 污名；負面標籤；羞恥感（尤指對精神病或求助的歧視標籤）
def_en: a strong feeling of disapproval that most people in a society have about something, especially when this is unfair
prep_trap: DSE 精神健康與弱勢題必背詞！消除對精神健康問題的污名化：remove the social stigma attached to mental illness（配 attached to 或 surrounding）。
example: Public education is needed to remove the social stigma attached to seeking psychological counselling.

def_zh: 刻板印象；定型觀念；對…存有偏見定型
def_en: a set idea that people have about what someone or something is like, especially an idea that is wrong
prep_trap: 注意中間是 -re-o-（ste-re-o-type）；打破性別或種族刻板印象用 break / shatter gender stereotypes。
example: Promoting female participation in engineering helps break traditional gender stereotypes in the STEM industry.

def_zh: 偏見；成見；歧視態度
def_en: an unfair and unreasonable opinion or feeling, especially when formed without enough thought or knowledge
prep_trap: 注意拼法為 prej-u-dice（由 pre- + judge 演變而來）；對某群體的偏見，後面介詞必須用 against（racial prejudice against ethnic minorities）！
example: Cultural exchange activities help eliminate deep-rooted prejudice against ethnic minorities in our community.

def_zh: 偏見；偏頗（傳媒報道或 AI 演算法偏差）
def_en: the action of supporting or opposing a particular person or thing in an unfair way, because of allowing personal opinions to influence your judgment
prep_trap: 形容詞為 biased（有偏見的/偏頗的，切勿漏寫 -ed：a biased news report）；對某事的偏見配 against 或 towards。
example: Students should read news from multiple sources to avoid being misled by media bias.

def_zh: 逃學；曠課
def_en: the problem or situation of children being absent from school regularly without permission
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，逃學的學生為 truant，逃學固定片語為 play truant（注意 truant 不加 a 亦不加 -s！）。
example: Social workers work closely with schools to help troubled students who frequently play truant.

def_zh: 拖延症；拖延習慣（不到最後一刻不做功課）
def_en: the act of delaying something that must be done, often because it is unpleasant or boring
prep_trap: DSE 學生時間管理與學習習慣題必背亮點詞！不可數名詞，動詞為 procrastinate（拖延）。
example: Breaking a large project into smaller daily tasks is an effective way to overcome procrastination.

def_zh: 身心俱疲；過勞倦怠（因長期學業或工作壓力耗盡精力）
def_en: extreme tiredness and a loss of enthusiasm and energy, usually caused by working too hard
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，一字連寫（burn-out）：學業倦怠為 academic burnout，職場過勞為 occupational burnout。
example: Taking regular breaks during revision periods is essential to prevent severe academic burnout.

def_zh: 失眠症；失眠
def_en: the condition of being unable to sleep, over a period of time
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意拼法為 in-som-ni-a；患上失眠搭配動詞 suffer from insomnia。
example: Using smartphones in bed right before sleeping is a major cause of insomnia among teenagers.

def_zh: 剝奪；缺乏（尤指睡眠不足 sleep deprivation 或貧困匱乏）
def_en: an absence or too little of something important
prep_trap: 動詞 deprive 去 e 加 -ation（dep-ri-va-tion）；DSE 最高頻黃金詞組：sleep deprivation（睡眠不足，替換 not enough sleep）！
example: Chronic sleep deprivation not only weakens the immune system but also impairs classroom concentration.

def_zh: 極度疲勞；疲乏；勞累
def_en: extreme tiredness
prep_trap: 替換 tiredness 的高分不可數名詞！注意字尾是 -tigue（讀 /tiːɡ/，ue 不發音）：mental and physical fatigue（身心疲勞）、eye fatigue（眼睛疲勞）。
example: Doing ten minutes of stretching exercises between study sessions helps relieve physical fatigue.

def_zh: 心理創傷；精神重創；外傷
def_en: severe emotional shock and pain caused by an extremely upsetting experience
prep_trap: 注意開頭是 trau-（au 發 /ɔː/ 音）；形容詞為 traumatic（造成心理創傷的 a traumatic experience）。
example: Severe campus bullying can leave victims with lifelong psychological trauma and low self-esteem.

def_zh: 極度痛苦；情緒困擾；悲傷憂慮
def_en: a feeling of extreme worry, sadness, or pain
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（emotional distress 情緒困擾）：處於痛苦或危難中用 in distress。
example: Teachers should be trained to identify early signs of emotional distress among their students.

def_zh: 心理輔導；諮詢服務
def_en: the job or process of listening to someone and giving that person advice about their problems
prep_trap: 絕對不可數名詞（切勿寫 counsellings 或 a counselling）！英式雙寫 ll（coun-sel-ling）；接受輔導用 receive / seek professional counselling。
example: Schools should provide confidential counselling services for students struggling with family or academic problems.

def_zh: 心態；心理狀態；思維習慣（如羊群心理）
def_en: a person's particular way of thinking about things
prep_trap: DSE 必背詞組：herd mentality（羊群心理/盲目跟風心態）！
example: Driven by herd mentality, many consumers queue for hours to buy limited-edition toys.

def_zh: 物質主義；拜金主義（過分追求名牌與物質享受）
def_en: the belief that having money and possessions is the most important thing in life
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 materialistic（崇尚物質的/拜金的 materialistic values）：香港消費文化與青少年價值觀題必考！
example: Social media influencers flaunting luxury handbags often fuel materialism among impressionable teenagers.

def_zh: 消費主義；過度消費風氣
def_en: the state of an advanced industrial society in which a lot of goods are bought and sold, often excessively
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，在環保（速食時裝、電子垃圾）與社會題中批判「鼓勵人不斷買新棄舊的消費主義」。
example: Online shopping festivals encourage excessive consumerism and generate massive amounts of packaging waste.

def_zh: 虛榮心；愛慕虛榮
def_en: the fact that you are too interested in your appearance or achievements
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（形容詞為 vain 徒勞的/愛慕虛榮的）：滿足某人的虛榮心固定搭配為 satisfy one's vanity。
example: Teenagers should not borrow money to buy luxury goods merely to satisfy their vanity.

def_zh: 自戀；自我中心傾向
def_en: too much interest in and admiration for your own physical appearance and/or your own abilities
prep_trap: 自拍文化（Selfie culture）與社交媒體題高分詞：注意 c 後是 i 再雙寫 ss（nar-cis-sism，形容詞為 narcissistic 自戀的）。
example: Posting edited selfies every day to seek online validation may breed unhealthy narcissism.

def_zh: 匿名性；不具名狀態（網絡世界的保護傘）
def_en: the situation in which someone's name is not given or known
prep_trap: DSE 解釋為何網絡欺凌與網上罪案猖獗的核心名詞！（源自形容詞 anonymous）：hide behind the veil of online anonymity（躲在網絡匿名的面紗後）。
example: Online anonymity emboldens cyberbullies to post malicious comments without fearing real-life consequences.

def_zh: 真實性；真確性（新聞資訊）；正宗原貌（文化古蹟）
def_en: the quality of being real or true
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（源自形容詞 authentic）：核實網上資訊的真偽用 verify the authenticity of online news。
example: Citizens should always verify the authenticity of shocking news before forwarding it on WhatsApp.

def_zh: 可信度；公信力（傳媒、機構或資料來源）
def_en: the fact that someone can be believed or trusted
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（形容詞為 credible 可信的，注意字尾是 -ible）：損害公信力用 undermine / damage the credibility of。
example: Spreading unverified rumours will severely damage the credibility of mainstream news organizations.

def_zh: 演算法（社交媒體或 AI 背後的推薦運算規則）
def_en: a set of mathematical instructions or rules that, especially if given to a computer, will help to calculate an answer to a problem
prep_trap: DSE 科技、AI 與短片沉迷題必考現代詞！注意拼法為 al-go-rithm（結尾是 -thm）。
example: Social media algorithms keep feeding users similar short videos, making it hard to stop watching.

def_zh: 回音；同溫層效應（固定配 echo chamber 回音室）；附和（動詞）
def_en: an environment in which a person only encounters information or opinions that reflect and reinforce their own
prep_trap: 科技與傳媒題 5** 概念詞組：an echo chamber（網絡同溫層/回音室，指演算法令人只看到與自己觀點相同的資訊，變得偏激）。
collocations: trap users in an echo chamber
example: Personalized news feeds can trap internet users in an echo chamber and narrow their perspectives.

def_zh: 監控；監視（如閉路電視或人臉識別監控）
def_en: the careful watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army, because of a crime that has happened or is expected
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，私隱與保安題必備！注意中間是 -veil-lance（雙 ll，字尾是 -ance）：surveillance cameras（閉路電視監控鏡頭）。
example: While installing surveillance cameras in classrooms deters misbehaviour, it may infringe on students' privacy.

def_zh: 洩漏；外洩（尤指個人資料外洩 data leakage 或滲水）
def_en: the act of leaking or the amount of liquid, gas, or secret information that leaks
prep_trap: 網購與科技題常考：personal data leakage（個人資料外洩）。
example: Online shoppers should use strong passwords to protect themselves against personal data leakage.

def_zh: 欺騙；詐騙；騙案（香港警方標準用語）
def_en: the act of hiding the truth, especially to get an advantage
prep_trap: 動詞為 deceive（c 後接 ei），變名詞時為 de-cep-tion；香港常見騙案標準英文：telephone deception（電話騙案）、online deception（網上騙案）。
example: The police have launched anti-scam commercials to warn citizens against sophisticated telephone deception.

def_zh: 欺詐罪；詐騙行為；騙子
def_en: the crime of getting money by deceiving people
prep_trap: 注意拼法為 f-r-a-u-d（au 發 /ɔː/ 音）：信用卡盜用或網上詐騙為 credit card fraud / online fraud。
example: Job seekers should beware of social media advertisements that are actually online employment fraud.

def_zh: 盜版行為；侵犯版權；海盜行為
def_en: the act of illegally copying a computer program, music, a film, etc. and selling it
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（盜版產品則是 pirated software/films）：online piracy（網上盜版行為）。
example: Rampant online piracy severely undermines the income and creativity of local musicians and filmmakers.

def_zh: 自動化（以機器或 AI 取代人手操作）
def_en: the use of machines and computers that can operate without needing human control
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（源自 automatic）：職場與科技題必考（workplace automation 職場自動化）。
example: While workplace automation boosts productivity, it may lead to unemployment among low-skilled workers.

def_zh: 人工的；人造的（如人工智能 AI 或人工食用色素）
def_en: made by people, often as a copy of something natural
prep_trap: 注意字尾是 -cial（ar-ti-fi-cial）：三大常考搭配 artificial intelligence (AI)（人工智能，不可數）、artificial island（人工島）、artificial additives（人工添加劑）。
example: Artificial intelligence can assist teachers in grading objective tests and preparing teaching materials.

def_zh: 虛擬的；網上的（相對於現實世界 real-world）
def_en: created by computer technology and appearing to exist but not existing in the physical world
prep_trap: 注意拼法為 vir-tu-al（與美德 virtue 同形異義）：virtual reality (VR)（虛擬實境）、the virtual world（虛擬世界）。
example: Virtual reality technology allows history students to explore ancient museums from their own classrooms.

def_zh: 沉浸式的；身臨其境的（體驗或學習環境）
def_en: seeming to surround the audience, player, etc. so that they feel completely involved in something
prep_trap: 由動詞 immerse 衍生（注意雙寫 mm：im-mer-sive）：形容 VR 科技、文化考察或英語營提供「身臨其境的學習體驗」（an immersive learning experience）。
example: Three-dimensional virtual tours provide an immersive learning experience that traditional textbooks cannot match.

def_zh: 創新的；新穎獨特的（意念、設計或教學法）
def_en: using new methods or ideas
prep_trap: 注意雙寫 nn（in-no-va-tive，名詞為 innovation 創新，不可數）：替換 new and creative 的高分詞。
example: We need innovative solutions to turn daily food waste into useful organic fertilizers.

def_zh: 最尖端的；最前沿的；最先進的（科技或研究）
def_en: very modern and with all the newest features
prep_trap: 必須加連字號（cutting-edge），且無需再用 more/most 比較級（本身已解作最尖端）！
example: The new science park is equipped with cutting-edge laboratories to attract biomedical researchers.

def_zh: 過時的；被淘汰的（因有新科技取代而不再使用）
def_en: not in use any more, having been replaced by something newer and better or more fashionable
prep_trap: 替換 old / out of date 的高分形容詞！注意拼法為 ob-so-lete：become obsolete（被時代淘汰）。
example: Workers must engage in lifelong learning so that their skills do not become obsolete.

def_zh: 被裁員的；多餘的；過剩的
def_en: having lost your job because your employer no longer needs you, or unnecessary because it is more than is needed
prep_trap: 英式職場常考固定搭配：be made redundant（因公司縮減人手或自動化而被裁員，名詞為 redundancy 裁員）。
example: Many bank tellers were made redundant after the bank introduced automated online banking services.

def_zh: 人際的；人與人之間交往的
def_en: connected with relationships between people
prep_trap: DSE 教育與青少年題必背高頻詞組：interpersonal skills（人際溝通技巧）、interpersonal relationships（人際關係），注意開頭是 inter-（人與人之間）。
example: Team sports and group projects help students develop strong interpersonal and communication skills.

def_zh: 親密的；密切的（友誼或家庭關係）；深入詳盡的（認識）
def_en: having, or being likely to cause, a very close friendship or personal relationship
prep_trap: 注意不要與意為「恐嚇」的 intimidate 混淆！intimate（無 d）形容真摯親密的關係（intimate friendship）或對某事的深入了解（an intimate knowledge of）。
example: Face-to-face conversations are essential for building intimate and lasting friendships with our peers.

def_zh: 和諧的；融洽的；和睦的
def_en: friendly and peaceful
prep_trap: DSE 社會與家庭題必備！（名詞為 harmony 和諧：live in harmony with 與…和諧共處）：build a harmonious society / family。
example: Mutual respect between different generations is the key to building a harmonious society.

def_zh: 共融的；包容各階層的；包含一切費用的（配 of）
def_en: including many different types of people and treating them all fairly and equally
prep_trap: 兩大考點：1. 社會與教育題解「傷健/種族共融的」（an inclusive society / inclusive education 融合教育）；2. Paper 3 費用題解「已包某費用」（$200 inclusive of lunch，配介詞 of）。
example: The government is committed to building a caring and inclusive society for disabled citizens.

def_zh: 人人平等的；主張平等主義的
def_en: believing that all people are equally important and should have the same rights and opportunities in life
prep_trap: 貧富懸殊與教育公平題衝 5* 詞彙（源自法文 equal）：an egalitarian society（機會均等的平等社會）。
example: Public libraries provide free access to books for everyone, reflecting an egalitarian spirit.

def_zh: 相互的；彼此的；共同的
def_en: feeling the same emotion, or doing the same thing to or for each other
prep_trap: 後接抽象單數名詞時，因本身已含「彼此」之意，切勿再畫蛇添足加 each other（如 mutual respect / mutual understanding / mutual trust）！
example: Cultural exchange programmes promote mutual understanding and friendship between local and overseas students.

def_zh: 互惠的；雙向回報的；相互的
def_en: involving two people or groups who agree to help each other or behave in the same way to each other
prep_trap: mutual 的進階同義詞：形容雙向互利的關係或安排（a reciprocal learning process 教學相長的互惠過程）。
example: Peer tutoring is a reciprocal process where both senior tutors and junior tutees benefit.

def_zh: 無私的；利他的；為他人著想的（義工精神）
def_en: showing a wish to help or bring advantages to others, even if it results in disadvantage for yourself
prep_trap: 義工服務與道德題衝 5** 詞彙（名詞為 altruism 利他主義）：替換 unselfish 的高雅形容詞。
example: Volunteering at animal shelters encourages teenagers to perform altruistic acts without expecting rewards.

def_zh: 慈善的；樂善好施的；博愛的
def_en: helping poor people, especially by giving them money
prep_trap: 注意中間是 ph 發 /f/ 音（名詞為 philanthropy 慈善事業，慈善家為 philanthropist）：替換 charitable 的高階詞。
example: Many university buildings in Hong Kong are named after generous local philanthropic donors.

def_zh: 仁慈的；樂善好施的；善心的
def_en: kind and helpful
prep_trap: 字首 bene- 代表「好」（與 beneficial 同源）：形容善心人士或慈善基金（benevolent donors）。
example: With the support of a benevolent foundation, fifty grassroots students joined the coding camp.

def_zh: 富有同情心的；仁愛慈悲的；體恤的
def_en: feeling or showing sympathy and sadness for the suffering or bad luck of others, and wanting to help them
prep_trap: 名詞為 compassion（同情心/惻隱之心，show compassion for the needy）：形容醫護人員、社工或關愛社會。
example: Nurses and social workers must be patient and compassionate when caring for elderly patients.

def_zh: 好客的；熱情款待客人的（旅遊業或接待家庭）
def_en: friendly and welcoming to guests and visitors
prep_trap: 名詞 hospitality 的形容詞形（hos-pi-ta-ble）：香港旅遊業推廣「好客之道」的核心詞（be hospitable to overseas tourists）。
example: Shopkeepers and taxi drivers should be polite and hospitable to build a tourist-friendly image.

def_zh: 有禮貌的；謙恭有禮的；客氣的
def_en: polite and showing respect
prep_trap: 替換 polite 的高分詞（名詞為 courtesy 禮貌/優惠：courtesy bus 免費接駁巴士）：注意開頭是 cour-te-ous。
example: Front-desk receptionists are trained to remain calm and courteous even when handling angry complaints.

def_zh: 熱誠的；誠摯友好的（尤用於邀請信）
def_en: friendly, but formal and polite
prep_trap: Paper 3 邀請信（Invitation Letter）必背滿分副詞：You are cordially invited to attend...（誠摯邀請閣下出席…）！
example: Parents and alumni are cordially invited to attend our annual speech day this Friday.

def_zh: 有建設性的；積極有益的（意見、批評或對話）
def_en: if advice, criticism, or actions are constructive, they are useful and intended to help or improve something
prep_trap: DSE 書信與議論文必備搭配：constructive feedback / suggestions / criticism（有建設性的意見/批評）。
example: Students should humbly accept constructive criticism from teachers in order to improve their writing.

def_zh: 富有成效的；高效率的；有收穫的（會議、學習或假期）
def_en: resulting in or providing a large amount or supply of something, or achieving a lot
prep_trap: 名詞為 productivity（生產力/學習效率）：put spare time to productive use（善用餘暇）。
example: Creating a daily study timetable helps students make productive use of their summer holidays.

def_zh: 成果豐碩的；收穫豐富的（旅程、討論或合作）
def_en: producing good results
prep_trap: Paper 3 演講稿或感謝信結尾祝福語必用：I wish you all a fruitful and enjoyable experience（祝願大家有個收穫豐碩的體驗）。
example: The five-day cultural exchange tour to Singapore was a truly fruitful experience for everyone.

def_zh: 值得做的；有意義且富滿足感的（經歷、義工或工作）
def_en: giving a lot of satisfaction, but possibly not much money
prep_trap: DSE 形容做義工、實習或教學工作「雖然辛苦但極具滿足感」的第一高頻形容詞：a rewarding experience！
example: Serving as a volunteer tutor for underprivileged children was an exhausting yet deeply rewarding experience.

def_zh: 令人充滿成就感的；充實美滿的（校園生活或人生）
def_en: making you feel happy and satisfied
prep_trap: 注意前單 l、中間雙寫 ll（ful-fill-ing）；常與 rewarding 並列使用（lead a fulfilling school life 過充實的校園生活）。
example: Balancing academic studies with extracurricular activities allows students to enjoy a fulfilling school life.

def_zh: 充實心靈的；增廣見聞的（體驗或活動）
def_en: improving the quality of something, especially by giving you new experiences and knowledge
prep_trap: 由動詞 enrich 加 -ing 構成之形容詞：專門修飾文化交流、閱讀或課外活動。
example: Living with a local host family in Australia was a culturally enriching experience for us.

def_zh: 大開眼界的；令人頓悟的
def_en: surprising, and teaching you new facts about life, people, etc.
prep_trap: 必須加連字號（eye-opening），且因以元音音素開頭，前面冠詞必須用 an（an eye-opening visit）；名詞則是 an eye-opener（大開眼界的事）。
example: Visiting the subdivided flats in Sham Shui Po was an eye-opening experience for our students.

def_zh: 發人深省的；引人深思的（電影、書籍、演講或問題）
def_en: making you think a lot about a subject
prep_trap: 必須加連字號（thought-provoking），書評、影評、演講感謝信必背萬用好評詞！
example: The principal delivered a thought-provoking speech on how young people should use technology responsibly.

def_zh: 鼓舞人心的；具啟發性的
def_en: encouraging, or making you feel you want to do something
prep_trap: 注意形容「人物故事或演講鼓舞人心」用 -ing（an inspiring story / role model），形容「自己受到啟發」則用 -ed（feel inspired by）。
example: The biography of Helen Keller is a truly inspiring book that teaches us perseverance.

def_zh: 有抱負的；有志成為…的（年輕人或初學者）
def_en: hoping and trying to be successful at a particular job or activity
prep_trap: 極易與 inspiring（鼓舞人心的）混淆！aspiring（a 開頭，源自 aspire 立志）永遠放在職業名詞前，指「有志成為…的年輕人」（aspiring young musicians / writers / entrepreneurs）！
example: The creative writing workshop provides a great platform for aspiring young writers to publish stories.

def_zh: 有雄心壯志的；有抱負的；宏大的（計劃）
def_en: having a strong wish to be successful, powerful, or rich, or needing a lot of effort to succeed
prep_trap: 名詞為 ambition（抱負/野心）：既可形容人有上進心，亦可形容政府計劃規模宏大（an ambitious target）。
example: The government has set an ambitious target of achieving carbon neutrality before the year 2050.

def_zh: 積極主動的；未雨綢繆的（在問題惡化前主動出擊，相對於被動 reactive）
def_en: taking action by causing change and not only reacting to change when it happens
prep_trap: DSE 建議段呼籲政府或學生採取主動的滿分詞：take a proactive approach to / take proactive measures（採取積極主動的措施）。
example: The government must take proactive measures to prevent hill fires during the dry autumn season.

def_zh: 務實的；講求實際成效的（非空談理想）
def_en: solving problems in a sensible way that suits the conditions that really exist now, rather than obeying fixed theories or ideals
prep_trap: 替換 practical 的高階詞：adopt a pragmatic approach to solving the housing shortage（採取務實方針解決房屋短缺）。
example: We need a pragmatic solution to balance historic preservation with the urgent need for housing.

def_zh: 嚴格的；嚴厲的；緊縮的（法規、安全標準或措施）
def_en: of a law, rule, or requirement: very strict and needing to be obeyed
prep_trap: 替換 strict laws / rules 的第一高分形容詞！注意只用來修飾「法例、標準、規管或檢查」（stringent regulations / safety checks），不可用來形容嚴厲的父母或老師！
example: The government should impose more stringent food safety checks on imported seafood products.

def_zh: 嚴謹的；嚴格的（訓練、測試或學術研究）
def_en: careful to look at or consider every part of something to make certain it is correct or safe; very strict and demanding
prep_trap: 注意中間是 -or-ous（無 u）：常修飾專業訓練、選拔或安全檢查（rigorous training / testing）。
example: All lifeguards must undergo rigorous physical training and pass a strict first-aid examination.

def_zh: 寬大的；過於寬鬆仁慈的（懲罰、判刑或管教）
def_en: not as severe or strong in punishment or judgment as would be expected
prep_trap: strict / stringent 的反義詞：批評現行罰則太輕毫無阻嚇力時必用（The current penalty for littering is too lenient）。
example: Critics argue that the current fines for illegal waste dumping are far too lenient.

def_zh: 阻嚇物；威懾力量（名詞）；具阻嚇性的（形容詞）
def_en: something that deters people from doing something illegal or harmful
prep_trap: DSE 法治與處罰題必背詞！注意雙寫 rr，字尾是 -ent（de-ter-rent）：1. 作名詞：act as a strong deterrent to offenders；2. 作形容詞：have a deterrent effect on。
example: Heavy fines and imprisonment serve as a strong deterrent against drunk driving.

def_zh: 懲罰性的（措施、稅項或罰則）
def_en: intended as a punishment
prep_trap: 與 punish 同源：常用於討論「單靠懲罰性措施（punitive measures）是否足夠，還是需配合教育」。
example: Relying solely on punitive measures without public education cannot solve the littering problem.

def_zh: 預防性的；防患於未然的（措施或醫療）
def_en: intended to stop something before it happens
prep_trap: 亦作 preventative，但寫 preventive 更簡潔不易拼錯：take preventive measures（採取預防措施）、preventive healthcare（基層預防醫療）。
example: Investing in preventive healthcare can significantly reduce the long-term burden on public hospitals.

def_zh: 補底的；輔導補救的（課堂或措施）
def_en: intended to help improve a situation or to help slow learners
prep_trap: 源自 remedy（補救方法）：香港學校常設的「課後補底班」即 remedial classes；事後補救措施為 remedial measures。
example: The school offers free after-school remedial classes for students who are weak in English.

def_zh: 適得其反的；弄巧反拙的（產生與原意相反的壞結果）
def_en: having an effect that is opposite to the one intended or wanted
prep_trap: DSE 駁論段與育兒題衝 5** 神字！一字連寫（counter + productive）：指「本想幫學生/解決問題，結果卻適得其反」（Assigning excessive homework is counterproductive）。
example: Forcing children to attend endless weekend tutorial classes is often counterproductive and causes burnout.

def_zh: 選修科目（名詞）；選修的（形容詞）
def_en: an optional course of study in a school or university
prep_trap: 香港 DSE 學制必考詞（4 個核心科目 core subjects + 2–3 個選修科目 elective subjects）：可以直接作可數名詞（take three electives）。
example: Secondary Three students should choose their DSE elective subjects based on their interests and strengths.

def_zh: 教學法；教育方法與理念
def_en: the method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject or theoretical concept
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，替換 teaching methods 的高分詞（student-centred pedagogy 以學生為本的教學法）。
example: Adopting a student-centred pedagogy encourages learners to ask questions and think independently.

def_zh: 反覆灌輸；諄諄教誨（良好習慣、品德或價值觀）
def_en: to fix beliefs or ideas in someone's mind, especially by repeating them often
prep_trap: instil 的進階替換詞：將正確價值觀灌輸給青少年，介詞搭配為 inculcate positive values in young people。
collocations: inculcate a sense of civic duty
example: Both families and schools share the responsibility to inculcate proper moral values in children.

def_zh: 陶冶（性情）；教化；啟迪心智
def_en: to improve someone's mind and character by teaching them something
prep_trap: 藝術、音樂與文學閱讀題的高雅詞彙（現在分詞 edifying 解作「陶冶性情的/有教化意義的」）。
example: Reading classic literature not only improves language skills but also edifies young people's minds.

def_zh: 扼殺；壓抑；窒礙（創意、想像力或獨立思考）
def_en: to prevent something from happening, being expressed, or continuing
prep_trap: DSE 批評死記硬背或過嚴管教的 5** 黃金搭配：stifle students' creativity and imagination（扼殺學生的創意與想像力，注意單寫 f）！
example: Overemphasizing standardized test scores will inevitably stifle students' creativity and curiosity.

def_zh: 記憶力；知識留存度；保留（人才）
def_en: the ability to keep or continue having something, especially information in your memory
prep_trap: 動詞 retain 的名詞形（不可數）：學習方法題常用 knowledge retention（知識記憶留存）。
example: Using colourful mind maps and flashcards can significantly improve long-term memory retention.

def_zh: 認知的；思維能力的（如記憶、推理與理解）
def_en: connected with thinking or conscious mental processes
prep_trap: 教育與兒童發展題必備學術形容詞：cognitive development（認知發展）、cognitive skills（認知能力）。
example: Learning to play a musical instrument in childhood enhances brain function and cognitive development.

def_zh: 分析的；善於邏輯分析的
def_en: examining or liking to examine things in detail, in order to discover more about them
prep_trap: 注意中間有 y（an-a-lyt-i-cal，源自 analyse）：常與 critical thinking 並列（analytical and problem-solving skills）。
example: Conducting scientific experiments trains students to develop an analytical mind and logical reasoning.

def_zh: 求知慾；好問精神
def_en: the quality of wanting to discover as much as you can about things
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，替換 curiosity 的高階詞。
example: Interactive museum exhibits encourage children's natural inquisitiveness about science and space exploration.

def_zh: 天資；天賦才能；性向（常配介詞 for）
def_en: a natural ability or skill
prep_trap: 極易與 attitude（態度，雙寫 tt）混淆！ap-ti-tude（中間是 pt）解作「在某方面的天賦才華」，後面介詞配 for（show a natural aptitude for languages）。
example: Career aptitude tests help senior students identify their strengths and choose suitable university majors.

def_zh: 傾向；意願；個人喜好興趣
def_en: a feeling that you want to do a particular thing, or the fact that you prefer or are more likely to do a particular thing
prep_trap: 形容詞 inclined 極好用：be academically inclined（有學術傾向/讀書材料的學生）vs less academically inclined（非傳統學術型學生）。
example: Schools should offer diverse sports and arts programmes for students who are less academically inclined.

def_zh: 抱負；志向；理想（常作複數 aspirations）
def_en: something that you hope to achieve
prep_trap: 替換 dreams / goals 的滿分名詞！注意開頭是 as-pi-（切勿與意為「靈感」的 inspiration 混淆）：career aspirations（職業志向）。
example: Parents should respect their children's personal career aspirations instead of forcing them to study medicine.

def_zh: 使命感強的職業（如教師、醫護或社工）；天職
def_en: a type of work that you feel you are suited to doing and to which you should give all your time and energy
prep_trap: 注意開頭是 vo-（切勿拼成意為「假期」的 vacation）！專門指需要愛心與使命感的專業。
example: Teaching is not merely a stable job, but a noble vocation that shapes young lives.

def_zh: 前途；發展前景；就業展望（永遠用複數）
def_en: the possibility of being successful, especially at work
prep_trap: DSE 生涯規劃題必考單複數陷阱！指「就業前景/前途」時，永遠必須加 -s 用複數（career prospects / job prospects）！
example: Graduates with strong bilingual skills and digital literacy enjoy much brighter career prospects.

def_zh: 流動性（尤指社會向上流動 upward social mobility）；行動能力
def_en: the ability to move freely or be easily moved, or the ability to move between different levels in society
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 青年出路與貧富懸殊題必背核心概念：upward social mobility（社會向上流動）！
example: Higher education has traditionally been seen as the main ladder for upward social mobility.

def_zh: 創業精神；創業活動
def_en: skill in starting new businesses, especially when this involves seeing new opportunities
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（由 entrepreneur + -ship 構成）：promote youth entrepreneurship（推動青年創業）。
example: The government has set up a startup fund to encourage youth entrepreneurship and innovation.

def_zh: 同儕友愛；手足情誼；大學兄弟會或學會群體
def_en: a feeling of friendship and support, or a group of people who have the same job or interest
prep_trap: 可指同輩間互助互愛的友愛精神（foster a spirit of fraternity）。
example: Living together in university halls fosters a strong spirit of fraternity and mutual support.

def_zh: 人生導師；良師益友；指導（後輩）
def_en: a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school
prep_trap: 注意字尾是 -tor（men-tor）；被指導的學員/後輩則稱為 mentee（雙寫 ee）。
example: Experienced alumni are invited to act as mentors and share workplace insights with senior students.

def_zh: 角色；作用；榜樣（role model）
def_en: the position or purpose that someone or something has in a situation, organization, society, or relationship
prep_trap: 兩大必考固定搭配：1. play a vital/pivotal role in V-ing（在…扮演重要角色，介詞必用 in）；2. set a good example and act as a positive role model for children（成為孩子的良好榜樣，介詞配 for）。
collocations: serve as a role model for
example: Parents must put down their smartphones at dinner to serve as good role models for children.

def_zh: 家庭教育；養育方式；成長教養環境
def_en: the way in which you are treated and educated when young, especially by your parents, especially in relation to the effect that this has on how you behave and make moral decisions
prep_trap: 由短語動詞 bring up（撫養長大）倒轉構成之單數名詞（一字連寫 up-bring-ing）：family upbringing（家庭教養）。
example: A child's moral character is heavily influenced by their early family upbringing and parental guidance.

def_zh: 育兒方式；家長管教之道
def_en: the raising of children and all the responsibilities and activities that are involved in it
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，香港家庭議題必考詞組：helicopter parenting（怪獸家長/直升機式過度保護管教）、authoritarian parenting（專制式管教）。
example: Overprotective helicopter parenting deprives children of the chance to learn from their own mistakes.

def_zh: 過度保護的（家長）
def_en: wishing to protect someone, especially a child, too much
prep_trap: 一字連寫，專門用來形容「事事代勞、不讓子女承受半點挫折的怪獸家長」（overprotective parents）。
example: Children raised by overprotective parents often lack basic self-care skills and emotional resilience.

def_zh: 放任的；過度縱容的（管教方式）
def_en: allowing behaviour that many other people would disapprove of
prep_trap: 與 strict 相反：permissive parents 指「對子女毫無規矩底線、百般遷就縱容的家長」。
example: An overly permissive parenting style may cause children to become self-centred and disrespectful of rules.

def_zh: 縱容；溺愛；嬌生慣養（孩子）
def_en: to give someone special treatment, making that person as comfortable as possible and giving them whatever they want
prep_trap: 替換 spoil children 的高分動詞：過去分詞 pampered 常作形容詞（pampered children 嬌生慣養的港孩）。
example: Pampered children who have everything done for them by domestic helpers struggle with independence.

def_zh: 世代；一代人；代溝（generation gap）；發電（不可數）
def_en: all the people of about the same age within a society or within a particular family
prep_trap: 三大必背搭配：1. the generation gap（代溝）；2. the younger/older generation（年輕/年長一代）；3. future generations（下一代/後代，常用複數）。
example: We have a moral duty to protect the environment for the sake of future generations.

def_zh: （與家人或伴侶）關係疏遠的；失和的
def_en: no longer friendly or in contact with family members
prep_trap: 内含 strange（陌生）：形容原本親密的家人因缺乏溝通或爭執而變得形同陌路（become estranged from their parents）。
example: Long working hours and lack of communication can cause teenagers to become estranged from parents.

def_zh: （家庭、室友或社會群體間的）摩擦；不和；矛盾
def_en: disagreement or unfriendliness caused by people having different opinions
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，替換 conflict / argument 的高雅詞彙：cause friction between parents and children（引起親子間的摩擦）。
example: Disagreements over smartphone usage and academic grades often cause daily friction between parents and teenagers.

def_zh: 不和；紛爭；失和（harmony 的反義詞）
def_en: the state of not agreeing or sharing opinions
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（千萬別只想到聊天軟件 Discord！）：在家庭與社會題中，marital/family discord 解作「家庭失和」。
example: Financial stress and cramped living conditions in subdivided flats often lead to family discord.

def_zh: 和解；修好；重歸於好
def_en: a situation in which two people or groups of people become friendly again after they have argued
prep_trap: 動詞 reconcile 的名詞形（注意中間是 -cil-i-a-tion）：記敘文或家庭題描寫爭吵後冰釋前嫌的高分詞。
example: A sincere apology is always the first step towards forgiveness and reconciliation after a quarrel.

def_zh: 陪伴；友誼；伴侶關係（尤指對獨居長者或孩童的陪伴）
def_en: the enjoyment of spending time with other people
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（源自 companion 同伴）：飼養寵物、探訪長者或親子關係題必備（provide warm companionship for lonely seniors）。
example: Keeping a pet dog can provide warm companionship and emotional comfort for elderly people living alone.

def_zh: 獨處；寧靜的獨居時光（多含正面平靜意味，有別於痛苦的 loneliness）
def_en: the situation of being alone without other people, often by choice and enjoyed peacefully
prep_trap: 不可數名詞：loneliness 是負面的「孤單寂寞」，而 solitude 則是享受遠離繁囂的「寧靜獨處」（enjoy moments of peaceful solitude）。
example: Hiking alone in country parks allows busy city dwellers to enjoy moments of peaceful solitude.

def_zh: 紐帶；緊密關係；親情/友情連繫（名詞）；建立親密關係（動詞，配 with）
def_en: a close connection joining two or more people
prep_trap: 替換 relationship 的首選高分詞！作名詞：strengthen family bonds（加強家庭紐帶）；作動詞：bond with children（與子女建立親密感情，配介詞 with）。
example: Cooking meals together at weekends is a wonderful way for parents to bond with children.

def_zh: 關係；連繫；紐帶（作此義時通常用複數 ties）
def_en: friendly relations or connections between people, groups, or countries
prep_trap: 指人際、家庭或地區間的「連繫/關係」時，幾乎永遠以複數形式 ties 出現（family ties / community ties / strengthen ties between Hong Kong and the Mainland）！
example: High-speed rail networks have greatly strengthened economic and cultural ties between cities in the region.

def_zh: 感激之情；感恩；謝意
def_en: the feeling or quality of being grateful
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（與形容詞 grateful 同源，注意開頭是 grat-i-tude）：向某人表達誠摯謝意固定搭配為 express our heartfelt gratitude to sb（介詞配 to）。
example: On Graduation Day, students presented flowers to express their heartfelt gratitude to their dedicated teachers.

def_zh: 誠信；正直；廉潔（個人品格或學術誠信）
def_en: the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles that you refuse to change
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 品德、AI 抄襲及香港核心價值題必背詞！academic integrity（學術誠信）、personal integrity（個人操守）。
example: Schools must educate students on the importance of upholding academic integrity when using AI tools.

def_zh: 道德規範；倫理準則（常作複數）；工作態度（單數 work ethic）
def_en: a system of accepted beliefs that control behaviour, especially such a system based on morals
prep_trap: 注意單複數分別：1. 指科技、醫療或專業倫理時用複數 ethics（professional ethics / AI ethics，形容詞為 ethical 合乎道德的）；2. 指「勤奮敬業的工作態度」時則用單數 a strong work ethic！
example: The rapid advancement of human cloning and artificial intelligence has raised serious ethical concerns.

def_zh: 公民的；市民的；有公德心的（civic-minded）
def_en: of a town or city or the people who live in it
prep_trap: DSE 社會公德與教育題必背三大搭配：civic education（公民教育）、civic awareness/responsibility（公民意識/責任）、civic-minded citizens（有公德心的市民）。
example: Civic education teaches young people to become responsible and civic-minded citizens who care for society.

def_zh: 禮貌；謙恭；文明舉止
def_en: polite behaviour, or a polite action or remark
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（注意開頭是 cour-te-sy）：展示基本禮貌用 show basic courtesy to others。
example: Saying thank you to bus drivers and cleaners is a sign of basic courtesy.

def_zh: 禮儀；社交規矩（如餐桌禮儀或網絡禮儀）
def_en: the set of rules or customs that control accepted behaviour in particular social groups or social situations
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，法文借詞，字尾是 -quette（讀 /ket/）：table etiquette（餐桌禮儀）、online etiquette / netiquette（網絡禮儀）。
example: Students should observe proper online etiquette and remain respectful during virtual classroom discussions.

def_zh: 營養；營養攝取
def_en: the process of providing or obtaining the food necessary for health and growth
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s；形容詞為 nutritious（有營養的，修飾食物）或 nutritional（營養學上的，如 nutritional value）。
example: Teaching primary students to read nutrition labels helps them avoid snacks packed with hidden sugar.

def_zh: 營養豐富的；有營養的（食物）
def_en: efficient as food; nourishing
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意拼字字尾是 -tious，專門修飾 meals / food / diet。
example: Eating a nutritious breakfast every morning gives students the energy needed to concentrate in class.

def_zh: 營養素；養分
def_en: a substance that provides nourishment essential for growth and the maintenance of life
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常用複數形式 essential nutrients（必需營養素）。
example: Freshly steamed vegetables retain far more essential nutrients than heavily processed fast-food meals.

def_zh: 營養不良
