def_en: lack of proper nutrition, caused by not having enough to eat, not eating enough of the right things
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 suffer from malnutrition。
example: Even in wealthy cities, elderly citizens living alone may suffer from malnutrition due to poor diets.

def_zh: 滋養；提供營養；培育（心靈或希望）
def_en: provide with the food or other substances necessary for growth, health, and good condition
prep_trap: 及物動詞，分詞形容詞為 nourishing（滋補有營養的，如 nourishing soup）。
example: Reading classic literature nourishes young minds and helps students develop deep empathy for others.

def_zh: 卡路里（熱量單位）
def_en: a unit of energy, often used as a measurement of the amount of energy that food provides
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 burn calories（消耗卡路里）或 calorie intake（熱量攝取）。
example: Sugary bubble tea contains hundreds of empty calories that contribute to childhood weight gain.

def_zh: 碳水化合物；澱粉質食物
def_en: any of a large group of organic compounds occurring in foods and living tissues, including sugars and starch
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，常用複數形式 carbohydrates（簡稱 carbs）。
example: Replacing refined carbohydrates like white bread with whole grains keeps blood sugar levels stable.

def_zh: 蛋白質
def_en: any of a class of nitrogenous organic compounds that are essential constituents of living cells
prep_trap: 不可數或可數名詞，注意拼字是 ei（protein），配 rich in protein。
example: Tofu, beans, and nuts are affordable sources of plant protein for students following a meatless diet.

def_zh: 鈣質
def_en: a chemical element and mineral that is essential for strong bones and teeth
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 calcium deficiency（缺鈣）。
example: Adequate calcium intake and outdoor sunlight exposure help prevent brittle bones among elderly women.

def_zh: 膳食纖維；纖維素
def_en: dietary material containing substances such as cellulose, which are resistant to the action of digestive enzymes
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（美式拼作 fiber），常配 dietary fibre（膳食纖維）。
example: Eating whole fruits instead of drinking fruit juice provides essential dietary fibre for healthy digestion.

def_zh: 咖啡因
def_en: a crystalline compound that is found especially in tea and coffee plants and is a stimulant of the central nervous system
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意拼字是 ei（caffeine）及雙 f。
example: Relying on energy drinks loaded with caffeine to stay awake before exams can trigger heart palpitations.

def_zh: 補充品；保健品（亦可作動詞：補充）
def_en: something that completes or enhances something else when added to it, especially a dietary pill
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 dietary / vitamin supplements（營養補充劑）。
example: Health experts emphasize that vitamin supplements cannot replace a balanced diet of fresh food.

def_zh: 食慾；胃口；對某事物的強烈慾望
def_en: a natural desire to satisfy a bodily need, especially for food
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，作「對某事物的渴求」時配介詞 for（an appetite for reading）。
example: Snacking on potato chips right before dinner will spoil children's appetite for healthy vegetables.

def_zh: 強烈渴望；嘴饞（尤指對甜食或垃圾食物）
def_en: a powerful desire for something
prep_trap: 可數名詞，源自動詞 crave，必配介詞 for（a craving for sugary snacks）。
example: Lack of sleep disrupts hormones and increases teenagers' cravings for sugary drinks and fried snacks.

def_zh: 暴飲暴食；貪食
def_en: habitual greed or excess in eating
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，討論自助餐（all-you-can-eat buffets）造成廚餘浪費時的高分字。
example: All-you-can-eat buffets often encourage gluttony and generate huge amounts of unnecessary food waste.

def_zh: 禁食；斷食
def_en: abstaining from all or some kinds of food or drink
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，近年流行 intermittent fasting（間歇性斷食減肥法）。
example: Teenagers should exercise regularly rather than resorting to extreme fasting to lose weight quickly.

def_zh: 厭食症
def_en: an emotional disorder characterized by an obsessive desire to lose weight by refusing to eat
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 討論社交媒體「瘦即是美」審美標準（unrealistic beauty standards）危害青少年時的必考字。
example: Unrealistic beauty standards on social media can drive insecure teenagers toward eating disorders like anorexia.

def_zh: 暴食症（暴食後催吐的飲食失調症）
def_en: an emotional disorder involving distortion of body image and bouts of extreme overeating followed by self-induced vomiting
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常與 anorexia 並稱為常見飲食失調症（eating disorders）。
example: School social workers should stay alert to early signs of eating disorders such as anorexia and bulimia.

def_zh: 癡肥的；過度肥胖的
def_en: grossly fat or overweight in a way that threatens health
prep_trap: 形容詞（注意切勿與名詞 obesity 混用：He is obese / He suffers from obesity）。
example: The proportion of overweight and obese primary students rose sharply during the months of online classes.

def_zh: 肥胖症；癡肥問題
def_en: the condition of being grossly fat or overweight
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 健康議題核心詞彙：childhood obesity（兒童肥胖問題）。
example: Imposing a sugar tax on soft drinks is one policy option to combat rising childhood obesity.

def_zh: 久坐不動的；缺乏運動的（生活或工作模式）
def_en: tending to spend much time seated; somewhat inactive
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 健康與都市生活題必背奪星詞組：lead a sedentary lifestyle（過著久坐少動的生活）！
example: Leading a sedentary lifestyle in front of computer screens increases the risk of heart disease and back pain.

def_zh: 新陳代謝
def_en: the chemical processes that occur within a living organism in order to maintain life
prep_trap: 不可數或單數名詞，常配 boost / speed up metabolism（促進新陳代謝）。
example: Regular aerobic exercise and strength training help boost our body's metabolism and burn excess fat.

def_zh: 心血管的（心臟及血管）
def_en: relating to the heart and blood vessels
prep_trap: 形容詞，體育課與健康飲食題必背：cardiovascular diseases（心血管疾病）或 cardiovascular fitness（心肺功能）。
example: Thirty minutes of brisk walking every day significantly reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases.

def_zh: 呼吸系統的；呼吸道的
def_en: relating to or affecting respiration or the organs of respiration
prep_trap: 形容詞，空氣污染與吸煙議題必考：respiratory illnesses / infections（呼吸道疾病）。
example: Roadside air pollutants irritate the lungs and trigger respiratory illnesses among young children and the elderly.

def_zh: 糖尿病
def_en: a disease in which the body's ability to produce or respond to the hormone insulin is impaired
prep_trap: 雖以 s 結尾但屬不可數單數名詞（Diabetes is...）；糖尿病患者為 diabetic。
example: Cutting down on sugary beverages is a simple yet effective way to prevent type 2 diabetes.

def_zh: 高血壓
def_en: abnormally high blood pressure
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，即 high blood pressure 的醫學正式寫法，字首 hyper- 表示「過高」。
example: Chronic work stress and a high-sodium diet are major risk factors for hypertension among middle-aged adults.

def_zh: 哮喘
def_en: a respiratory condition marked by spasms in the bronchi of the lungs, causing difficulty in breathing
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意中間 th 不發音（讀 /ˈæsmə/），常配 trigger an asthma attack（引發哮喘發作）。
example: Worsening smog and roadside emissions can easily trigger acute asthma attacks in sensitive children.

def_zh: 敏感；過敏症（如食物或鼻敏感）
def_en: a damaging immune response by the body to a substance, especially pollen, fur, or a particular food
prep_trap: 可數名詞，必配介詞 to（a peanut allergy / allergic to nuts 對堅果敏感）。
example: School registration forms ask parents to declare whether their children have any severe food allergies.

def_zh: 近視；（比喻）目光短淺
def_en: nearsightedness, or lack of imagination, foresight, or intellectual insight
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，即 short-sightedness 的正式用字；形容詞 myopic 亦常批評政策「短視近利」（a myopic policy）。
example: Staring at tablet screens in dim lighting has caused childhood myopia rates in Hong Kong to skyrocket.

def_zh: 坐姿；站姿；體態；（政府的）立場態度
def_en: the position in which someone holds their body when standing or sitting
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，討論「低頭族」玩手機引致頸椎痛時必提 poor sitting posture。
example: Hunching over smartphones for hours leads to poor posture and chronic neck pain among teenagers.

def_zh: 符合人體工學的（減少疲勞與勞損的設計）
def_en: relating to or designed for efficiency and comfort in the working environment
prep_trap: 形容詞，Paper 2/3 提議改善學校圖書館或辦公室設備時的亮眼專業字：ergonomic chairs and desks。
example: Replacing old wooden stools in the computer room with ergonomic chairs will protect students' spines.

def_zh: 體格；體型
def_en: the form, size, and development of a person's body
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，注意字尾是 -sique（讀 /ziːk/），討論青少年健身熱潮（gym culture）時常用。
example: Some teenage boys take dangerous steroid supplements in an unhealthy obsession with building a muscular physique.

def_zh: 耐力；體力；持久力
def_en: the ability to sustain prolonged physical or mental effort
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，不加 s，推廣長跑或體育課時必背：build physical and mental stamina。
example: Long-distance running not only builds physical stamina but also trains students' willpower to overcome hardship.

def_zh: 忍耐力；耐力（尤指極限運動或長期逆境）
def_en: the fact or power of enduring an unpleasant or difficult process or situation without giving way
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自動詞 endure（忍受），常配 endurance sports（耐力運動，如馬拉松）。
example: Completing the Oxfam Trailwalker hike is a gruelling test of both physical endurance and team spirit.

def_zh: 敏捷度；靈活度（身體或思維）
def_en: ability to move quickly and easily, or ability to think and understand quickly
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 agile（身手敏捷的 / 靈活應變的）。
example: Playing badminton and table tennis improves students' hand-eye coordination, reflexes, and physical agility.

def_zh: 靈巧（尤指雙手操作技巧或思維敏銳）
def_en: skill in performing tasks, especially with the hands
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 manual dexterity（手部靈巧度，如學習樂器、書法或手工藝）。
example: Learning Chinese calligraphy or origami helps young children develop fine motor skills and manual dexterity.

def_zh: 劇烈的（運動）；精力充沛的；強而有力的
def_en: strong, healthy, and full of energy; characterized by or involving physical strength or effort
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意中間沒有 u（名詞則可拼作 vigour / vigor），世衛運動建議常配 vigorous aerobic exercise。
example: World Health Organization guidelines recommend that teenagers engage in at least sixty minutes of vigorous exercise daily.

def_zh: 費力的；繁重劇烈的（運動或努力）
def_en: requiring or using great exertion
prep_trap: 形容詞，Paper 3 遠足或運動通告常考：Avoid strenuous exercise if you feel unwell（如感不適切勿進行劇烈運動）。
example: Hikers with heart conditions should avoid strenuous mountain trails during hot and humid summer days.

def_zh: 輕快敏捷的（步速）；清涼颯爽的；（生意）興旺的
def_en: active, fast, and energetic
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 建議長者或忙碌上班族運動時最實用的詞組：a brisk walk（急步行）。
example: Getting off the bus one stop earlier for a fifteen-minute brisk walk is an easy daily habit.

def_zh: 安多酚；內啡肽（運動時大腦分泌的快樂荷爾蒙）
def_en: chemicals produced naturally by the nervous system to cope with pain or stress, often called 'feel-good' hormones
prep_trap: 常用複數形式 endorphins，DSE 論證「運動為何能減壓抗抑鬱」的必殺科學詞彙：release endorphins！
example: Aerobic exercise stimulates the brain to release endorphins, which act as natural mood lifters for stressed students.

def_zh: 多巴胺（與獎賞、成癮及短片沉迷相關的神經傳導物質）
def_en: a compound present in the body as a neurotransmitter, associated with pleasure, reward, and addiction
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 討論為何青少年沉迷手機短片（short videos）或社交媒體「呃 Like」的 5** 科學解釋字！
example: Endless scrolling on short-video platforms provides instant dopamine hits that shorten teenagers' attention spans.

def_zh: 皮質醇（壓力荷爾蒙）
def_en: a steroid hormone released by the adrenal cortex in response to stress
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，與 endorphins 相反，用來科學化解釋長期學業或工作壓力的生理傷害（elevated cortisol levels）。
example: Spending time in green parks helps lower levels of cortisol, the body's primary stress hormone.

def_zh: 腎上腺素（緊張刺激時分泌的荷爾蒙）
def_en: a hormone secreted by the adrenal glands, especially in conditions of stress, increasing rates of blood circulation and breathing
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，描寫比賽或極限運動（extreme sports）緊張刺激感時必配 an adrenaline rush。
example: Stepping onto the stage for the debate finals gave me a sudden surge of adrenaline.

def_zh: 褪黑激素（調節睡眠生理時鐘的荷爾蒙）
def_en: a hormone secreted by the pineal gland which inhibits melanin formation and regulates sleep-wake cycles
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 解釋「為何睡前玩手機藍光（blue light）會導致失眠」的滿分科學詞彙！
example: Blue light emitted by smartphone screens suppresses melatonin production and makes it harder to fall asleep.

def_zh: 晝夜節律的；生理時鐘的
def_en: relating to or exhibiting approximately 24-hour biological cycles
prep_trap: 形容詞，必配 circadian rhythm（生理時鐘 / 晝夜節律），熬夜溫習（burning the midnight oil）題必用。
example: Staying up late during holidays disrupts students' natural circadian rhythm and causes severe daytime fatigue.

def_zh: 睡眠不足的；長期缺眠的
def_en: suffering from a lack of sleep
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，名詞片語為 sleep deprivation（睡眠剝奪/長期不夠瞓）。
example: Chronically sleep-deprived adolescents struggle with memory retention, mood swings, and weakened immunity.

def_zh: 睡過頭；瞓過龍
def_en: sleep longer or later than one intended
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，過去式為 overslept。
example: Students who play online games past midnight often oversleep the next morning and arrive late for school.

def_zh: 小睡；午睡（亦可作動詞）
def_en: a short sleep, especially during the day
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 take a power nap（小睡 15-20 分鐘充電）。
example: Taking a twenty-minute power nap after lunch can restore alertness and improve afternoon study efficiency.

def_zh: 午睡；午休時間
def_en: an afternoon rest or nap, especially one taken during the hottest hours of the day
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: Some progressive technology companies provide quiet pods for employees to take a brief post-lunch siesta.

def_zh: 康復；休養恢復（病後或手術後）
def_en: recover from illness or physical exertion
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，常配介詞 from（recuperate from surgery / illness），名詞為 recuperation。
example: Employees should be allowed to rest and recuperate fully at home instead of working while sick.

def_zh: 病後療養；漸漸康復
def_en: recover one's health and strength over a period of time after an illness or operation
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，名詞為 convalescence（療養期，如香港的療養院 convalescent hospital）。
example: Stable patients are transferred from acute wards to convalescent hospitals to free up emergency beds.

def_zh: 寬慰；紓緩；救濟物資（如賑災或扶貧）
def_en: a feeling of reassurance and relaxation following release from anxiety, or financial/practical assistance given to those in need
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿與動詞 relieve 混淆！常配 stress relief（減壓）、disaster relief（賑災）或 poverty relief（扶貧）。
example: One-off tax rebates provide temporary financial relief to middle-class families struggling with inflation.

def_zh: 安慰；撫慰（傷痛或孤單的人）
def_en: give comfort or consolation to someone in distress
prep_trap: 及物動詞。
example: Therapy dogs visit elderly care homes every weekend to solace lonely seniors and bring them joy.

def_zh: 鎮靜劑；安眠藥
def_en: a medicinal drug taken to reduce tension or anxiety
prep_trap: 可數名詞（美式單寫 l：tranquilizer），野生動物救援亦常指麻醉槍（tranquillizer dart）。
example: Wildlife officers used a tranquillizer dart to safely capture the wild boar that wandered into the MTR station.

def_zh: 抗抑鬱藥
def_en: a drug used to alleviate clinical depression
prep_trap: 可數名詞，字尾是 -ant。
example: Regular outdoor exercise acts as a powerful natural antidepressant without any chemical side effects.

def_zh: 精神科醫生（具處方藥物資格的專科醫生）
def_en: a medical practitioner specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of mental illness
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意字頭 p 不發音；精神病學或精神科為 psychiatry。
example: Shortages of child psychiatrists in public hospitals have resulted in long waiting times for diagnostic assessments.

def_zh: 心理學家（如教育心理學家或臨床心理學家）
def_en: an expert or specialist in psychology
prep_trap: 可數名詞，學校常駐的是 educational psychologist（教育心理學家）。
example: Educational psychologists work closely with teachers to design tailored learning plans for students with dyslexia.

def_zh: 讀寫障礙
def_en: a general term for disorders that involve difficulty in learning to read or interpret words, letters, and other symbols
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 討論融合教育（inclusive education）及 SEN 學童（students with Special Educational Needs）必考字！
example: Audio textbooks and speech-to-text software help students with dyslexia overcome reading barriers in class.

def_zh: 自閉症
def_en: a neurodevelopmental condition of variable severity with lifelong effects that can be recognized from early childhood
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 autistic（患自閉症的，更尊重的寫法是 children with autism）。
example: Early intervention and social skills training help children with autism adapt to mainstream primary schools.

def_zh: 過度活躍症（常配專注力不足 ADHD）
def_en: the condition of being abnormally or extremely active
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 hyperactive。
example: Breaking long lessons into interactive ten-minute tasks helps students with hyperactivity stay engaged.

def_zh: 認知障礙症（舊稱腦退化症或老年癡呆症）
def_en: a chronic or persistent disorder of the mental processes caused by brain disease or injury and marked by memory disorders
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，香港人口老化議題必備核心詞彙（elderly patients with dementia）。
example: GPS tracking wristbands help families locate elderly relatives with dementia if they accidentally wander off.

def_zh: 阿茲海默症（最常見的認知障礙症類型）
def_en: progressive mental deterioration that can occur in middle or old age, due to generalized degeneration of the brain
prep_trap: 專有名詞，寫作時首字母大寫（Alzheimer's disease）。
example: Community day-care centres offer cognitive training games to slow memory decline in patients with Alzheimer's disease.

def_zh: 中風；中暑（heatstroke）；泳姿；神來之筆
def_en: a sudden disabling attack or loss of consciousness caused by an interruption in the flow of blood to the brain
prep_trap: 可數名詞（suffer a stroke 中風）；而中暑則是不可數名詞 heatstroke。
example: Outdoor construction workers must drink plenty of water and rest in the shade to prevent heatstroke.

def_zh: 中暑
def_en: a condition marked by fever and often by unconsciousness, caused by failure of the body's temperature-regulating mechanism when exposed to excessively high temperatures
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，極端酷熱天氣（extreme heat）與遠足安全題必考字。
example: Hikers should wear breathable clothing and carry sufficient water to prevent heatstroke in summer.

def_zh: 脫水（身體嚴重缺水）
def_en: a harmful reduction in the amount of water in the body
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 dehydrate，相反詞為 hydrate（stay hydrated 保持水分充足）。
example: Athletes running marathons in humid weather must drink electrolyte beverages at water stations to prevent dehydration.

def_zh: 補充水分
def_en: cause to absorb water; keep the body supplied with enough water
prep_trap: 常作形容詞分詞：stay hydrated（保持身體水分充足），運動日或遠足通告必用。
example: Installing water dispensers across the campus encourages students to bring reusable bottles and stay hydrated.

def_zh: 急救
def_en: help given to a sick or injured person until full medical treatment is available
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，作定語時常加連字號（a first-aid kit 急救箱 / first-aid station 急救站）。
example: Every secondary student should learn basic first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation to save lives in emergencies.

def_zh: 急救復甦術（如心肺復甦法 CPR）
def_en: the action or process of reviving someone from unconsciousness or apparent death
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，即 CPR（cardiopulmonary resuscitation）。
example: Installing automated external defibrillators in shopping malls and teaching resuscitation skills can save cardiac arrest victims.

def_zh: 心臟去顫器（俗稱 AED 自動體外心臟去顫器）
def_en: an apparatus used to control heart fibrillation by application of an electric current to the chest wall
prep_trap: 可數名詞，即香港公共場所及學校常見的 AED。
example: All sports grounds and school gymnasiums should be equipped with an automated external defibrillator for emergencies.

def_zh: 救護車（白車）
def_en: a vehicle specially equipped for taking sick or injured people to and from the hospital
prep_trap: 可數名詞，討論「濫用救護車服務」（abuse of ambulance services）時必用。
example: Calling an ambulance for minor scrapes wastes precious emergency resources needed by critically ill patients.

def_zh: 救護員（隨救護車出動的緊急醫療人員）
def_en: a health care worker who provides emergency medical assistance outside of a hospital
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: Frontline paramedics arrived at the accident scene within minutes to stabilize the injured cyclist.

def_zh: 傷亡人員；受害者；急症室（Casualty Department）
def_en: a person killed or injured in a war or accident, or a person/thing badly affected by an event
prep_trap: 可數名詞，複數為 casualties（注意不是 casual「便服/隨便」的意思！）。
example: Fortunately, the early typhoon warning system prevented any serious casualties when the storm hit the coast.

def_zh: 死亡事故；死者（因意外或災難死亡）
def_en: an occurrence of death by accident, in war, or from disease
prep_trap: 可數名詞，複數為 fatalities，源自形容詞 fatal（致命的）。
example: Stricter penalties for speeding and red-light jumping have significantly reduced road traffic fatalities.

def_zh: 致命的；災難性的（錯誤）
def_en: causing death, or leading to failure or disaster
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 a fatal accident（奪命意外）或 a fatal mistake（致命錯誤）。
example: Glancing at a mobile phone for just two seconds while driving can result in a fatal accident.

def_zh: 致命的；殺傷力極強的（武器或毒物）
def_en: sufficient to cause death; very harmful or destructive
prep_trap: 形容詞，多修飾毒物、藥物過量或武器（a lethal dose / weapon）。
example: Fentanyl and other synthetic drugs are so potent that even a tiny amount can be lethal.

def_zh: 接觸傳染的；（笑聲或熱情）具感染力的
def_en: of a disease spread from one person or organism to another by direct or indirect contact
prep_trap: 形容詞，既可形容傳染病（a highly contagious virus），亦可正面形容熱誠具感染力（contagious enthusiasm）。
example: Students with contagious illnesses like chickenpox or influenza must rest at home until fully recovered.

def_zh: 傳染性的；有感染力的
def_en: liable to be transmitted to people, organisms, etc. through the environment
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 infection（感染），常配 infectious diseases（傳染病）。
collocations: prevent the spread of infectious viruses
example: Wearing surgical masks in crowded clinics helps prevent the transmission of airborne infectious diseases.

def_zh: 流行病；疫情；（壞現象的）迅速蔓延
def_en: a widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community at a particular time
prep_trap: 可數名詞，亦可用於比喻肥胖或孤獨問題（an obesity / loneliness epidemic）。
example: Public health experts warn that urban isolation has created a silent loneliness epidemic among the elderly.

def_zh: （疾病、食物中毒或衝突）爆發
def_en: the sudden or violent start of something unwelcome, such as war, disease, etc.
prep_trap: 可數名詞，前面配 an，必配介詞 of（an outbreak of food poisoning / dengue fever）。
example: Clearing stagnant water in flowerpots every week prevents mosquito breeding and dengue fever outbreaks.

def_zh: 不流動的（積水）；停滯不前的（經濟或薪酬）
def_en: having no current or flow and often having an unpleasant smell, OR showing no activity or growth
prep_trap: 形容詞，動詞為 stagnate，名詞為 stagnation；衛生題配 stagnant water（積水生蚊），社會題配 stagnant wages（薪酬停滯）。
example: Stagnant wages combined with soaring housing rents have made it difficult for young graduates to save money.

def_zh: 由蚊傳播的（疾病，如登革熱）
def_en: carried or transmitted by mosquitoes
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，注意 borne 有 e（源自 bear 攜帶），同類字有 airborne（空氣傳播的）、waterborne（水源傳播的）。
example: Global warming allows mosquitoes to thrive in warmer winters, increasing the threat of mosquito-borne diseases.

def_zh: 齧齒目動物（尤指老鼠）
def_en: a gnawing mammal of an order that includes rats, mice, squirrels, and hamsters
prep_trap: 可數名詞，Paper 2/3 討論後巷環境衛生（back-alley hygiene）時替換 rats 的正式政府用字（rodent infestation 鼠患）。
example: Proper disposal of restaurant food waste in sealed bins is essential for curbing rodent infestations in back alleys.

def_zh: （害蟲、老鼠或木蝨）大量滋生；蟲鼠患
def_en: the presence of an unusually large number of insects or animals in a place, typically so as to cause damage or disease
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，常配 rodent / bedbug / mosquito infestation（鼠患 / 床蝨患 / 蚊患）。
example: Thermal steamers and thorough vacuuming are effective ways to eliminate bedbug infestations in crowded flats.

def_zh: 害蟲；有害動物（如老鼠、蟑螂）
def_en: a destructive insect or other animal that attacks crops, food, livestock, etc.
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 pest control（滅蟲防鼠工作）。
example: The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department stepped up pest control operations across public wet markets.

def_zh: 通風；空氣流通（室內或建築設計）
def_en: the provision of fresh air to a room, building, etc.
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 well-ventilated（空氣流通良好的）或 poorly ventilated（通風不良的，如劏房）。
example: Upgrading air purifiers and ventilation systems in classrooms reduces the risk of flu transmission.

def_zh: 幽閉恐懼的；空間狹小得令人窒息壓迫的
def_en: inducing or suffering from an extreme or irrational fear of confined places
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 描寫香港劏房（subdivided flats）或籠屋（coffin homes）狹窄壓迫環境的 5** 詞彙！
example: Growing up in a windowless, claustrophobic subdivided flat takes a heavy toll on children's mental health.

def_zh: 狹窄擁擠的（居住或工作空間）
def_en: uncomfortably small or restricted
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意字尾有 ed（cramped living conditions），香港房屋問題必背字。
example: Due to cramped living conditions at home, many public estate students prefer revising in community study rooms.

def_zh: 寬敞的；空間廣闊的
def_en: especially of a room or building having ample space
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意拼字沒有 e（spacious），與 cramped 相反。
example: The newly renovated youth centre features a bright and spacious dance studio with floor-to-ceiling mirrors.

def_zh: 破舊失修的；殘破危殆的（舊樓或設施）
def_en: of a building or object in a state of disrepair or ruin as a result of age or neglect
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 市區重建（urban renewal）與舊唐樓石屎剝落議題的 5** 形容詞！
example: Falling concrete from dilapidated tenement buildings poses a serious safety hazard to pedestrians below.

def_zh: 唐樓；舊式分租住宅大樓
def_en: a room or a set of rooms forming a separate residence within a house or block of apartments, especially older urban walk-up buildings
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港寫作中指沒有升降機的「舊唐樓」（old tenement buildings / walk-up tenements）。
example: Elderly residents living in walk-up tenement buildings without lifts struggle to climb five flights of stairs daily.

def_zh: 分間的（尤指香港「劏房」subdivided flats/units）
def_en: divided into smaller parts, especially a single apartment split into multiple tiny rental units
prep_trap: DSE 香港社會議題必背專有名詞：subdivided flats / units（劏房）！
example: Thousands of grassroots families live in poorly ventilated subdivided flats while waiting for public rental housing.

def_zh: 基層的；草根階層的（亦可作複數名詞：基層市民）
def_en: the most basic level of an activity or organization; ordinary working-class people
prep_trap: 無論作定語形容詞（grassroots families）或名詞（the grassroots），字尾都保留 s。
example: Community food banks provide free groceries to help grassroots families cope with rising food prices.

def_zh: 弱勢的；貧困清貧的（不享一般社會資源的）
def_en: not enjoying the same standard of living or rights as the majority of people in a society
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意字尾有 d，替換 poor students / families 最得體尊重的 DSE 高分字；加上 the 指「弱勢社群」（the underprivileged）。
example: Free after-school tutoring programmes help underprivileged children keep up with their wealthier classmates.

def_zh: 處於弱勢的；條件不利的
def_en: in unfavorable circumstances, especially with regard to financial or social opportunities
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意必須有 d（切勿寫成 disadvantage people！），常配 socially / financially disadvantaged。
example: Subsidized musical instrument classes give financially disadvantaged students a fair chance to develop artistic talents.

def_zh: 被邊緣化的；被社會忽視的（弱勢群體）
def_en: treated as insignificant or peripheral
prep_trap: 分詞形容詞（英式亦拼作 marginalised），動詞為 marginalize，名詞為 marginalization。
example: Language barriers often leave ethnic minority jobseekers feeling marginalized in the local employment market.

def_zh: 赤貧的；一貧如洗的（連基本食住都缺乏）
def_en: without the basic necessities of life; extremely poor
prep_trap: 形容詞，指極度貧困（比 poor 程度深得多），名詞為 destitution。
example: Emergency relief funds provide immediate cash assistance to families left destitute by sudden fires or accidents.

def_zh: 貧困的；窮困潦倒的
def_en: reduced to poverty
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意字尾有 ed，替換 poor 的高階寫作字。
example: Many impoverished elderly citizens collect cardboard boxes on the streets just to earn a few dollars.

def_zh: 富裕的；富足的
def_en: especially of a group or area having a great deal of money; wealthy
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 affluence（富裕，不可數），替換 rich 的 DSE 必備高分字！
example: Children from affluent families often enjoy private tutoring and overseas summer tours that widen the learning gap.

def_zh: 小康的；家境富裕的
def_en: wealthy; in a good financial position
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，與 impoverished / hard-up 相反。
example: Means-tested university grants ensure public funds go to needy students rather than those from well-off families.

def_zh: 懸殊；巨大差距（尤指貧富或資源差距）
def_en: a great difference, especially one perceived as unfair
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，DSE 貧富懸殊題必背：wealth disparity / income disparity（貧富差距）！
example: Widening wealth disparity in Hong Kong has sparked heated debate over the need for a fairer tax system.

def_zh: 不平等；不均（收入、教育或性別不平等）
def_en: difference in size, degree, circumstances, etc.; lack of equality
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，常配 social / income / gender inequality。
example: Providing free laptops and home Wi-Fi subsidies helps narrow digital inequality among secondary school students.

def_zh: 兩極化；分化（社會意見或貧富兩極化）
def_en: division into two sharply contrasting groups or sets of opinions or beliefs
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 polarize，討論社交媒體演算法（echo chambers）加劇社會分化時必用。
example: Social media algorithms often trap users in echo chambers and intensify opinion polarization.

def_zh: 階層化；社會階層固化
def_en: the arrangement or classification of something into different groups, especially social classes
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 social stratification（社會階層分化）。
example: When top schools only admit children from wealthy backgrounds, rigid social stratification becomes harder to break.

def_zh: 跨代的；代際之間的（如跨代貧窮或長幼共融）
def_en: relating to, involving, or affecting several generations
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 兩大必考搭配：intergenerational poverty（跨代貧窮）及 intergenerational harmony（長幼跨代共融）！
collocations: break the cycle of intergenerational poverty
example: Mentorship funds and quality education are key to breaking the vicious cycle of intergenerational poverty.

def_zh: 惡性的（循環）；惡毒兇殘的（攻擊）
def_en: deliberately cruel or violent, or continuing in a worsening self-reinforcing spiral
prep_trap: 形容詞，必背議論文高分片語：a vicious circle / cycle（惡性循環）！相反詞為 a virtuous cycle（良性循環）。
example: Lack of sleep leads to poor exam results and anxiety, trapping students in a vicious cycle.

def_zh: 良性的（循環）；品德高尚的
def_en: having or showing high moral standards, or creating a self-reinforcing positive effect
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自名詞 virtue（美德），必背搭配：create a virtuous cycle（創造良性循環）。
example: Regular exercise improves sleep quality and daytime energy, creating a virtuous cycle for mental wellness.

def_zh: 無家可歸問題；露宿街頭現象
def_en: the state of having no home
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，露宿者可稱為 homeless people / street sleepers / rough sleepers。
example: Providing temporary shelters alongside job placement services is essential for tackling chronic homelessness.

def_zh: 逼遷；驅逐租客
def_en: the action of expelling someone, especially a tenant, from a property
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，動詞為 evict（evict tenants from subdivided flats），租務管制（tenancy control）題必用。
example: Tenancy control laws protect vulnerable subdivided flat tenants from sudden rent hikes and unfair eviction.

def_zh: 租客；住戶
def_en: a person who occupies land or property rented from a landlord
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意字尾是 -ant，與業主 landlord 相對。
example: The Housing Authority enforces a marking scheme to penalize public housing tenants who litter or make excessive noise.

def_zh: 業主；房東；包租公
def_en: a person who rents land, a building, or an apartment to a tenant
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常討論業主濫收水電費（overcharging tenants for water and electricity）。
example: New regulations prohibit subdivided flat landlords from overcharging tenants for water and electricity.

def_zh: 按揭貸款；樓宇供款
def_en: a legal agreement by which a bank or other creditor lends money at interest in exchange for taking title of the debtor's property
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意中間的 t 完全不發音（讀 /ˈmɔːɡɪdʒ/）！
example: Many young couples delay having children because of the heavy financial burden of paying off a home mortgage.

def_zh: （買樓的）首期；訂金
def_en: an initial payment made when something is bought on credit, especially a home
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港青年置業難（homeownership difficulties）必提詞彙：save for a down payment（儲首期）。
example: Even university graduates with stable salaries need over ten years to save enough for a flat's down payment.

def_zh: 自置居所；置業（成為業主）
def_en: the state of owning a home
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，香港資助房屋有「居者有其屋計劃」（Home Ownership Scheme）。
example: Subsidized starter homes help young middle-class families achieve their dream of homeownership.

def_zh: 填海造地；開墾；回收再利用
def_en: the process of claiming something back or of returning land from the sea for building
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 reclaim（注意拼字中間沒有 i，是 reclamation！），香港土地供應與海洋保育爭論的核心字。
example: Large-scale land reclamation provides space for new towns but inevitably destroys marine habitats.

def_zh: 填海拓地；收回；重新煥發
def_en: retrieve or recover something previously lost, or bring land under cultivation/use from the sea
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常配 reclaim land from the sea。
example: Much of Hong Kong's central business district is built on land reclaimed from Victoria Harbour over the past century.

def_zh: 棕地（新界已荒廢或作露天貨櫃場的農地）
def_en: previously developed land, especially rural land used for open storage, container yards, or workshops
prep_trap: 常作定語 brownfield sites（棕地），DSE 討論「應發展棕地而非郊野公園邊陲」的 5** 必備專業詞彙！
example: Environmental groups urge the government to develop degraded brownfield sites before touching pristine country parks.

def_zh: 綠地（未曾開發的自然綠化土地）
def_en: undeveloped land in a city or rural area either used for agriculture or left to evolve naturally
prep_trap: 常作定語 greenfield sites，與 brownfield sites 相對。
example: Preserving greenfield sites on the fringes of cities helps mitigate the urban heat island effect.

def_zh: 邊陲；外圍邊緣地帶（如郊野公園邊陲）
def_en: the outer limits or edge of an area or object
prep_trap: 單數名詞，常配 on the periphery of country parks（在郊野公園邊陲），形容詞為 peripheral。
collocations: on the periphery of the city
example: Building housing estates on the periphery of country parks may fragment wildlife corridors and increase bushfire risks.

def_zh: 蠶食；侵佔（自然棲息地、公眾空間或個人私隱時間）
def_en: intrude on a person's territory or a thing considered to be a right; advance gradually beyond usual limits
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，必考介詞：encroach on / upon something（蠶食郊野公園 / 侵佔員工放工休息時間），名詞為 encroachment。
example: Instant messaging apps allow work messages to encroach upon employees' family time late at night.

def_zh: （城市的）無序擴張；蔓延（亦可作動詞）
def_en: the expansion of an urban or industrial area into the adjoining countryside in an irregular way
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必配 urban sprawl（城市無序擴張）。
example: Strict zoning laws and country park ordinances have protected Hong Kong's green hills from unchecked urban sprawl.

def_zh: 城市土地規劃分區（如商業區、住宅區、綠化地帶）
def_en: the act of dividing a city or town into zones reserved for different purposes such as residence and business
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 town planning and zoning laws（城市規劃與分區條例）。
example: Rezoning vacant industrial buildings for transitional housing can help ease the acute shortage of flats.

def_zh: 預製組件的（如「組裝合成」建築法 MiC）
def_en: manufactured in sections beforehand to enable quick or easy assembly on site
prep_trap: 形容詞，香港興建過渡性房屋與簡約公屋（Light Public Housing）常提的 prefabricated modules。
example: Using prefabricated building modules shortens construction time and reduces dust and noise on building sites.

def_zh: 天際線（摩天大廈構成的城市輪廓）
def_en: an outline of land and buildings defined against the sky
prep_trap: 可數名詞，形容維多利亞港兩岸景色必用：Hong Kong's iconic skyline。
example: Millions of tourists take the Star Ferry every year to admire Hong Kong's glittering harbour skyline.

def_zh: 摩天大樓
def_en: a very tall building of many stories
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意討論「屏風樓效應」（wall effect）時可配 densely packed skyscrapers。
example: Walls of densely packed coastal skyscrapers block sea breezes and worsen the urban heat island effect.

def_zh: 微氣候（如高樓林立街道的局部高溫環境）
def_en: the climate of a very small or restricted area, especially when this differs from the climate of the surrounding area
prep_trap: 可數名詞，討論城市綠化（vertical greening / rooftop gardens）改善市區溫度的專業詞彙。
example: Planting rooftop gardens and vertical green walls helps cool the surrounding urban microclimate during summer.

def_zh: 樹冠層（遮蔭的樹蔭）；天幕；遮陽篷
def_en: the uppermost branches of the trees in a forest, forming a more or less continuous layer of foliage, or an overhanging cover
prep_trap: 可數名詞，複數為 canopies，常配 urban tree canopy（市區樹冠遮蔭）。
example: Expanding the urban tree canopy along pavements provides natural shade and lowers street-level temperatures.

def_zh: 枝葉；綠葉（總稱）
def_en: plant leaves, collectively
prep_trap: 不可數集合名詞，切勿加 s！描寫郊野公園或秋季紅葉（autumn foliage）的優美詞彙。
example: Every December, thousands of hikers flock to Tai Tong in Yuen Long to photograph the vibrant red autumn foliage.

def_zh: 植物群（常與動物群 fauna 並用）
def_en: the plants of a particular region, habitat, or geological period
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 生態保育與地質公園題必背黃金拍檔：flora and fauna（動植物群）！
example: Guided eco-tours educate secondary students about the rich diversity of native flora and fauna in Hong Kong.

def_zh: 動物群；野生動物（常配 flora and fauna）
def_en: the animals of a particular region, habitat, or geological period
prep_trap: 不可數集合名詞，不加 s，常與 flora 連用。
example: Hill fires caused by careless grave-sweepers destroy thousands of trees and threaten local flora and fauna.

def_zh: 海洋的；海生的
def_en: of, found in, or produced by the sea
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意 marine life（海洋生物）中 life 為不可數名詞，切勿寫成 marine lives！
example: Discarded plastic bags and fishing nets entangle sea turtles and pose a deadly threat to marine life.

def_zh: 陸地的；陸生的（與海洋 marine 相對）
def_en: of, on, or relating to the earth or dry land
prep_trap: 形容詞，與 marine / aquatic 相對（terrestrial and marine ecosystems 陸地及海洋生態系統）。
example: Both terrestrial and marine ecosystems in Hong Kong are facing growing pressure from urban development.

def_zh: 水生的；水棲的；水上運動的
def_en: relating to water; living or growing in or near water
prep_trap: 形容詞，可指水生動植物（aquatic plants/animals）或水上運動中心（aquatic centre）。
example: Chemical runoff from factories depletes oxygen in rivers and suffocates aquatic organisms.

def_zh: 兩棲動物（如香港特有的盧氏小樹蛙）
def_en: a cold-blooded vertebrate animal of a class that comprises the frogs, toads, newts, and salamanders
prep_trap: 可數名詞，形容詞為 amphibious。
example: Polluting mountain streams with hiking litter endangers sensitive native amphibians such as Romer's tree frog.

def_zh: 鯨豚類海洋哺乳動物（如中華白海豚及江豚）
def_en: a marine mammal of the order Cetacea; a whale, dolphin, or porpoise
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 討論大嶼山填海與高速船威脅中華白海豚（Chinese white dolphins）時的 5** 專業字。
example: High-speed ferry traffic and underwater construction noise disrupt the sonar navigation of local cetaceans.

def_zh: （鯨魚或海豚）擱淺；（旅客因天氣）滯留
def_en: an instance of a whale, dolphin, or boat running aground on a shore
prep_trap: 可數名詞（whale strandings）；動詞被动 be stranded at the airport 指「滯留機場」。
example: Marine biologists investigate every dolphin stranding case to determine whether plastic ingestion or boat strikes caused its death.

def_zh: 聲納；回聲定位系統（海豚或蝙蝠覓食導航用）
def_en: a system for the detection of objects under water and for measuring the water's depth by emitting sound pulses
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，解釋海上工程噪音為何傷害海豚（interfere with dolphins' sonar）的關鍵詞彙。
example: Loud underwater piling noise interferes with Chinese white dolphins' natural sonar and prevents them from finding fish.

def_zh: 紅樹林（如米埔及流浮山海岸濕地）
def_en: a tree or shrub which grows in tidal, chiefly tropical, coastal swamps, having numerous tangled roots above ground
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 mangrove swamps / forests（紅樹林濕地），DSE 生態旅遊與減緩風暴潮（storm surges）必提例子。
example: Coastal mangrove forests not only nurture juvenile fish and crabs but also protect shorelines from typhoon waves.

def_zh: 濕地（如香港天水圍濕地公園及米埔）
def_en: land consisting of marshes or swamps; saturated land
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，常配 coastal wetlands。
example: Field trips to the Hong Kong Wetland Park teach primary students why conserving mudflats and marshes is vital.

def_zh: 泥炭地（儲存大量碳的自然濕地）
def_en: land consisting largely of peat or peat bogs, acting as a major natural carbon sink
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞。
example: Conserving forests, mangroves, and peatlands is one of the most cost-effective ways to absorb atmospheric carbon.

def_zh: 重新造林；植樹復林
def_en: the process of replanting an area with trees
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，與 deforestation（濫伐林木）相反。
example: Every spring, student volunteers join countryside reforestation days to replant native saplings on hillsides damaged by fire.

def_zh: 濫伐林木；森林砍伐
def_en: the action of clearing a wide area of trees
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s，全球暖化與生物多樣性喪失的核心成因字。
example: Rampant deforestation in tropical rainforests destroys wildlife habitats and accelerates global warming.

def_zh: 減碳；去碳化
def_en: the reduction or removal of carbon dioxide emissions from energy sources
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 decarbonize，香港《氣候行動藍圖 2050》核心詞彙。
example: Transitioning from coal to natural gas and solar energy is central to Hong Kong's decarbonization strategy.

def_zh: 電氣化（尤指公共交通轉用電動車）
def_en: the process of making a system or machine work using electricity
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 fleet electrification（車隊電動化）。
example: Accelerating the electrification of public buses and taxis will significantly improve roadside air quality.

def_zh: 混合動力的；混合模式的（如混合教學或辦公）
def_en: combining two different elements, such as a petrol engine and electric motor, or online and in-person work
prep_trap: 可作形容詞或名詞，既可指混能車（hybrid vehicles），亦可指混合辦公/學習（hybrid learning）。
example: Many companies have adopted a flexible hybrid working mode that combines office days with remote work.

def_zh: 氫；氫能（新能源）
def_en: a colorless, odorless gas that is being developed as a clean zero-emission fuel
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常作定語：hydrogen fuel-cell buses（氫能雙層巴士）。
example: Testing hydrogen fuel-cell double-decker buses marks a new milestone in Hong Kong's green transport transition.

def_zh: 生物燃料（由廚餘廢油或植物提煉的環保燃料）
def_en: a fuel derived directly from living matter or organic waste
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，DSE 常考將餐廳「廢置食用油」轉化為 biodiesel / biofuel。
example: Recycling used cooking oil from restaurants into sustainable biofuel reduces both water pollution and carbon emissions.

def_zh: 地熱的（地熱能發電）
def_en: relating to or produced by the internal heat of the earth
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 geothermal energy（地熱能）。
example: Countries with volcanic activity can harness geothermal energy to provide clean heating and electricity.

def_zh: 水力發電的
def_en: relating to or denoting the generation of electricity using flowing water
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 hydroelectricity / hydropower（水力發電）。
example: While large hydroelectric dams generate clean electricity, they may flood valleys and displace local villagers.

def_zh: 利用；開發（自然能源、科技或青年潛能）
def_en: control and make use of natural resources, especially to produce energy, or utilize skills
prep_trap: 及物動詞，DSE 環保與科技題替換 use 的 5** 動詞：harness solar energy / harness the power of AI！
example: Schools should learn how to harness the power of artificial intelligence to personalize student learning.

def_zh: 水塘；水庫；知識寶庫
def_en: a large natural or artificial lake used as a source of water supply
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意字尾拼字是 -voir（讀 /vwɑː/），香港遠足與水資源題常提（floating solar panels on reservoirs）。
example: Installing floating solar panels on reservoirs generates renewable electricity while reducing water evaporation.

def_zh: 海水化淡（如將軍澳海水化淡廠）
def_en: the process of removing salt from seawater so that it can be used for drinking
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，香港水資源安全必提例子：Tseung Kwan O Desalination Plant。
example: Operating a seawater desalination plant provides Hong Kong with a climate-resilient source of fresh drinking water.

def_zh: 植林；造林（在原本無樹的土地種樹）
def_en: the act of establishing a forest, especially on land not previously forested
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意雙寫 f（afforestation）。
example: Large-scale afforestation projects help stabilize hillside soil and absorb atmospheric carbon dioxide.

def_zh: 侵蝕；水土流失；（信心的）削弱
def_en: the gradual destruction or diminution of something by wind, water, or other natural agents
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 erode，常配 soil erosion（水土流失）或 coastal erosion（海岸侵蝕）。
example: Tree roots bind the earth together and prevent severe soil erosion during heavy summer rainstorms.

def_zh: 山泥傾瀉；（選舉的）壓倒性勝利
def_en: a collapse of a mass of earth or rock from a mountain or cliff
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港暴雨常發生的自然災害（landslide warning 山泥傾瀉警告）。
example: Torrential rain triggered several landslides across the territory, blocking mountain roads and hiking trails.

def_zh: 傾盆的；滂沱的（大雨）
def_en: of rain falling rapidly and in copious quantities
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 描寫黑雨或颱風暴雨的必備高分搭配：torrential rain / downpours！
example: The super typhoon brought torrential rain that flooded underground shopping malls and subway stations.

def_zh: 水浸的；積水飽和的（街道、球場或農田）
def_en: saturated with or full of water
prep_trap: 形容詞，運動日因雨取消或極端天氣水浸題極好用（a waterlogged sports ground）。
example: The inter-school football final had to be postponed because the grass pitch was completely waterlogged.

def_zh: 排水系統；渠務
def_en: the system of drains and pipes by which water or waste liquid is drained from an area
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，香港應對世紀暴雨必提：upgrade stormwater drainage systems（升級雨水排放系統）。
example: Upgrading underground stormwater drainage tunnels is vital for preventing flash floods in low-lying urban areas.

def_zh: 用完即棄的；崇尚丟棄浪費的（文化）
def_en: denoting or relating to products that are intended to be discarded after being used once
prep_trap: 形容詞，只作定語，DSE 批評速食時裝或即棄塑膠必背詞組：a throwaway culture / society（即棄文化）！
example: Fast fashion fuels a wasteful throwaway culture where teenagers discard cheap clothes after wearing them once.

def_zh: 守護者；管理員；（活動場地）糾察幹事
def_en: a person employed to look after passengers or supervise arrangements at a large public event, or a guardian of nature
prep_trap: 可數名詞，既可指地球守護者（stewards of the planet），Paper 3 亦常指運動會場地糾察（student stewards）。
example: Education should inspire young people to act as responsible stewards of our planet's natural resources.

def_zh: 可生物降解的（能被微生物自然分解的）
def_en: of a substance or object capable of being decomposed by bacteria or other living organisms
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 環保減塑議題核心字：biodegradable plastics / packaging。
example: Replacing styrofoam lunchboxes with biodegradable containers helps reduce permanent plastic pollution in landfills.

def_zh: 發泡膠（聚苯乙烯泡沫塑膠）
def_en: a kind of expanded polystyrene used especially for making food containers
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（香港亦常用 polyfoam），走塑政策（plastic-free policy）常提 styrofoam lunchboxes。
example: Banning single-use styrofoam lunchboxes for takeaway meals has significantly reduced white pollution along beaches.

def_zh: 用完即棄的；（收入）可自由支配的
def_en: intended to be thrown away after use, OR financial income remaining after taxes
prep_trap: 形容詞，環保題配 disposable cutlery（即棄餐具）；經濟題配 disposable income（可支配收入）。
example: Bringing a reusable tumbler to coffee shops eliminates the need for hundreds of disposable paper cups.

def_zh: 一次性的；即棄的
def_en: designed to be used once and then disposed of or destroyed
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，注意中間有連字號且 use 不加 d，必配 single-use plastics。
example: Since the legislation banning single-use plastic tableware took effect, more diners have brought their own cutlery.

def_zh: 堆填區；垃圾掩埋場
def_en: a site for the disposal of waste materials by burial
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，香港垃圾問題必背金句：Our three strategic landfills are nearing full capacity（三個堆填區將近飽和）！
example: Food waste recycling schemes are urgently needed because Hong Kong's landfills are rapidly reaching full capacity.

def_zh: 堆肥；有機肥料（亦可作動詞：將廚餘堆肥）
def_en: decayed organic material used as a plant fertilizer
prep_trap: 不可數名詞或及物動詞，校園環保建議常提：install a food waste composter to turn leftovers into compost。
example: Our Gardening Club uses a composting machine to turn canteen fruit peels into nutrient-rich compost.

def_zh: 排放；排放物（尤指碳排放或廢氣排放）
def_en: the production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation
prep_trap: 常用複數形式 carbon emissions / greenhouse gas emissions（溫室氣體排放），動詞為 emit。
example: Switching from private cars to mass transit railways is the most effective way to slash carbon emissions.

def_zh: 足印；（碳或生態）足跡
def_en: the impact that a person, organization, or activity has on the environment
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 環保作文必背搭配：reduce our carbon footprint / ecological footprint！
example: Buying locally grown seasonal vegetables reduces the carbon footprint caused by long-distance air freight.

def_zh: 中立；中和（尤指碳中和 carbon neutrality）
def_en: the state of not supporting or helping either side in a conflict, or achieving net-zero carbon emissions
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，香港特區政府目標在 2050 年前實現 carbon neutrality（碳中和）。
example: Achieving carbon neutrality by 2050 requires concerted efforts in energy saving, green buildings, and waste reduction.

def_zh: 可再生的（能源）；可續期的（合約）
def_en: of a natural resource or source of energy not depleted when used
prep_trap: 形容詞，複數名詞 renewables 指可再生能源（renewable energy sources）。
example: Investing in renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power reduces our reliance on fossil fuels.

def_zh: 不可再生的（如煤、石油、天然氣等化石燃料）
def_en: of a natural resource existing in finite amounts and not capable of being replenished quickly
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，常配 non-renewable fossil fuels。
example: Burning non-renewable fossil fuels for electricity releases massive amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

def_zh: 可持續性；可持續發展
def_en: avoidance of the depletion of natural resources in order to maintain an ecological balance
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 sustainable（sustainable development 可持續發展）。
example: Integrating environmental sustainability into business operations helps companies build a positive brand image.

def_zh: 可持續的；環保長遠的
def_en: able to be maintained at a certain rate or level; conserving an ecological balance
prep_trap: 形容詞，相反詞為 unsustainable（難以為繼的 / 過度消耗的）。
example: Adopting a sustainable lifestyle begins with simple habits like refusing plastic bags and saving water.

def_zh: 生物多樣性
def_en: the variety of plant and animal life in the world or in a particular habitat
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，不加 s，DSE 討論郊野公園或填海議題的必考核心字：preserve rich biodiversity！
example: Hong Kong's country parks cover forty percent of our land mass and support remarkably rich biodiversity.

def_zh: 生態系統；（創業或創科）生態圈
def_en: a biological community of interacting organisms and their physical environment
prep_trap: 可數名詞，除自然生態（fragile marine ecosystem）外，亦可指創科生態圈（start-up ecosystem）。
example: Dumping untreated industrial sewage into rivers can destroy the entire freshwater ecosystem.

def_zh: （動植物的）自然棲息地；生長環境
def_en: the natural home or environment of an animal, plant, or other organism
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，切勿與 habit（習慣）或 inhabitant（居民/棲息動物）混淆！
example: Reclaiming shallow coastal waters causes irreversible habitat loss for endangered Chinese white dolphins.

def_zh: 居民；棲息動物
def_en: a person or animal that lives in or occupies a place
prep_trap: 可數名詞，源自動詞 inhabit（居住於，及物動詞不加 in）。
example: Eco-tourists should respect the customs and privacy of local village inhabitants when visiting rural areas.

def_zh: 瀕危的；瀕臨絕種的（物種或傳統技藝）
def_en: of a species seriously at risk of extinction
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意字尾有 ed，必配 endangered species（瀕危物種）。
example: Green turtles and black-faced spoonbills are endangered species that visit Hong Kong's coastal waters.

def_zh: 絕種；滅絕；（傳統文化的）消亡
def_en: the state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 extinct（已絕種的），常配 on the brink / verge of extinction（瀕臨絕種邊緣）。
example: Without urgent international conservation efforts, many polar animals will face extinction within this century.

def_zh: 已滅絕的；絕跡的；（火山）死寂的
def_en: of a species, family, or other group of animals or plants having no living members
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 become / go extinct（滅絕）。
example: Traditional handwritten neon signs could soon become extinct if no young artisans learn the craft.

def_zh: 保育（大自然或歷史古蹟）；節約（能源或水）
def_en: preservation, protection, or restoration of the natural environment and of wildlife, or historical monuments
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿與 conversation（對話）拼錯！保育人士為 conservationist。
example: Striking a balance between urban development and heritage conservation is a major challenge for town planners.

def_zh: 自然或古蹟保育人士
def_en: a person who advocates or acts for the protection and preservation of the environment and wildlife
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 議論文引述環保人士觀點時必用：Conservationists argue that...。
example: Conservationists warn that building roads through wetlands will drive away migratory birds.

def_zh: 保存；維護（古蹟原貌、文化或食品）
def_en: the action of preserving something in its original state
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，與 conservation 相比，preservation 更強調「原封不動地保存歷史原貌」。
example: Digitizing ancient manuscripts and photographs aids in the long-term preservation of local history.

def_zh: 污染物；有害雜質（水源、食物或空氣中）
def_en: a polluting or poisonous substance that makes something impure
prep_trap: 可數名詞，字尾是 -ant。
example: Advanced water filtration systems remove heavy metals and chemical contaminants from tap water.

def_zh: 污染物（排放到空氣、水或土壤中的有害物質）
def_en: a substance that pollutes something, especially water or the atmosphere
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意拼字字尾是 -ant（與不可數的「污染」pollution 區分清楚）。
example: Idling vehicle engines on busy streets emit toxic air pollutants that harm pedestrians' lungs.

def_zh: 污水；排泄廢水
def_en: waste water and excrement conveyed in sewers
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s！必考搭配：sewage treatment plant（污水處理廠）。
example: Discharging untreated industrial sewage into rivers kills fish and contaminates drinking water sources.

def_zh: （工廠或農場排出的）液態廢水、污水
def_en: liquid waste or sewage discharged into a river or the sea
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，注意與 affluent（富裕的）只差首字母 e/a！
example: Factories that illegally discharge toxic effluent into streams should face heavy fines and prosecution.

def_zh: 地表徑流（雨水沖刷農田化肥或街道污染物入河）
def_en: the draining away of water (and substances carried in it) from the surface of an area of land
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 agricultural runoff（含農藥化肥的農田徑流導致紅潮）。
example: Agricultural runoff containing chemical fertilizers washes into coastal waters and triggers harmful red tides.

def_zh: 藻華；紅潮（水中藻類異常大量繁殖導致魚類缺氧死亡）
def_en: a rapid increase or accumulation in the population of algae in freshwater or marine water systems
prep_trap: 可數名詞，即紅潮（red tide）的科學專業寫法。
example: Warm water and nutrient pollution can trigger harmful algal blooms that suffocate farmed fish.

def_zh: 乾旱；旱災
def_en: a prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall, leading to a shortage of water
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，注意發音為 /draʊt/（字尾是 t），與 flood（水災）相對。
example: Climate change has brought prolonged droughts to agricultural regions, threatening global food supplies.

def_zh: 饑荒
def_en: extreme scarcity of food
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，常由 drought（乾旱）或 war 引發。
example: Extreme weather events and prolonged droughts have pushed millions of people toward severe famine.

def_zh: 大災難；浩劫
def_en: an event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意四音節讀法（字尾 e 讀 /fi/），形容詞為 catastrophic（災難性的）。
example: Immediate global action is required to avert an irreversible climate catastrophe.

def_zh: 災難性的；毀滅性的
def_en: involving or causing sudden great damage or suffering
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 very bad / disastrous 的高分詞彙。
example: Melting polar ice caps could have catastrophic consequences for low-lying coastal cities worldwide.

def_zh: 災禍；不幸災難
def_en: an event causing great and often sudden damage or distress; a disaster
prep_trap: 可數名詞，複數為 calamities。
example: Emergency relief funds help communities rebuild their homes after natural calamities such as earthquakes.

def_zh: 摧毀；使荒蕪；令某人極度悲痛震驚
def_en: destroy or ruin something, or cause someone severe and overwhelming shock or grief
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常作分詞形容詞：devastating（具毀滅性的，修飾颱風或影響）及 devastated（悲痛欲絕的，修飾人）。
example: The super typhoon had a devastating impact on coastal fishing villages and farmland.

def_zh: 蹂躪；嚴重毀壞（自然災害、山火或疾病）
def_en: cause severe and extensive damage to
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常用被動語態：be ravaged by bushfires / war / floods。
example: Volunteers planted thousands of tree seedlings on the hillside that had been ravaged by autumn bushfires.

def_zh: 禍害；社會毒瘤（如毒品、詐騙或欺凌）
def_en: a person or thing that causes great trouble or suffering
prep_trap: 單數名詞，配 the scourge of something（某種嚴重社會禍害），議論文極具氣勢的用字。
example: Cross-border police cooperation is essential for eradicating the scourge of online telecom fraud.

def_zh: 威脅；危險人物或禍患（亦可作動詞）
def_en: a person or thing that is likely to cause harm; a threat or danger
prep_trap: 單數可數名詞，常配介詞 to（pose a menace to public safety 對公眾安全構成威脅）。
example: Illegal road racing late at night poses a serious menace to innocent pedestrians and motorists.

def_zh: 巨大危險；危難
def_en: serious and immediate danger
prep_trap: 不可數或可數名詞，形容詞為 perilous（危機四伏的），常配 put lives in peril。
example: Hiking alone during a typhoon warning puts both your own life and rescue workers in grave peril.

def_zh: 安全隱患；危險源（如消防、交通或健康隱患）
def_en: a danger or risk
prep_trap: 可數名詞，形容詞為 hazardous（危險有害的，如 hazardous chemical waste），投訴信與安全報告必備字！
example: Stacking cardboard boxes in building staircases blocks escape routes and creates a deadly fire hazard.

def_zh: 不穩定的；朝不保夕的（工作或生計）；搖搖欲墜的
def_en: not securely held or in position; dangerously likely to fall or collapse; uncertain
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 討論零工經濟（gig economy）外賣員缺乏勞工保障時必配 precarious employment / livelihood！
example: Many platform delivery riders face precarious employment without paid sick leave or retirement protection.

def_zh: 動盪易變的（局勢或市場）；情緒易暴躁失控的
def_en: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 volatility。
example: In a volatile global economy, young people must equip themselves with adaptable lifelong learning skills.

def_zh: 動盪不安的；波濤洶湧的；（青春期）跌宕起伏的
def_en: characterized by conflict, disorder, or confusion; not controlled or calm
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 turbulence（氣流顛簸 / 動盪）。
example: Supportive teachers act as a steady anchor for teenagers navigating the turbulent years of adolescence.

def_zh: 熱烈歡呼的（掌聲）；動盪劇烈的
def_en: making a loud, confused noise; uproarious, or excited, confused, or disorderly
prep_trap: 形容詞，活動報告描寫觀眾掌聲雷動時可用 tumultuous applause。
example: The school choir received tumultuous applause from the audience after their moving finale performance.

def_zh: 響亮的；徹底而巨大的（成功）
def_en: unmistakable; emphatic; very great
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE Paper 2/3 活動報告總結活動大獲成功的必背金句詞組：a resounding success！
example: Thanks to the tireless efforts of student volunteers, our Annual Charity Fun Fair was a resounding success.

def_zh: 重大勝利；成功壯舉（亦可作動詞：戰勝）
def_en: a great victory or achievement
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，作動詞配介詞 over（triumph over adversity 戰勝逆境）；形容詞為 triumphant。
example: Crossing the marathon finish line after months of injury recovery was a moment of personal triumph.

def_zh: 壯舉；高難度成就；本領
def_en: an achievement that requires great courage, skill, or strength
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 no mean feat / no easy feat（絕非易事/了不起的成就）。
example: Balancing student union duties with public exam revision is no easy feat for Form Five leaders.

def_zh: 成就；完成；才藝
def_en: something that has been achieved successfully
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，必背搭配：a strong sense of accomplishment（強烈的成功感/成就感）。
example: Completing a fifty-kilometre charity hike gives teenagers a lasting sense of accomplishment and confidence.

def_zh: 滿足感；自我實現；履行（職責）
def_en: satisfaction or happiness as a result of fully developing one's abilities or character
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（美式拼作 fulfillment），常配 personal / job fulfilment（個人/工作滿足感）。
example: Many young volunteers find that helping disadvantaged children brings greater inner fulfilment than material wealth.

def_zh: 滿足；喜悅（尤指即時享樂 vs 延遲滿足）
def_en: pleasure, especially when gained from the satisfaction of a desire
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 青少年心理與自律題 5** 詞組：instant gratification（即時滿足）vs delayed gratification（延遲滿足）！
example: Social media conditions teenagers to expect instant gratification rather than practising patience and delayed gratification.

def_zh: 知足常樂；安然滿足
def_en: a state of happiness and satisfaction
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 content（be content with what one has 知足，注意讀 /kənˈtent/）。
example: True happiness comes from gratitude and inner contentment rather than endless comparison with others online.

def_zh: 極度興奮；欣快感（如奪冠或放榜高分一刻）
def_en: a feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 euphoric。
example: A wave of euphoria swept through the stadium when our school relay team broke the record.

def_zh: 興高采烈；歡欣鼓舞
def_en: great happiness and exhilaration
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 elated（感到欣喜若狂的）。
example: Seeing our hand-built robot complete the obstacle course filled every team member with sheer elation.

def_zh: 令人極度興奮暢快的；扣人心弦的（戶外活動或體驗）
def_en: making one feel very happy, animated, or elated; thrilling
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意中間有不發音的 h（exhilarating），描寫水上運動、衝浪或過山車的極佳高分字。
example: Windsurfing across the waves in Stanley is an exhilarating outdoor activity for adventurous teenagers.

def_zh: 緊張刺激的；扣人心弦的（比賽或表演）
def_en: causing excitement and pleasure; exhilarating
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 thrill（a thrill of excitement）。
example: The inter-house basketball final was a thrilling match that kept spectators on the edge of their seats.

def_zh: 扣人心弦的；引人入勝得令人放不低的（書籍或電影）
def_en: firmly holding the attention or interest; exciting
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意雙寫 p，書評或影評（Book/Film Review）替換 interesting 的滿分詞彙！
example: The gripping detective novel kept me turning the pages until midnight to discover the culprit.

def_zh: 引人入勝的；令人全神貫注的
def_en: absorbing all one's attention or interest
prep_trap: 形容詞，被動結構 be engrossed in a book（全神貫注看書）極常用。
example: To cultivate reading habits, school libraries should stock engrossing fiction alongside academic reference books.

def_zh: 精彩絕倫的；牢牢吸引注意力的（演講或表演）
def_en: completely engrossing; compelling
prep_trap: 形容詞，修飾演講、戲劇或紀錄片。
example: The guest speaker delivered a riveting talk on his expedition to the South Pole.

def_zh: 感人肺腑的；令人心酸動容的；深刻的
def_en: evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret; deeply moving
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意中間 g 不發音（讀 /ˈpɔɪnjənt/），書評、影評或描寫探訪長者經歷的 5** 詞彙！
example: The film offers a poignant portrayal of an elderly mother struggling with memory loss and loneliness.

def_zh: 喚起回憶或感情的；令人共鳴的
def_en: bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自動詞 evoke（喚起），常配介詞 of（evocative of old Hong Kong）。
example: The exhibition features evocative black-and-white photographs of Hong Kong's street life in the 1960s.

def_zh: 莊嚴肅穆的；憂鬱沉重的（氣氛或心情）
def_en: dark or dull in color or tone; gloomy; serious and solemn
prep_trap: 形容詞（美式拼作 somber），描寫參觀戰爭紀念館或歷史博物館氣氛時極精準。
example: A sombre silence fell over the students as they walked through the wartime history gallery.

def_zh: 憂鬱；傷感（亦可作形容詞：憂傷的）
def_en: a feeling of pensive sadness, typically with no obvious cause
prep_trap: 不可數名詞或形容詞，注意 ch 發 /k/ 音。
example: Listening to the gentle rain outside the window filled the poet with a quiet sense of melancholy.

def_zh: 灰心喪氣的；情緒低落沮喪的（因失敗或挫折）
def_en: in low spirits from loss of hope or courage
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 sad / upset 的高階情緒字，名詞為 despondency。
example: Students should not feel despondent over a single disappointing mock exam result.

def_zh: 垂頭喪氣的；失落沮喪的
def_en: sad and depressed; dispirited
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫落敗或未獲錄取時的失落神情（look dejected）。
example: Our coach comforted the dejected football players and praised them for fighting until the final whistle.

def_zh: 垂頭喪氣的；大失所望的
def_en: sad and disappointed
prep_trap: 形容詞，生動描寫「原本滿懷希望卻落空」的失望神態。
example: Although she looked crestfallen after missing out on the scholarship, she vowed to try again next year.

def_zh: 心煩意亂的；極度焦慮悲痛的
def_en: very worried and upset; agitated with grief or anxiety
prep_trap: 形容詞，常形容失蹤學童家長或意外受害者家屬（distraught parents）。
example: Police officers and social workers comforted the distraught elderly woman who had been tricked by phone scammers.

def_zh: 劇烈痛苦；極度煎熬（精神或肉體上）
def_en: severe mental or physical pain or suffering
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 mental anguish（精神煎熬）。
example: Cyberbullying inflicts severe mental anguish on teenage victims, even when no physical harm occurs.

def_zh: 折磨；痛苦煎熬（作動詞讀 /tɔːˈment/：折磨、欺凌）
def_en: severe physical or mental suffering
prep_trap: 可作不可數名詞或及物動詞，欺凌議題常配 emotional torment。
example: Many victims of school bullying suffer in silent torment because they are afraid to tell teachers.

def_zh: 懊悔；悔恨；良心自責
def_en: deep regret or guilt for a wrong committed
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必配介詞 for（show genuine remorse for one's mistake），形容詞為 remorseful（悔疚的）。
example: Restorative justice programmes encourage young offenders to apologize to victims and show genuine remorse.

def_zh: 悔過的；深感歉意的
def_en: feeling or expressing remorse or penitence; affected by guilt
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 contrition（悔意）。
example: Because the student offered a sincere and contrite apology, the discipline master gave him a second chance.

def_zh: 悔過的；懺悔的
def_en: feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong; repentant
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Community service orders allow penitent first-time offenders to make amends by serving society.

def_zh: 賠罪；補償（必配 make amends）
def_en: reparation or compensation for a loss, damage, or insult
prep_trap: 複數形式名詞，必背固定片語：make amends for a mistake / to somebody（彌補過錯）。
example: Apologizing sincerely and repairing the damaged property is the best way to make amends for one's mistake.

def_zh: 洗脫罪名；證明無辜；免除責任
def_en: absolve someone from blame for a fault or wrongdoing
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常配 exonerate somebody from blame。
example: Security camera footage from the shop exonerated the student who had been falsely accused of shoplifting.

def_zh: 證明（某人或某決定）正確無誤；還⋯⋯清白
def_en: clear someone of blame or suspicion, OR show or prove to be right, reasonable, or justified
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常指當初受質疑的決定最終被事實證明是對的（feel vindicated）。
example: The dramatic drop in plastic bag usage vindicated the government's decision to increase the levy.

def_zh: 元兇；罪魁禍首；犯錯者
def_en: a person who is responsible for a crime or other misdeed, or the cause of a problem
basic_word: main cause of a problem / offender
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 議論文分析問題主因時極好用：The main culprit behind childhood obesity is...（兒童肥胖的主因是⋯⋯）！
example: Excessive screen time late at night is the main culprit behind chronic sleep deprivation among youth.

def_zh: 施暴者；作案者；欺凌者（與受害者 victim 相對）
def_en: a person who carries out a harmful, illegal, or immoral act
prep_trap: 可數名詞，字尾是 -or，動詞為 perpetrate；討論網上欺凌或詐騙時，perpetrators 與 victims 對舉極具專業感！
example: Online anonymity often emboldens perpetrators of cyberbullying to post cruel comments without fear of punishment.

def_zh: 共犯；幫兇
def_en: a person who helps another commit a crime
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 silent accomplice（沉默的幫兇，如欺凌事件中的旁觀者 bystanders）。
example: Bystanders who laugh at or forward cyberbullying messages become silent accomplices to the cruelty.

def_zh: 旁觀者；袖手旁觀的人
def_en: a person who is present at an event or incident but does not take part
prep_trap: 可數名詞，校園欺凌題必提：turn passive bystanders into active upstanders（將冷漠旁觀者轉化為挺身而出的助人者）！
example: Anti-bullying workshops teach students not to be passive bystanders when they witness a classmate being teased.

def_zh: 代罪羔羊（亦可作動詞：拿某人當代罪羔羊）
def_en: a person who is blamed for the wrongdoings, mistakes, or faults of others
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 make somebody a scapegoat for something。
example: Blaming video games alone as a scapegoat for youth violence ignores deeper family and social problems.

def_zh: 阻嚇作用；威懾力（刑罰或罰款）
def_en: the action of discouraging an action or event through instilling doubt or fear of the consequences
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意雙寫 r，與可數名詞 deterrent（阻嚇物/阻嚇措施）同字根。
example: Increasing the fixed penalty for littering to three thousand dollars provides strong deterrence against offenders.

def_zh: 重犯率；累犯現象（釋囚出獄後再次犯罪）
def_en: the tendency of a convicted criminal to reoffend
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，討論更生服務（rehabilitation services）成效時的 5** 專業名詞：reduce recidivism！
example: Providing vocational training to young inmates helps them find stable jobs after release and reduces recidivism.

def_zh: 拘留；羈押；（子女的）撫養監護權
def_en: the protective care or guardianship of someone or something, or imprisonment
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，配 in custody（被羈留中）或 child custody（子女撫養權）。
example: Suspects arrested for operating online scam syndicates are held in police custody pending trial.

def_zh: 感化令；試用期（職場或法律）
def_en: the release of an offender from detention, subject to a period of good behavior under supervision, or a workplace trial period
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，配 on probation（在感化期間 / 在試用期內），感化官為 probation officer。
example: First-time juvenile offenders are often placed on probation under the supervision of a social worker.

def_zh: 門禁時間；宵禁（家長或宿舍規定回家時間）
def_en: a regulation requiring people to remain indoors between specified hours, or a family rule on when a teenager must return home
basic_word: time limit to be home at night
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 討論父母管教或大學迎新營（O-camp）規矩時常配 impose a curfew on teenagers。
example: Reasonable parents negotiate a sensible weekend curfew with their teenage children instead of locking them indoors.

def_zh: （對犯錯子女的）禁足處罰；基礎訓練
def_en: a solid foundation in a subject, OR punishing a child by forbidding them to go out
prep_trap: 作「學科基礎」時配 a solid grounding in English；作動詞 be grounded 指被父母「禁足」不准出街。
example: Primary education should provide children with a solid grounding in both literacy and numeracy.

def_zh: 嚴厲批評；責罰；斥責
def_en: rebuke or reprimand severely
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常配 chastise somebody for doing something（因某事嚴責某人）。
example: Wise teachers guide students privately rather than chastising them in front of the whole class.

def_zh: 訓誡；嚴詞斥責（亦可作名詞：申斥）
def_en: rebuke someone, especially officially
prep_trap: 及物動詞或可數名詞，比 scold 正式得多，常指校長、訓導主任或上司的正式訓斥。
example: The employee received a formal written reprimand for leaking confidential customer information.

def_zh: 指責；非難；訓斥（亦可作名詞）
def_en: express sharp disapproval or criticism of someone because of their behavior or actions
prep_trap: 及物動詞或可數名詞，常配 sharply rebuke。
example: The judge issued a stern rebuke to the contractor for ignoring workplace safety regulations.

def_zh: 告誡；規勸；溫和地訓誡
def_en: warn or reprimand someone firmly; advise or urge earnestly
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常配 admonish somebody to do something（叮囑/告誡某人做某事）。
example: Our class teacher gently admonished us not to leave our revision until the night before exams.

def_zh: 責罵；申斥
def_en: find fault with someone; scold
prep_trap: 及物動詞，配介詞 for（upbraid somebody for carelessness）。
example: Instead of upbraiding players for missing a shot, a good coach analyses how to improve teamwork.

def_zh: 公開譴責；嚴厲批評（亦可作不可數名詞）
def_en: express severe disapproval of someone or something, especially in a formal statement
prep_trap: 正式動詞或不可數名詞，注意與 censor（審查刪剪）拼字及意思完全不同！
example: Medical associations publicly censure doctors who engage in unethical advertising practices.

def_zh: 審查；刪剪（電影、書籍或網上言論）
def_en: examine a book, movie, etc. officially and suppress unacceptable parts of it
prep_trap: 及物動詞，名詞為 censorship（審查制度，不可數），討論網絡規管與言論自由時必考！
example: Parents can install parental control software to filter and censor violent content on their children's tablets.

def_zh: 審查制度（如電影分級審查或網絡內容審查）
def_en: the suppression or prohibition of any parts of books, films, news, etc. that are considered obscene or harmful
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 media / internet censorship 或 self-censorship（自我審查）。
example: Striking a balance between protecting minors from harmful websites and avoiding excessive internet censorship is difficult.

def_zh: 誹謗（抹黑損害他人名譽的言論）
def_en: the action of damaging the good reputation of someone; slander or libel
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 defame，DSE 討論「網絡起底與鍵盤戰士造謠」是否犯法時的 5** 法律詞彙！
example: Freedom of speech on social media does not give users the right to spread malicious defamation.

def_zh: 惡意中傷；口頭誹謗（亦可作動詞）
def_en: the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation
prep_trap: 不可數名詞或及物動詞，常與 rumors 並用（spread malicious rumors and slander）。
example: Anonymous gossip pages on Instagram often become breeding grounds for malicious slander among secondary students.

def_zh: 起底（在網上非法公開他人私隱資料以作滋擾）
def_en: search for and publish private or identifying information about a particular individual on the internet, typically with malicious intent
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，香港私隱條例已將「起底」刑事化（criminalize doxxing），網絡欺凌題必背 5** 字！
example: Amending the privacy ordinance to criminalize malicious doxxing has effectively deterred online bullies.

def_zh: 網絡酸民；專在網上挑釁引戰的人（亦可作動詞）
def_en: a person who makes a deliberately offensive or provocative online post
prep_trap: 可數名詞（internet trolls 網絡酸民/鍵盤戰士），動名詞為 trolling。
example: Celebrities and teenagers alike should learn to block and ignore malicious internet trolls.

def_zh: 鍵盤戰士（躲在熒幕後肆意批評攻擊他人的人）
def_en: a person who makes abusive or aggressive posts on the internet, typically concealing their true identity
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 討論網絡文化與網絡公審（online public trials）的地道高分字！
example: Hiding behind anonymous accounts emboldens keyboard warriors to launch harsh personal attacks on others.

def_zh: 自發執法者；私刑者（如網上公審肉搜他人者）
def_en: a member of a self-appointed group of citizens who undertake law enforcement in their community without legal authority
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意四音節讀法（字尾 e 讀 /ti/），DSE 批評「網絡公審」（online vigilante justice）時的頂級詞彙！
example: Posting videos online to shame passengers on the MTR is a form of digital vigilante justice.

def_zh: 公開羞辱；網絡公審（public shaming）
def_en: the act of subjecting someone to shame, disgrace, or humiliation, especially on social media
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必考搭配：public online shaming（網絡公審）或 body shaming（身材羞辱）。
example: Public online shaming often escalates minor misunderstandings on public transport into lifelong psychological trauma.

def_zh: 羞辱；奇恥大辱；丟臉
def_en: the action of humiliating someone or the state of being humiliated
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 humiliate（當眾羞辱），校園欺凌題必備字。
example: Mocking a student's family background or appearance in class causes deep emotional humiliation.

def_zh: 極度尷尬羞愧的；無地自容的
def_en: feeling or showing strong shame or embarrassment
prep_trap: 形容詞，記敘文（Narrative / Short Story）替換 very embarrassed 的 5** 生動情緒字！
example: I felt utterly mortified when I accidentally tripped and dropped my lunch tray in the crowded canteen.

def_zh: 不好意思的；靦腆尷尬的（因做錯小事而傻笑）
def_en: showing or feeling embarrassment from shame or a lack of self-confidence
prep_trap: 形容詞，副詞為 sheepishly，常配 a sheepish grin / smile（尷尬不好意思的微笑）。
example: Realizing he had entered the wrong classroom, the Form One boy apologized with a sheepish smile.

def_zh: 慌張失措的；手忙腳亂的（因突發狀況或緊張）
def_en: agitated or confused
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫演講忘詞或口試緊張時手足無措的極佳詞彙（get flustered）。
example: Even when the projector suddenly broke down during her presentation, she did not get flustered.

def_zh: 張口結舌的；緊張得說不出話來的
def_en: too shy or embarrassed to speak
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，口語溝通與面試技巧題必備生動字（become tongue-tied）。
collocations: feel tongue-tied in front of strangers
example: Practising English with native speakers regularly helps shy students overcome the fear of becoming tongue-tied.

def_zh: 怯場（上台演講或表演前的極度緊張）
def_en: nervousness before or during an appearance before an audience
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，演講比賽、戲劇匯演或音樂節（Music Festival）文章必用！
example: Joining the Drama Club helped me conquer my stage fright and speak confidently before hundreds of schoolmates.

def_zh: （胃裏七上八下的）緊張感（have butterflies in one's stomach）
def_en: a fluttering or tremulous sensation in the stomach, caused by nervousness
prep_trap: 必考地道慣用語：have butterflies in my stomach（心裏七上八下、緊張萬分），演講辭或記敘文開頭極佳！
example: Waiting backstage for my turn in the Solo Verse Speaking competition, I had butterflies in my stomach.

def_zh: 令人高度緊張的；扣人心弦煎熬的（如等DSE放榜）
def_en: causing stress or anxiety
prep_trap: 複合形容詞（亦拼作 nerve-wracking），形容等候放榜（DSE results release）或面試過程的 5* 詞彙！
example: Waiting for the release of the HKDSE results in July is a nerve-racking experience for Form Six students.

def_zh: 令人望而生畏的；艱巨得令人卻步的
def_en: seeming difficult to deal with in anticipation; intimidating
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 difficult / scary 的高頻高分字，常配 a daunting task / prospect（艱巨的任務）。
example: Transitioning from primary to secondary school can feel like a daunting challenge for twelve-year-olds.

def_zh: 強大的；令人生畏的；極為艱巨的（對手或挑戰）
def_en: inspiring fear or respect through being impressively large, powerful, intense, or capable
prep_trap: 形容詞，既可修飾艱巨障礙（a formidable obstacle），亦可讚賞強勁對手（a formidable opponent）。
example: Although the defending champions were a formidable opponent, our debate team prepared thoroughly and won.

def_zh: 令人膽怯的；有壓迫感的
def_en: having a frightening, overawing, or threatening effect
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自動詞 intimidate（恐嚇/使膽怯）。
example: Peer tutors create a friendly, non-intimidating environment where junior students feel safe asking questions.

def_zh: 極度艱辛累人的；耗盡體力的（訓練、賽程或考試）
def_en: extremely tiring and demanding
prep_trap: 形容詞（美式單寫 l：grueling），描寫馬拉松訓練、毅行者或緊湊考試時間表的 5** 詞彙！
example: After six months of gruelling physical training, our dragon boat team won the championship trophy.

def_zh: 艱苦的；費力的；漫長艱巨的（旅程或過程）
def_en: involving or requiring strenuous effort; difficult and tiring
prep_trap: 形容詞，母音開頭配冠詞 an（an arduous journey / process）。
example: Mastering a musical instrument is a long and arduous journey that demands daily discipline.

def_zh: 費時費力的；繁重辛勞的（工序）
def_en: requiring considerable time and effort
prep_trap: 形容詞，討論人工智能（AI）或自動化科技取代繁瑣人工工序（laborious manual tasks）時極精準。
example: Spreadsheet software and AI tools can complete laborious data-entry tasks in a fraction of a second.

def_zh: 沉悶乏味的；冗長單調的
def_en: too long, slow, or dull; tiresome or monotonous
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 boring 的 DSE 必備高分字！
example: Interactive educational games turn tedious vocabulary memorization into an enjoyable classroom competition.

def_zh: 單調乏味的；千篇一律無變化的（生活、工作或語調）
def_en: dull, tedious, and repetitious; lacking in variety and interest
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 monotony（break the monotony of exam revision 打破溫習的沉悶單調）。
example: Outdoor field trips break the monotony of classroom lectures and spark students' curiosity about nature.

def_zh: 平凡日常的；世俗單調的
def_en: lacking interest or excitement; dull; of this earthly world rather than a heavenly or spiritual one
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 mundane daily chores（日常瑣碎家務）。
example: Reading fantasy novels allows busy students to temporarily escape their mundane daily routine.

def_zh: 平淡乏味的；一成不變的
def_en: lacking excitement or variety; boringly monotonous
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 a humdrum existence / life。
example: Learning a new hobby like pottery or salsa dancing adds colour to an otherwise humdrum office life.

def_zh: 平庸乏善可陳的；缺乏活力的（表現或成績）
def_en: lacking in vitality, force, or conviction; uninspired or uninspiring
prep_trap: 形容詞（美式拼作 lackluster），影評或活動檢討報告中批評表現欠佳（a lacklustre performance）的高分字。
example: Despite a huge publicity budget, the movie received negative reviews for its predictable and lacklustre plot.

def_zh: 平庸的；質素普通的（含貶義）
def_en: of only moderate quality; not very good
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意字尾拼字是 -cre，名詞為 mediocrity，餐廳評論或影評極好用。
example: The new cafe charges exorbitant prices for mediocre food and slow service.

def_zh: 不合標準的；劣質的（貨品、工程或居住環境）
def_en: below the usual or required standard
prep_trap: 形容詞，Paper 2/3 投訴信（Letter of Complaint）批評劣質產品或服務的必殺高分字！
example: I am writing to express my strong dissatisfaction with the substandard catering service provided at our banquet.

def_zh: 粗製濫造的；劣質馬虎的（工程或產品）
def_en: badly made or done
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 shoddy workmanship（手工粗糙劣質）。
example: Consumers should check online reviews carefully to avoid hiring renovation companies known for shoddy workmanship.

def_zh: 有瑕疵的；損壞失靈的（產品或零件）
def_en: imperfect or faulty
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自名詞 defect（缺陷），Paper 3 退換貨品信件必考：replace the defective item！
example: Customers are entitled to a full refund or free replacement if the purchased headphones are found to be defective.

def_zh: 有故障的；出問題的（電線或設備）
def_en: working badly or unreliably because of imperfections
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 faulty wiring（電線故障引致火警）或 faulty equipment。
example: Regular inspections of old buildings are necessary because faulty electrical wiring is a leading cause of fires.

def_zh: 發生故障；失靈（機器、訊號系統或軟件，亦可作名詞）
def_en: of a piece of equipment or machinery fail to function normally or satisfactorily
prep_trap: 不及物動詞或可數名詞，MTR 訊號故障（signal malfunction）或電腦系統死機必用字。
example: A sudden signal system malfunction caused severe delays along the railway line during morning rush hour.

def_zh: （軟件或系統的）小故障、技術失誤
def_en: a sudden, usually temporary malfunction or fault of equipment or software
prep_trap: 可數名詞，複數為 glitches，常配 a technical glitch（技術故障，如網上報名系統死機）。
example: Due to a temporary technical glitch on the ticketing website, thousands of fans could not book concert seats.

def_zh: 停電；斷網（電力或網絡中斷期間）
def_en: a period when a power supply or other service is not available
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 power outage（停電）或 internet outage（網絡中斷）。
example: Hospitals are equipped with backup generators so life-support machines keep running during a sudden power outage.

def_zh: 大停電；漆黑一片
def_en: a failure of electrical power supply
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常指整個地區的大停電（a massive power blackout）。
