example: Damage to the high-voltage cable bridge plunged tens of thousands of Yuen Long households into a blackout.

def_zh: 中斷；擾亂；混亂（交通或課堂受阻）
def_en: disturbance or problems which interrupt an event, activity, or process
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，源自動詞 disrupt，Paper 3 道歉通告常配：We apologize for any disruption caused。
example: Roadworks should be scheduled at night to minimize traffic disruption during peak commuting hours.

def_zh: 不便；麻煩（亦可作動詞：給某人帶來不便）
def_en: trouble or difficulty caused to one's personal requirements or comfort
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，Paper 3 公函及通告結尾萬用金句：We apologize for any inconvenience caused（對造成任何不便，謹此致歉）！
example: We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience caused by the temporary closure of the swimming pool.

def_zh: 麻煩事；繁瑣不便（半正式及日常實用字）
def_en: irritating inconvenience
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，複合形容詞 hassle-free（輕鬆無憂的/免卻繁瑣手續的）在宣傳小冊子極受歡迎！
example: Booking sports courts through the mobile app saves citizens the hassle of queuing in person.

def_zh: 笨重的（器材）；繁瑣累贅而緩慢的（申請程序）
def_en: large or heavy and therefore difficult to carry or use; unwieldy; slow and complicated
prep_trap: 形容詞，既可修飾沉重書包器材，亦可批評政府津貼申請手續太繁瑣（cumbersome application procedures）。
example: Simplifying cumbersome application forms will help elderly citizens apply for welfare allowances more easily.

def_zh: 龐大笨重的；難以運作管理的（機構或制度）
def_en: difficult to carry or move because of its size, shape, or weight, or too large to be managed efficiently
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Breaking a huge, unwieldy committee into smaller working groups makes decision-making much faster.

def_zh: 古老過時的；陳舊落伍的（校規或法例）
def_en: very old or old-fashioned
prep_trap: 形容詞，母音開頭配冠詞 an，DSE 議論文批評不合時宜的舊校規或法例（archaic school rules）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Many students argue that strict hair-length rules are archaic regulations that serve no educational purpose.

def_zh: 陳舊過時的；老掉牙的（設備、制度或觀念）
def_en: old-fashioned or outdated
prep_trap: 形容詞，母音開頭配冠詞 an（an antiquated system），替換 old-fashioned 的高分字。
example: Upgrading antiquated hospital computer systems with cloud technology will reduce medical record errors.

def_zh: 過時的；不再適用的（教學法或觀念）
def_en: out of fashion; no longer usable or practicable
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 outmoded teaching methods（過時的填鴨式教學法）。
example: Rote learning is an outmoded teaching method that fails to prepare students for the AI era.

def_zh: 當代的；現代的；同時代的（作名詞：同齡人）
def_en: living or occurring at the same time, OR belonging to or occurring in the present
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 modern society（in contemporary society 在當代社會）的 DSE 議論文高頻詞彙！
example: M+ is a world-class museum dedicated to showcasing twentieth- and twenty-first-century contemporary visual culture.

def_zh: 前衛的；先鋒派的（藝術、時裝或設計）
def_en: favoring or introducing experimental or unusual ideas, especially in the arts
prep_trap: 形容詞或不可數名詞，討論西九文化區藝術展覽或時裝設計時的高分字。
example: The student fashion show featured bold, avant-garde outfits crafted entirely from recycled newspapers and plastic.

def_zh: 兼收並蓄的；多元融合不同風格的
def_en: deriving ideas, style, or taste from a broad and diverse range of sources
prep_trap: 形容詞，形容香港建築、飲食或文化中西合璧、多元交融（an eclectic mix of East and West）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Sheung Wan offers tourists an eclectic mix of traditional Chinese herbal shops and trendy Western art galleries.

def_zh: 最典型的；最具代表性的；精髓的
def_en: representing the most perfect or typical example of a quality or class
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 typical 的頂級高分字：Riding the 'Ding Ding' tram is the quintessential Hong Kong experience！
example: Riding the upper deck of a historic tram is the quintessential Hong Kong experience for first-time visitors.

def_zh: 標誌性的；具代表性的（地標或人物）
def_en: relating to or of the nature of an icon; widely known and acknowledged especially for distinctive excellence
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 icon（cultural icon 文化標誌），旅遊及文化保育題必用：iconic landmarks（標誌性地標）。
example: The Clock Tower in Tsim Sha Tsui is an iconic historical landmark that must be preserved.

def_zh: 地標建築；（歷史或法律上的）重大里程碑
def_en: an object or feature of a landscape or town that is easily seen and recognized, or a major turning point
prep_trap: 可數名詞，亦可作定語：a landmark court ruling / agreement（具里程碑意義的裁決/協議）。
example: Conserving historical landmarks gives citizens a shared sense of identity and collective memory.

def_zh: 法定古蹟；紀念碑
def_en: a statue, building, or other structure erected to commemorate a famous or notable person or event
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港最高級別保護建築稱為 declared monument（法定古蹟）；形容詞 monumental 則指「意義極其重大的」。
example: Declaring the century-old market a monument saved it from being demolished for luxury flats.

def_zh: 歷史遺物；遺跡；（過時的）殘留習俗
def_en: an object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or sentimental interest
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 historical / cultural relics（歷史文物）。
example: Archaeological excavations at the construction site uncovered precious ceramic relics from the Song Dynasty.

def_zh: 文物；歷史工藝品
def_en: an object made by a human being, typically an item of cultural or historical interest
prep_trap: 可數名詞（美式拼作 artifact），香港故宮文化博物館（Hong Kong Palace Museum）文章必備字！
example: Interactive digital screens at the Palace Museum allow students to examine ancient royal artefacts up close.

def_zh: （博物館或展覽的）策展人、館長
def_en: a keeper or custodian of a museum or other collection
prep_trap: 可數名詞，動詞為 curate（策劃展覽或精選內容）。
example: The museum curator gave our history class a guided tour of the special porcelain exhibition.

def_zh: （博物館、古蹟或生態公園的）義務導賞員
def_en: a person who acts as a guide, typically on a voluntary basis, in a museum, art gallery, or heritage site
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 提議讓中學生參與古蹟或地質公園保育時，train students as volunteer docents（培訓學生做導賞員）是極佳建議！
example: Training secondary students as volunteer heritage docents deepens their knowledge of local history and boosts speaking confidence.

def_zh: 展品（作動詞：展出、表現出某特質）
def_en: an object or collection of objects on public display in an art gallery or museum
prep_trap: 注意區分：exhibit 作名詞指「單件展品」（Do not touch the exhibits），而 exhibition 指「整場展覽會」！
example: Hands-on interactive exhibits at the Science Museum make physics concepts fun for primary children.

def_zh: 紀念品珍藏（與重要歷史事件、名人或校慶相關的收藏品）
def_en: objects kept or collected because of their historical interest, especially those associated with memorable people or events
prep_trap: 複數形式集合名詞，校慶展覽（school anniversary exhibition）展示舊校服、舊校刊時必用！
example: Alumni donated old school badges, photographs, and memorabilia for our centenary history gallery.

def_zh: 檔案館；歷史文獻檔案（亦可作動詞：歸檔保存）
def_en: a collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people
prep_trap: 可數名詞（常用複數 archives），注意 ch 發 /k/ 音（讀 /ˈɑːkaɪv/）。
example: Creating a digital archive of oral history interviews preserves the memories of elderly fishermen.

def_zh: 手稿；原稿；古籍手抄本
def_en: a book, document, or piece of music written by hand rather than typed or printed
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: Visitors to the literary exhibition can view the author's original handwritten manuscripts and letters.

def_zh: 書法（藝術）
def_en: decorative handwriting or handwritten lettering
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，中國文化週（Chinese Culture Week）必提活動：Chinese calligraphy workshops。
example: Practising Chinese calligraphy teaches students patience, concentration, and appreciation for traditional aesthetics.

def_zh: 美學；審美觀；美感設計
def_en: a set of principles concerned with the nature and appreciation of beauty, especially in art
prep_trap: 名詞，形容詞為 aesthetic（具美感的/審美的，如 aesthetic value 美學價值）。
example: Preserving historic shophouses is important for both their architectural aesthetics and cultural history.

def_zh: 建築風格；建築學；建築設計
def_en: the art or practice of designing and constructing buildings, or the style of a building
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意 ch 發 /k/ 音；建築師為 architect，形容詞為 architectural。
example: Tai Kwun is a shining example of how colonial architecture can be revitalized into a vibrant arts hub.

def_zh: （建築物的）正面外牆；（虛假的）表面假象
def_en: the principal front of a building, that faces on to a street or open space, OR a deceptive outward appearance
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意中間 c 發 /s/ 音（讀 /fəˈsɑːd/）；既可指保育舊樓外牆（preserve the historic facade），亦可指社交媒體上的快樂假象（put on a happy facade）！
example: Many teenagers put on a cheerful facade on social media while hiding deep academic anxiety inside.

def_zh: 宏偉建築物；大廈；（信仰或制度）體系
def_en: a large, imposing building
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: The century-old courthouse stands as a grand edifice in the heart of the financial district.

def_zh: 有礙觀瞻之物
def_en: a thing that is very ugly, especially a building
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: Rusty abandoned cars along rural roads have become a terrible eyesore.

def_zh: 拆卸；清拆（舊建築物）
def_en: the action or process of demolishing or being demolished
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 demolish（清拆），古蹟保育與市區重建必考字！
example: Local residents launched a petition to save the historic cinema from imminent demolition.

def_zh: 清拆；夷平（建築物）；推翻（錯誤論點）
def_en: pull or knock down a building, or overwhelmingly defeat an argument
prep_trap: 及物動詞。
example: Instead of demolishing old factory buildings, the government encourages owners to convert them into art studios.

def_zh: 疏散；撤離（火警、水災或危險場所）
def_en: remove someone from a place of danger to a safer place
prep_trap: 及物或不及物動詞，名詞為 evacuation（fire evacuation drill 火警逃生演習），Paper 3 校園安全通告必考！
example: When the fire alarm rings, all students must leave their schoolbags behind and evacuate calmly to the playground.

def_zh: 滅火筒（fire extinguisher）
def_en: a portable device that discharges a jet of water, foam, gas, or other material to put out a fire
prep_trap: 可數名詞，源自動詞 extinguish（撲滅火焰 / 破滅希望）。
example: Old tenement buildings should be equipped with fire extinguishers and smoke detectors on every floor.

def_zh: 易燃的
def_en: easily set on fire
prep_trap: 形容詞，極大陷阱：inflammable 也是「易燃的」（不是不易燃！）；「不易燃/防火的」必須寫 non-flammable！
example: Campers must never leave campfires unattended near dry grass and other highly flammable vegetation.

def_zh: 可燃的；易燃燒的
def_en: able to catch fire and burn easily
prep_trap: 形容詞，內燃機汽車為 internal combustion engine vehicles（傳統燃油車）。
example: Phasing out internal combustion engine cars in favour of electric vehicles will drastically reduce roadside smog.

def_zh: 縱火罪
def_en: the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，縱火犯為 arsonist。
example: Police are investigating whether the midnight blaze in the back alley was an act of arson.

def_zh: 盜竊罪；偷竊行為
def_en: the action or crime of stealing
prep_trap: 不可數或可數名詞，常配 identity theft（身份盜竊）或 petty theft（小偷小摸）。
example: Using strong passwords and two-factor authentication protects citizens against online identity theft.

def_zh: 入屋犯法罪；爆竊
def_en: illegal entry of a building with intent to commit a crime, especially theft
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，爆竊賊人為 burglar。
example: Installing window sensors and security cameras helps deter residential burglaries during long holidays.

def_zh: 店舖盜竊；高買
def_en: the action of stealing goods from a shop while pretending to be a customer
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，青少年最常誤墮法網的罪行之一（peer-pressured shoplifting）。
example: Some teenagers commit shoplifting not out of poverty, but due to peer dares or exam stress.

def_zh: 扒竊；打荷包
def_en: the action of stealing from people's pockets or bags in crowded places
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，扒手為 pickpocket（Beware of pickpockets 小心扒手）。
example: Tourists visiting crowded night markets are reminded to zip up their backpacks to prevent pickpocketing.

def_zh: 勒索；敲詐
def_en: the practice of obtaining something, especially money, through force or threats
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞 extortionate 則常用於批評「天價/漫天索價的」（extortionate rents / ticket prices）！
example: Unscrupulous scalpers buy up concert tickets and resell them online at extortionate prices.

def_zh: 黃牛黨（炒賣門票或緊絀物資牟暴利的人）
def_en: a person who resells shares or tickets at a large or quick profit
prep_trap: 可數名詞（英式亦稱 ticket tout），香港演唱會「實名制購票」（real-name ticketing）題必考字！
example: Introducing real-name ticketing for concerts and sports matches effectively stops ticket scalpers from profiteering.

def_zh: 牟取暴利；發災難財（趁短缺哄抬物價）
def_en: the practice of making or seeking to make an excessive or unfair profit, especially illegally or in a shortage
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 profiteer。
example: Strict laws should penalize merchants who engage in profiteering by hoarding medical supplies during emergencies.

def_zh: 囤積居奇；病態囤積雜物（如長者拾荒塞滿屋）
def_en: the practice of accumulating money, food, or objects in excess
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 hoard；既可指搶購囤積（panic buying and hoarding），亦可指獨居長者屋企塞滿雜物造成火警隱患（compulsive hoarding）！
example: Social workers help elderly residents overcome compulsive hoarding habits that turn their flats into fire traps.

def_zh: 假冒的；偽造的（冒牌貨或偽鈔，亦可作名詞及動詞）
def_en: made in exact imitation of something valuable or important with the intention to deceive or defraud
prep_trap: 形容詞、名詞或動詞，香港海關打擊冒牌貨（combat counterfeit goods）及保障知識產權題必用！
example: Customs officers raided several warehouses and seized thousands of counterfeit luxury handbags and watches.

def_zh: 侵犯；侵權（尤指版權或私隱侵犯）
def_en: the action of breaking the terms of a law, agreement, etc.; violation
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，源自動詞 infringe，討論 AI 生成藝術是否侵犯版權（copyright infringement）的核心詞彙！
example: Using artists' paintings to train AI models without permission has sparked lawsuits over copyright infringement.

def_zh: 專利權（保障發明者的知識產權，亦可作動詞）
def_en: a government authority or license conferring a right or title for a set period, especially the sole right to exclude others from making, using, or selling an invention
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 apply for a patent（申請專利），創科教育與科研成果轉化題常用。
example: Strong patent protection encourages local university researchers to turn their scientific inventions into commercial products.

def_zh: 版稅；專利使用費（複數 royalties）；皇室成員
def_en: a sum of money paid to a patentee for the use of a patent or to an author or composer for each copy of a book sold or for each public performance of a work
prep_trap: 作「版稅」解時常用複數形式 royalties。
example: Streaming platforms should pay fair royalties to independent musicians and songwriters for their creative work.

def_zh: 給⋯⋯報酬；向⋯⋯支付酬勞
def_en: pay someone for services rendered or work done
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常用被動 be fairly remunerated for one's labour。
example: Frontline care workers should be fairly remunerated for their physically demanding service to the elderly.

def_zh: 微薄的薪酬；少得可憐的錢
def_en: a very small or inadequate amount of money paid to someone as an allowance or wage
prep_trap: 單數名詞，配 a pittance（work for a pittance 為微薄薪水辛勞工作），描寫基層外判清潔工或拾荒長者極具感染力！
example: Elderly cardboard collectors toil under the scorching sun all day just to earn a mere pittance.

def_zh: 辛勤勞作；苦幹（亦可作不可數名詞：辛勞）
def_en: work extremely hard or incessantly
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，替換 work hard 的文學高分動詞（toil day and night 日夜辛勞）。
example: Outdoor construction workers toil under the scorching summer sun to build our city's infrastructure.

def_zh: 苦工；枯燥繁重的苦差事
def_en: hard, menial, or dull work
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常指家務或機械式重複勞動（domestic drudgery / office drudgery）。
example: Smart home appliances such as robotic vacuum cleaners free working parents from daily domestic drudgery.

def_zh: （工作）低微繁重的；不需專門技術的
def_en: of work not requiring much skill and lacking prestige
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 menial jobs / tasks（基層體力或重複性工作）。
example: Using service robots for menial cleaning tasks allows human staff to focus on warm customer service.

def_zh: 藍領的；從事體力或技術勞動的
def_en: relating to manual work or workers, particularly in industry or construction
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，與 white-collar（白領文職的）相對。
example: Society should accord equal respect and status to skilled blue-collar technicians and white-collar office workers.

def_zh: 白領的；從事辦公室專業或文職工作的
def_en: relating to the work done or those who work in an office or other professional environment
prep_trap: 複合形容詞。
example: Generative AI is now automating many routine white-collar jobs in accounting, translation, and law.

def_zh: 自由身的；自僱接案的（亦可作動詞及副詞）
def_en: working for different companies at different times rather than being permanently employed by one company
prep_trap: 自由工作者為 freelancer（可數名詞），DSE 討論斜槓族（slashers）與零工經濟必用！
example: Many young graduates prefer working as freelancers because they value flexible hours and creative autonomy.

def_zh: 遙距辦公；在家工作（work from home 的正式寫法）
def_en: working from home, making use of the internet, email, and the telephone
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 telecommute，替換口語 WFH 的正式高分詞彙！
example: Adopting telecommuting arrangements reduces rush-hour traffic congestion and helps working parents balance family duties.

def_zh: 彈性上班時間制度
def_en: a system of working a set number of hours with the starting and finishing times chosen within agreed limits by the employee
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，家庭友善僱傭政策（family-friendly workplace policies）的具體核心建議。
example: Introducing flexitime allows employees to avoid packed morning trains and pick up their children after school.

def_zh: 休假進修期；長假（工作數年後放數月充電或進修）
def_en: a period of paid or unpaid leave granted to a university teacher or employee for study, travel, or rest
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 take a sabbatical（放一個進修或充電長假，防止職場過勞 burnout）。
example: Taking a three-month sabbatical allowed the exhausted teacher to travel, study art, and regain her passion.

def_zh: 天職；人生使命；強烈感召
def_en: a strong urge toward a particular way of life or career; a vocation
prep_trap: 單數可數名詞，常配 find one's true calling in life。
example: Volunteering at an animal shelter helped her discover her true calling as a veterinary surgeon.

def_zh: 專長；強項；拿手好戲
def_en: a thing at which someone excels
prep_trap: 單數名詞，常配 somebody's forte（某人的強項：Public speaking is her forte）。
example: While mathematics was never his forte, he excelled in creative writing and dramatic arts.

def_zh: 訣竅；特殊本領；天賦巧勁
def_en: an acquired or natural skill at performing a task
prep_trap: 單數名詞，注意字頭 k 不發音；必考搭配：have a knack for doing something（對做某事很有辦法/天分）。
example: A good tutor has a knack for explaining complicated scientific theories in simple everyday terms.

def_zh: 天賦才華；獨特品味與觸覺
def_en: a special or instinctive aptitude or ability for doing something well
prep_trap: 單數或不可數名詞，必配介詞 for（have a flair for languages / design 有語言/設計天分），推薦信極佳用字！
example: Students with a natural flair for graphic design were invited to create posters for the school musical.

def_zh: 才幹；素質；水準（人才或作品）
def_en: the quality of someone's character or the level of their ability
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（美式拼作 caliber），常配 high-calibre talent / candidates（高質素人才）。
collocations: attract international talent of high calibre
example: Offering generous research scholarships helps local universities attract students of the highest academic calibre.

def_zh: 優良背景；門第出身；（純種動物的）血統
def_en: the recorded ancestry, especially upper-class ancestry, of a person or family, or purebred animal
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，既可指市民不應盲目追求名種寵物（pedigree pets，應領養代替購買），亦可指學術背景。
example: Animal welfare groups urge citizens to adopt abandoned mongrels rather than buying expensive pedigree puppies.

def_zh: 混種狗（唐狗）
def_en: a dog of no definable type or breed
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港領養寵物題（Adopt, Don't Shop）常提 local mongrels（本地唐狗，比純種狗更健康少遺傳病）。
example: Local mongrels at animal shelters make loyal, intelligent, and healthy companions for families.

def_zh: 流浪的；走失的（貓狗，亦可作可數名詞及動詞）
def_en: of a domestic animal having no home or having wandered away from home
prep_trap: 形容詞或可數名詞，DSE 動物權益題必考：stray dogs and cats（流浪貓狗）及 trap-neuter-return (TNR) schemes。
example: Trap-neuter-return programmes are a humane way to control the population of stray cats and dogs.

def_zh: 為（動物）絕育
def_en: castrate or spay a domestic animal
prep_trap: 及物動詞，香港漁護署及愛協推行的流浪動物「捕捉、絕育、放回」計劃即 Trap-Neuter-Return (TNR)。
example: Responsible pet owners should have their cats and dogs neutered to prevent unwanted litters.

def_zh: 安樂死；人道毀滅（動物或末期病人）
def_en: the painless killing of a patient suffering from an incurable and painful disease, or putting down homeless animals
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 euthanize，既可用於倫理議題「病人安樂死」，亦可用於反對漁護署人道毀滅流浪動物！
example: Expanding animal adoption centres provides a compassionate alternative to the euthanasia of healthy stray dogs.

def_zh: 殘酷；虐待行為（尤指虐待動物或兒童）
def_en: callous indifference to or pleasure in causing pain and suffering
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必配介詞 to 或 toward：cruelty to animals（虐待動物，如香港 SPCA 即防止虐待動物協會）。
example: Imposing heavier prison sentences for cruelty to animals sends a clear message that abuse will not be tolerated.

def_zh: 人道的；仁慈的；富同情心的
def_en: having or showing compassion or benevolence
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意字尾有 e（讀 /hjuːˈmeɪn/，切勿與 human「人類的」混淆！），相反詞為 inhumane（不人道的）。
example: A civilized city must ensure the humane treatment of both domestic pets and wild animals.

def_zh: 仁慈；善心；樂善好施
def_en: the quality of being well meaning; kindness
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 benevolent。
example: Charity flag days rely on the benevolence and generosity of ordinary citizens passing by.

def_zh: 同情心；慈悲；悲憫之情
def_en: sympathetic pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必配介詞 for（show compassion for the needy），形容詞為 compassionate。
example: Visiting elderly homes during festivals nurtures genuine compassion for the weak among young students.

def_zh: 同理心；感同身受的能力
def_en: the ability to understand and share the feelings of another
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必配介詞 for 或 with（develop empathy for others），比 sympathy（單純可憐同情）層次更高！
example: Role-play activities in moral education classes help students develop deep empathy for people with disabilities.

def_zh: 同情；慰問；支持贊同
def_en: feelings of pity and sorrow for someone else's misfortune
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 express sympathy for the victims。
example: Citizens donated generously out of sympathy for the families who lost their homes in the flood.

def_zh: 哀悼；弔唁；慰問（對喪親家屬）
def_en: an expression of sympathy, especially on the occasion of adeath
prep_trap: 常用複數形式 condolences，必配 offer / express our deepest condolences to the bereaved family。
example: The Principal sent a letter expressing the school's deepest condolences to the bereaved family.

def_zh: 對⋯⋯表示同情；互相安慰（同病相憐）
def_en: express or feel sympathy or pity; sympathize
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，配介詞 with（commiserate with somebody over a loss）。
example: After losing the debate final, the teammates gathered at a cafe to commiserate with each other.

def_zh: 祝賀；道賀
def_en: give someone one's good wishes when something special or pleasant has happened to them
prep_trap: DSE 必考介詞伏位：congratulate somebody ON (doing) something（切勿用 for！）名詞則必用複數 congratulations。
example: I would like to warmly congratulate our debate team on winning the inter-school championship.

def_zh: 讚美；稱讚；致意（亦可作動詞）
def_en: a polite expression of praise or admiration
prep_trap: 可數名詞或動詞，注意中間是 i（compliment somebody on something），切勿與 complement（互補，中間是 e）混淆！
example: Giving sincere compliments to classmates boosts their self-esteem and creates a warm classroom atmosphere.

def_zh: 補充；與⋯⋯相輔相成（亦可作名詞）
def_en: add to something in a way that enhances or improves it; make perfect
prep_trap: 及物動詞，注意中間是 e（源自 complete），議論文極佳句型：E-learning should complement, rather than replace, classroom teaching！
example: Extracurricular activities should complement academic studies rather than overwhelming students' schedules.

def_zh: 奉承；討好；使感到榮幸（be flattered）
def_en: lavish insincere praise and compliments upon someone, especially to further one's own interests
prep_trap: 及物動詞，名詞為 flattery（甜言蜜語/奉承，不可數）。
example: Online romance scammers often use sweet flattery to win the trust of lonely victims.

def_zh: 哄騙；用甜言蜜語勸誘（某人做某事）
def_en: persuade someone to do something by sustained coaxing or flattery
prep_trap: 及物動詞，必配 cajole somebody into doing something。
example: Parents often have to coax and cajole young children into putting down their tablets before bedtime.

def_zh: 耐心哄勸；善言誘勸
def_en: gently and persistently persuade someone to do something
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常配 coax somebody into doing something 或 coax a shy child out of their shell。
collocations: coax a shy student to speak
example: Patient drama teachers know how to gently coax shy students into performing on stage.

def_zh: 強迫；脅迫（用威嚇手段逼人就範）
def_en: persuade an unwilling person to do something by using force or threats
prep_trap: 及物動詞，名詞為 coercion（高壓脅迫），討論不良銷售手法強迫長者簽單（coerce customers into signing contracts）必用！
example: Salespeople at unscrupulous fitness centres sometimes coerce young customers into signing expensive membership contracts.

def_zh: 恐嚇；威脅；令人生畏怯場
def_en: frighten or overawe someone, especially in order to make them do what one wants
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常配 intimidate somebody into silence（恐嚇某人使其不敢作聲）。
example: School bullies often try to intimidate weaker classmates into handing over their pocket money.

def_zh: 欺凌威嚇；咄咄逼人地斥責迫使就範
def_en: intimidate someone, typically into doing something, with stern or abusive words
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常配 browbeat somebody into doing something。
example: Consumers should stand firm and never allow aggressive salespeople to browbeat them into buying unnecessary packages.

def_zh: 勒索；要脅（尤指裸聊勒索或情感勒索，亦可作動詞）
def_en: the action, treated as a criminal offense, of demanding payment or another benefit from someone in return for not revealing compromising information
prep_trap: 不可數名詞或及物動詞，DSE 必考兩個組合：online blackmail scams（網上勒索騙案）及 emotional blackmail（情緒勒索）！
example: Police warn teenagers never to send private photos to strangers online to avoid falling victim to blackmail.

def_zh: 騙局；詐騙案（亦可作動詞）
def_en: a dishonest scheme; a fraud
prep_trap: 可數名詞，騙徒為 scammer（online / phone scammers），香港近年最高頻社會議題詞彙！
example: Anti-deception hotlines help citizens verify suspicious calls before they transfer money into a phone scam.

def_zh: 詐騙；騙取（金錢，亦可作可數名詞：騙局）
def_en: use deception to deprive someone of money or possessions
prep_trap: 及物動詞，必考結構：swindle somebody out of their life savings（騙走某人的畢生積蓄）！騙徒為 swindler。
collocations: swindle elderly victims out of savings
example: Ruthless phone swindlers impersonated officials and swindled the retired couple out of their life savings.

def_zh: 欺詐；騙取（政府津貼、保險或長者金錢）
def_en: illegally obtain money from someone by deception
prep_trap: 及物動詞，源自名詞 fraud，常配 defraud somebody of money。
example: Clinics that submit false medical voucher claims to defraud the government face criminal prosecution.

def_zh: 惡作劇騙局；假消息（如炸彈嚇詐或網上假新聞）
def_en: a humorous or malicious deception
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 internet hoax（網絡假消息騙局）或 bomb hoax（虛報炸彈惡作劇）。
example: Fact-checking websites quickly exposed the viral health rumour as a complete internet hoax.

def_zh: 謠言；傳聞
def_en: a currently circulating story or report of uncertain or doubtful truth
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞（美式拼作 rumor），必背動詞搭配：spread / dispel rumours（散播 / 澄清謠言）。
example: Authorities held an urgent press conference to dispel unfounded rumours that triggered panic buying.

def_zh: 虛假資訊（蓄意捏造以誤導公眾的假新聞）
def_en: false information which is intended to mislead, especially propaganda issued by an organization
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意與 misinformation（無心誤傳的錯誤資訊）相比，disinformation 強調「惡意蓄意捏造」！
example: Media literacy lessons teach students how to spot malicious disinformation generated by fake social media accounts.

def_zh: 錯誤資訊；誤傳的消息
def_en: false or inaccurate information, especially that which is deliberately intended to deceive or shared by mistake
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s，健康與網絡議題常配 medical misinformation online。
example: Relying on unverified medical misinformation online can delay proper hospital treatment for serious illnesses.

def_zh: 煽情主義；誇大渲染作風（傳媒或YouTuber為博取點擊）
def_en: the use of exciting or shocking stories or language at the expense of accuracy, in order to provoke public interest
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 sensationalist（譁眾取寵的），批評八卦傳媒或「標題黨」必備 5** 詞彙！
example: Responsible journalism should prioritize factual accuracy rather than resorting to cheap sensationalism for clicks.

def_zh: 標題黨；誘餌式標題（吸引網民點擊的誇大標題）
def_en: content on the internet whose main purpose is to attract attention and encourage visitors to click on a link
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 討論網絡媒體質素下降時極貼地又高分的專業字！
example: Content creators often use exaggerated clickbait titles to boost advertising revenue on video platforms.

def_zh: 狗仔隊（追拍名人私生活的攝影記者）
def_en: independent photographers who take pictures of high-profile people, typically while they go about their daily life
prep_trap: 複數名詞，討論名人私隱權（celebrities' right to privacy）與傳媒操守時必考！
example: Strict privacy laws are needed to stop intrusive paparazzi from stalking celebrities' young children.

def_zh: 八卦小報；通俗報章（常報導名人緋聞與聳動新聞）
def_en: a newspaper having pages half the size of those of a standard broadsheet, typically popular in style and dominated by sensational stories
prep_trap: 可數名詞，與嚴肅報章 broadsheet 相對，常作定語 tabloid journalism（八卦小報式新聞）。
example: Unlike serious broadsheets, gossip tabloids focus heavily on celebrity scandals rather than global affairs.

def_zh: 嚴肅大報（報導政經、社評與深度新聞的報紙）
def_en: a newspaper with a large format, regarded as more serious and less sensationalist than tabloids
prep_trap: 可數名詞，閱讀英文大報社評（reading broadsheet editorials）是提升 DSE 寫作的最佳建議。
example: Reading editorials in reputable English broadsheets helps senior secondary students build advanced vocabulary.

def_zh: 社論；社評（報章代表編輯部立場的評論文章）
def_en: a newspaper article written by or on behalf of an editor that gives an opinion on a topical issue
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意與 Letter to the Editor（讀者來函）區分清楚。
example: In yesterday's editorial, your newspaper rightly highlighted the urgent need to support elderly carers.

def_zh: 專欄作家
def_en: a journalist contributing regularly to a newspaper or magazine
prep_trap: 可數名詞，源自專欄 column（注意 n 發音，而 column 單獨讀時 n 不發音）。
example: As an advice columnist for the school magazine, I answer fellow students' questions about friendship and stress.

def_zh: 特派記者；通訊記者
def_en: a person employed to report for a newspaper or broadcasting organization, typically on a particular subject or from a particular country
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意字尾是 -ent，與不可數名詞 correspondence（書信來往）同字根。
example: Foreign correspondents risk their lives in conflict zones to bring accurate news to the world.

def_zh: 新聞業；新聞工作；新聞學
def_en: the activity or profession of writing for newspapers, magazines, or news websites
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，新聞工作者/記者為 journalist，調查報導為 investigative journalism。
example: Investigative journalism plays a vital role in exposing corporate corruption and protecting public interest.

def_zh: 政治或商業宣傳（常指帶偏見或誤導性的洗腦宣傳）
def_en: information, especially of a biased or misleading nature, used to promote or publicize a particular political cause or point of view
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s。
example: Critical thinking skills enable young people to distinguish objective facts from biased propaganda.

def_zh: 灌輸（不許質疑地強行灌輸單一思想）
def_en: the process of teaching a person or group to accept a set of beliefs uncritically
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 indoctrinate，討論「真正的教育是啟發思考而非單向灌輸」（education vs indoctrination）時的 5** 字！
example: True education encourages independent inquiry and open debate rather than uncritical indoctrination.

def_zh: 啟迪；啟發；開明豁達
def_en: the action of enlightening or the state of being enlightened
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自動詞 enlighten，形容詞為 enlightened（開明的，如 enlightened parents 開明的父母）。
example: Reading biographies of great thinkers is a source of both inspiration and intellectual enlightenment.

def_zh: 陶冶性情；道德或知識上的教化提升
def_en: the instruction or improvement of a person morally or intellectually
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自動詞 edify（陶冶/啟迪）。
example: Good theatre productions provide audiences with both enjoyable entertainment and moral edification.

def_zh: 博學；淵博學識
def_en: the quality of having or showing great knowledge or learning; scholarship
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 erudite。
example: The professor's public lectures are admired for their humour, clarity, and deep erudition.

def_zh: 識字的；具某領域素養的（如 computer-literate 懂電腦的）
def_en: able to read and write, OR having knowledge or competence in a specified area
prep_trap: 形容詞，相反詞為 illiterate（文盲的）；DSE 常作複合形容詞：computer-literate / media-literate / financially literate！
example: Schools must train students to become financially literate before they apply for their first credit card.

def_zh: 文盲的；不識字的；對某事物一竅不通的（如電腦盲）
def_en: unable to read or write
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 illiteracy（文盲問題）；討論長者不懂用智能手機時可用 digitally illiterate。
example: Community centres run smartphone classes to help digitally illiterate seniors use hospital booking apps.

def_zh: 算術能力；基本數學運算素養
def_en: the ability to understand and work with numbers
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常與 literacy（讀寫能力）並稱為基礎教育兩大支柱：literacy and numeracy。
example: Board games involving counting and budgeting are a fun way to build children's numeracy skills.

def_zh: 雙語的（尤指中英雙語兼擅的）
def_en: speaking two languages fluently
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 bilingualism，香港語文政策「兩文三語」即 biliterate and trilingual！
example: Hong Kong's strong bilingual proficiency in Chinese and English remains a vital competitive advantage.

def_zh: 三語的（香港指粵語、英語及普通話）
def_en: speaking three languages fluently
prep_trap: 形容詞，香港教育目標必背官方詞組：biliterate and trilingual（兩文三語）！
example: Language immersion camps help nurture students into confident biliterate and trilingual communicators.

def_zh: 多語言的；通曉多種外語的
def_en: in or using several languages
prep_trap: 形容詞，旅遊業及國際大都會題常用：multilingual signage / tour guides。
example: Installing multilingual signage at tourist attractions makes visitors from Southeast Asia and the Middle East feel welcome.

def_zh: 方言；母語；日常白話口語（如廣東話口語）
def_en: the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region
prep_trap: 單數名詞或形容詞，討論保育廣東話俚語文化或教學語言（mother-tongue vs English medium）時的高分字。
example: Cantopop lyrics and local films capture the lively humour of Hong Kong's everyday vernacular.

def_zh: 方言（如客家話、圍頭話、潮州話）
def_en: a particular form of a language which is peculiar to a specific region or social group
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港非物質文化遺產題常提保存圍村傳統方言（preserve indigenous dialects like Hakka and Waitau）。
example: Recording folk songs sung by elderly villagers helps preserve endangered local dialects such as Hakka.

def_zh: 俚語；潮語（如網絡潮語 internet slang）
def_en: a type of language that consists of words and phrases that are regarded as very informal, are more common in speech than writing
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s（切勿寫 slangs！應寫 slang words / expressions），DSE 討論「網絡潮語會否破壞學生書面語能力」必考！
collocations: avoid using slang in formal writing
example: While using internet slang in text messages is fun, students must avoid it in formal essays.

def_zh: 專業術語；行話（令外行人難以明白的字眼）
def_en: special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s！Paper 3 向公眾撰寫健康或科技小冊子時，常要求 avoid technical/medical jargon。
example: Doctors should explain diagnoses in plain language rather than confusing patients with complicated medical jargon.

def_zh: 口語的；日常會話式的（不適合正式公函）
def_en: of language used in ordinary or familiar conversation; not formal or literary
prep_trap: 形容詞，Paper 2/3 評分標準（Tone & Register）常提醒考生正式書信切勿使用 colloquial expressions。
example: Formal letters to the editor should maintain an objective tone and avoid overly colloquial expressions.

def_zh: 語域（按場合與對象選用的正式或非正式語氣）；登記冊
def_en: a variety of a language or a level of usage, as determined by degree of formality and choice of vocabulary
prep_trap: 除了作動詞「報名登記」外，作名詞指寫作的「語氣正式程度」（adopt an appropriate formal register）。
example: Using a polite and formal register is essential when writing a funding proposal to the principal.

def_zh: （書信開頭的）稱呼語（如 Dear Sir/Madam）
def_en: a standard formula of words used in a letter to address the person being written to
prep_trap: 可數名詞，Paper 3 格式必知：Dear Sir/Madam 要配 Yours faithfully；Dear Mr Chan 要配 Yours sincerely。
example: Always check that your closing complimentary close matches the opening salutation of your business letter.

def_zh: 收件人；收信人（與寄件人 sender 相對）
def_en: the person to whom something, typically a letter or parcel, is addressed
prep_trap: 可數名詞，字尾 -ee 表被動接受者（如 interviewee 受訪者、employee 僱員）。
collocations: return to sender if addressee is unknown
example: Formal letters should clearly state the name, title, and organization of the addressee at the top.

def_zh: 領受者；獲獎者；受助人；收件人
def_en: a person or thing that receives or is awarded something
prep_trap: 可數名詞，Paper 2/3 必背高頻字：scholarship recipients（獎學金得主）或 CSSA recipients（綜援受助人）！
example: Past scholarship recipients were invited to share their university study experiences with junior schoolmates.

def_zh: 獲提名者；候選人（獎項或職位）
def_en: a person who is nominated for an office, position, or award
prep_trap: 可數名詞，動詞為 nominate（提名），名詞為 nomination（提名）。
example: All shortlisted nominees for the Student of the Year Award demonstrated outstanding commitment to community service.

def_zh: 把⋯⋯列入最後入圍名單（亦可作可數名詞：入圍名單）
def_en: put someone or something on a shortlist of selected candidates from which a final choice is made
prep_trap: 及物動詞或可數名詞，Paper 3 篩選場地、供應商或應徵者必考：We have shortlisted three candidates/venues！
example: After reviewing ten applications, the committee shortlisted three suitable campsites for the leadership camp.

def_zh: 審查；嚴格審核（申請人背景、資格或開支提案）
def_en: make a careful and critical examination of something, especially a candidate or proposal
prep_trap: 及物動詞（過去式及分詞雙寫 t：vetted，動名詞為 vetting），切勿只當作「獸醫（veterinarian）」解！
example: All articles written by student reporters are carefully vetted by our teacher advisor before publication.

def_zh: 獸醫（簡稱 vet）
def_en: a person qualified to treat diseased or injured animals; a veterinary surgeon
prep_trap: 可數名詞（英式亦稱 veterinary surgeon），討論香港城大設立獸醫學院及寵物醫療費用昂貴時必用。
example: Before adopting a pet, families must consider whether they can afford expensive veterinarian bills.

def_zh: 兒科醫生
def_en: a medical practitioner specializing in children and their diseases
prep_trap: 可數名詞（英式拼作 paediatrician）。
example: Pediatricians advise parents not to give smartphones to toddlers under two years of age.

def_zh: 老人醫學的；高齡長者護理的
def_en: relating to old people, especially with regard to their healthcare
prep_trap: 形容詞，香港人口老化與公營醫療題 5** 專業字：expand geriatric care services（擴展老人科醫療護理服務）。
example: With our rapidly ageing population, public hospitals must allocate more resources to geriatric medicine.

def_zh: 骨科的；矯形的（如護脊書包或矯形鞋墊）
def_en: relating to the branch of medicine dealing with the correction of deformities of bones or muscles
prep_trap: 形容詞（美式拼作 orthopedic），小學書包過重（heavy schoolbags）傷脊椎題可用 orthopaedic schoolbags。
example: Using e-textbooks on lightweight tablets spares primary students from carrying heavy bags that cause orthopaedic problems.

def_zh: 物理治療
def_en: the treatment of disease, injury, or deformity by physical methods such as massage, heat treatment, and exercise
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，物理治療師為 physiotherapist（香港大學聯招 JUPAS 最熱門學科之一）。
example: Regular physiotherapy sessions helped the injured basketball captain regain full mobility in his knee.

def_zh: 針灸（中醫傳統療法）
def_en: a system of integrative medicine that involves pricking the skin or tissues with needles, used to alleviate pain
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，香港成立首間中醫醫院（Chinese Medicine Hospital）及中西醫結合治療題必備字！
example: Combining Western physiotherapy with traditional Chinese acupuncture speeds up stroke patients' recovery.

def_zh: 草藥的；中草藥的（如涼茶 herbal tea）
def_en: relating to or made from herbs, especially those used in cooking and medicine
prep_trap: 形容詞，香港地道文化與中醫題必背：Chinese herbal medicine（中藥）及 Cantonese herbal tea（廣東涼茶）！
example: Century-old Cantonese herbal tea shops are a cherished part of Hong Kong's intangible cultural heritage.

def_zh: 診斷（醫學診斷結果）
def_en: the identification of the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，複數為 diagnoses（讀 /siːz/），動詞為 diagnose（be diagnosed with cancer/ADHD）。
example: Early diagnosis and timely treatment significantly increase the recovery rate for cancer patients.

def_zh: 預後（醫生對病情發展及康復機會的預測）
def_en: the likely course of a disease or ailment
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意與 diagnosis（診斷是什麼病）區分，prognosis 指「病程發展預測」。
example: With early surgery and rehabilitation, the doctor gave the injured athlete a very favourable prognosis.

def_zh: 慢性的（疾病）；長期的；積習難改的（社會問題）
def_en: of an illness persisting for a long time or constantly recurring, OR of a problem long-lasting and difficult to eradicate
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意 ch 發 /k/ 音，與 acute（急性的）相對；必考搭配：chronic illnesses（長期病患）或 chronic land shortage（長期土地短缺）！
example: Community health centres help elderly patients manage chronic illnesses such as diabetes and high blood pressure.

def_zh: 急性的（疾病）；嚴重的（短缺）；敏銳的
def_en: present or experienced to a severe or intense degree
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 必背高分搭配：an acute shortage of nurses/land（護士/土地嚴重短缺）！
example: Public hospitals are facing an acute shortage of doctors and nurses during the winter flu surge.

def_zh: 末期的；不治的（疾病）；（作名詞：客運大樓、電腦終端機）
def_en: of a disease predicted to lead to death, especially slowly; incurable
prep_trap: 形容詞，副詞為 terminally（terminally ill patients 末期病人），作名詞指機場客運大樓（airport terminal）。
example: Hospice services provide compassionate care and pain relief for terminally ill patients and their families.

def_zh: 良性的（腫瘤，與惡性 malignant 相對）；溫和無害的
def_en: of a disease not harmful in effect: in particular, of a tumor not malignant
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意中間 g 不發音（讀 /bɪˈnaɪn/）。
example: To the family's immense relief, the biopsy confirmed that the tumour was completely benign.

def_zh: 惡性的（致命腫瘤）；惡毒有害的
def_en: very virulent or infectious; tending to invade normal tissue and spread
prep_trap: 形容詞，與 benign 相反。
example: Regular cancer screenings can detect malignant cells early before they spread to other organs.

def_zh: 遺傳的；世代相傳的
def_en: conferred by or based on inheritance; passed from parents to offspring genetically
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 hereditary diseases（遺傳病）。
example: Genetic testing allows couples to check whether they carry genes for rare hereditary diseases.

def_zh: 先天性的（出生時即有的疾病或缺陷）
def_en: of a disease or physical abnormality present from birth
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 congenital heart disease（先天性心臟病）。
example: Charities raise funds to sponsor life-saving heart surgeries for children born with congenital heart defects.

def_zh: 免疫力
def_en: resistance to infection
prep_trap: 不可數名詞。
example: Getting enough sleep and eating fresh fruit helps boost children's natural immunity.

def_zh: 易受感染性；易受影響的脆弱程度
def_en: the state or fact of being likely or liable to be influenced or harmed by a particular thing
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自形容詞 susceptible（必配介詞 to：susceptibility to flu / peer pressure）。
example: Chronic stress weakens the immune system and increases our susceptibility to viral infections.

def_zh: 安慰劑
def_en: harmless pill
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: The placebo effect shows how strongly our mind influences physical recovery.

def_zh: 非處方的（毋須醫生紙可在藥房直接購買的成藥）
def_en: of a medicinal drug sold legally without a doctor's prescription
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，簡稱 OTC，常配 over-the-counter medicine / painkillers。
example: Pharmacists in community pharmacies can advise citizens on choosing safe over-the-counter remedies for mild colds.

def_zh: 藥劑師
def_en: a person who is professionally qualified to prepare and dispense medicinal drugs
prep_trap: 可數名詞，藥房為 pharmacy，香港基層醫療（primary healthcare）常提賦權社區藥劑師（empower community pharmacists）。
example: Consulting a community pharmacist for minor ailments can ease the workload of public hospital doctors.

def_zh: 配藥處；藥房（醫院或診所內的取藥處）
def_en: a room where medicines are prepared and provided
prep_trap: 可數名詞，源自動詞 dispense（配發藥物）。
example: Smart automated drug-dispensing systems shorten patient waiting times at public hospital dispensaries.

def_zh: （藥物的）劑量、服量
def_en: the size or frequency of a dose of a medicine or drug
prep_trap: 可數名詞，源自 dose（一劑藥），Paper 3 醫療或健康指引常考 check the recommended dosage。
example: Patients must read medicine labels carefully and never exceed the recommended daily dosage.

def_zh: （藥物的）副作用；（政策的）負面連帶影響
def_en: a secondary, typically undesirable effect of a drug or medical treatment, or unintended policy consequence
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常用複數 side effects（adverse side effects 不良副作用）。
collocations: cause drowsiness as a side effect
example: Diet pills bought from unverified online shops may cause dangerous side effects such as heart failure.

def_zh: 反感的；不願意的；規避的（常配 risk-averse）
def_en: having a strong dislike of or opposition to something
prep_trap: 形容詞，只作表語，必配介詞 to（be averse to change / risk-averse 規避風險的），切勿與 adverse 混淆！
collocations: not averse to trying new ideas
example: An overly risk-averse mentality discourages Hong Kong students from starting their own tech companies.

def_zh: 厭惡；強烈抗拒感
def_en: a strong dislike or disinclination
prep_trap: 單數名詞，必配介詞 to（develop an aversion to reading 對閱讀產生抗拒感）。
example: Forcing young children to write tedious book reports after every story can create a lifelong aversion to reading.

def_zh: 冷漠；漠不關心（尤指對公共事務或他人苦難無動於衷）
def_en: lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 apathetic（冷漠的），DSE 討論都市人冷漠或青年對社區事務無感（civic apathy）必用！
example: Widespread public apathy toward waste separation remains the biggest obstacle to reducing landfill pressure.

def_zh: 漫不經心的；滿不在乎的；若無其事的
def_en: of a person or manner feeling or appearing casually calm and relaxed; not displaying anxiety, interest, or enthusiasm
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 nonchalance。
example: Adopting a nonchalant attitude toward group project deadlines is unfair to hardworking teammates.

def_zh: 自滿的；掉以輕心的；故步自封的
def_en: showing smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 complacency（自滿，不可數），DSE 討論香港面對周邊城市競爭絕不能自滿（cannot afford to be complacent）的 5** 字！
example: Facing fierce competition from neighbouring cities, Hong Kong cannot afford to become complacent.

def_zh: 自滿；沾沾自喜；掉以輕心
def_en: a feeling of smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 there is no room for complacency（絕無自滿鬆懈的空間）。
example: Even when flu cases drop in summer, health authorities warn that there is no room for complacency.

def_zh: 保持警覺的；時刻提防的（防騙或防疫）
def_en: keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 vigilance，DSE 防騙、網絡安全及公共衛生題結尾萬用呼籲：stay vigilant against scams！
example: Citizens must remain constantly vigilant against suspicious phone calls claiming to be from bank staff.

def_zh: 提防的；戒心謹慎的
def_en: feeling or showing caution about possible dangers or problems
prep_trap: 形容詞，必考介詞：be wary of something（對網上陌生人或高回報投資保持戒心），切勿與 weary（疲倦的）混淆！
example: Jobseekers should be wary of online recruitment advertisements that promise high pay for no experience.

def_zh: 疲憊不堪的；厭倦的（亦可作動詞：使疲倦）
def_en: feeling or showing tiredness, especially as a result of excessive exertion or lack of sleep
prep_trap: 形容詞，發音為 /ˈwɪəri/（與 ear 同音），配介詞 of 指「對某事感到厭倦」（grow weary of endless exams）。
example: Soft lighting and classical music in subway stations can soothe weary commuters returning home at night.

def_zh: 筋疲力盡的；（資源）耗盡的
def_en: drained of one's physical or mental resources; very tired
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 exhaustion（heat exhaustion 熱衰竭 / mental exhaustion 精神透支）。
example: After working twelve-hour shifts in the hospital ward, the nurses felt physically and mentally exhausted.

def_zh: 精力耗盡的；被掏空的（情緒或體力）
def_en: very tired; completely exhausted of energy or emotion
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 emotionally / mentally drained（心力交瘁）。
example: Constant comparison with peers on social media leaves many teenagers feeling emotionally drained.

def_zh: 負荷過重的；不堪重負的（公營醫療系統或學生身心）
def_en: make excessive demands on a person's strength or an institution's resources
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 形容香港公營醫院（our overtaxed public healthcare system）極為地道精準！
example: Encouraging citizens with mild colds to visit private doctors relieves our overtaxed public hospital system.

def_zh: 負擔過重的（功課、工作或基建）
def_en: load someone or something with too many things to do or deal with
basic_word: weighed down with too much work
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 overburdened with homework / administrative duties。
example: Reducing unnecessary administrative paperwork allows overburdened teachers to spend more time caring for students.

def_zh: 應接不暇的；被大量（投訴、查詢或洪水）淹沒的
def_en: overwhelmed with things or people to be dealt with, or flooded with water
prep_trap: 分詞形容詞，必配介詞 with：be inundated with complaints / enquiries / applications，Paper 3 公函極好用！
example: Following the concert cancellation announcement, our customer hotline was inundated with refund enquiries.

def_zh: 忙得不可開交的；被（功課或工作）淹沒的
def_en: overwhelmed with an excessive amount of something; flooded
prep_trap: 分詞形容詞，配介詞 with（be swamped with assignments and revision）。
example: During May and June, university students are often swamped with final-year projects and examination revision.

def_zh: 工作堆積如山的；忙得喘不過氣的
def_en: overwhelmed with a large quantity of work or other demands
prep_trap: 地道慣用片語，配介詞 with（be snowed under with schoolwork），非正式書信（Informal Email/Letter）向朋友訴苦必用！
example: Sorry for my late reply, as I have been completely snowed under with SBA projects all week.

def_zh: 繁忙緊湊的；忙亂的（日程或都市生活）
def_en: full of incessant or frantic activity
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 描寫香港人生活節奏急促必背：lead a hectic lifestyle / have a hectic schedule！
example: Even with a hectic study schedule, Form Six students should set aside thirty minutes daily for exercise.

def_zh: 焦急萬分的；忙亂緊張的；手忙腳亂的
def_en: wild or distraught with fear, anxiety, or other emotion; conducted in a hurried, excited, and disorganized way
prep_trap: 形容詞，副詞為 frantically（焦急忙亂地）。
example: Last-minute cramming at a frantic pace the night before an exam is far less effective than steady revision.

def_zh: 狂亂快節奏的；極度忙碌緊張的（都市步調）
def_en: fast and energetic in a rather wild and uncontrolled way
prep_trap: 形容詞，比 hectic 更具文采，常配 the frenetic pace of city life。
example: Country parks offer urbanites a peaceful sanctuary away from the frenetic pace of city life.

def_zh: 快節奏的；步調急促的（城市、工作或電影情節）
def_en: moving or developing very quickly
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，注意 paced 有 d，描寫香港社會或動作片必備字。
example: Living in a fast-paced city like Hong Kong makes stress management skills essential for everyone.

def_zh: 悠閒的；從容不迫的（注意：是形容詞而非只有副詞！）
def_en: acting or done at leisure; unhurried or relaxed
prep_trap: 極重要文法提示：雖然字尾是 -ly，但 leisurely 是形容詞（a leisurely stroll 悠閒漫步 / a leisurely pace）！
example: On Sunday mornings, my grandparents enjoy dim sum and read the newspaper at a leisurely pace.

def_zh: 不慌不忙的；從容悠閒的
def_en: moving, acting, or taking place without haste or urgency
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫離島（如長洲、南丫島）慢活步調時極佳。
example: Lamma Island attracts visitors who appreciate its car-free paths and unhurried village lifestyle.

def_zh: 田園詩般的；幽美寧靜得如世外桃源的
def_en: like an idyll; extremely happy, peaceful, or picturesque
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意雙寫 l，母音開頭配冠詞 an（an idyllic rural village），生態旅遊文章滿分描寫字！
example: Camping at an idyllic beach in Sai Kung under a starry sky was the highlight of our summer holiday.

def_zh: 原始未受污染的；潔淨無瑕的（自然生態或沙灘）
def_en: in its original condition; unspoiled; clean and fresh as if new
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 環保題保護天然沙灘與郊野公園的 5** 詞彙：preserve pristine beaches and woodlands！
collocations: keep country parks in pristine condition
example: Careless campers who leave barbecue litter behind ruin the beauty of our pristine beaches.

def_zh: 未受破壞的；保持自然原貌的
def_en: of a place not spoiled, in particular not made less beautiful by development
prep_trap: 形容詞（英式亦拼作 unspoilt），常配 unspoiled natural beauty。
example: Many hikers oppose building cable cars in country parks to protect the unspoiled natural scenery.

def_zh: 翠綠的；草木蔥蘢的（山巒或草地）
def_en: of countryside green with grass or other rich vegetation
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫香港綠意盎然的郊野山徑（verdant hillsides）的優美高分字。
example: Despite its dense skyscrapers, Hong Kong is blessed with verdant hillsides just minutes away from the city.

def_zh: 茂盛的；鬱鬱蔥蔥的（植物或森林）
def_en: of vegetation growing luxuriantly
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 lush greenery / lush vegetation（茂密綠植）。
example: Vertical gardens on building exteriors bring lush greenery into grey concrete neighbourhoods.

def_zh: 乾旱貧瘠的（氣候或土地）；枯燥乏味的
def_en: of land or a climate having little or no rain; too dry or barren to support vegetation
prep_trap: 形容詞，與 lush 相反，討論荒漠化（desertification）時必用。
collocations: turn fertile soil into arid land
example: Overgrazing and climate change are turning once-fertile farmland into arid desert.

def_zh: 荒蕪的；寸草不生的（山頭或土地）
def_en: of land too poor to produce much or any vegetation
prep_trap: 形容詞，十九世紀初香港曾被形容為 a barren rock（荒蕪的石島），植林題亦常指 barren hillsides（光禿荒山）。
collocations: transform a barren rock into a metropolis
example: Decades of afforestation have transformed once-barren hillsides into shady woodlands.

def_zh: 肥沃的（土壤）；富創造力的（頭腦或創科環境）
def_en: of soil or land producing or capable of producing abundant vegetation or crops
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 fertility（土壤肥力，或人口生育率 fertility rate！），既可指肥沃農田，亦可指創科溫床（fertile ground for innovation）。
example: Hong Kong's declining fertility rate has worsened the problem of an ageing workforce.

def_zh: 出生率（亦分寫作 birth rate）
def_en: the number of live births per thousand of population per year
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港人口政策（現金生育獎勵 baby bonus）必考：boost the plunging birthrate！
example: High housing costs and long working hours are the main reasons behind Hong Kong's record-low birthrate.

def_zh: 人口結構的（作名詞：特定年齡消費群體）
def_en: relating to the structure of populations
prep_trap: 形容詞或可數名詞，複數名詞 demographics 指人口統計特徵，DSE 人口老化題 5** 詞組：demographic shift（人口結構轉變）！
example: A rapid demographic shift toward an ageing society requires long-term planning in healthcare and pensions.

def_zh: 勞動力；全體員工（不可數或單數集合名詞）
def_en: the people engaged in or available for work, either in a country or area or in a particular company or industry
prep_trap: 單數名詞（the local workforce），切勿加 s！香港經濟與輸入外勞題必提：a shrinking workforce（萎縮的勞動人口）。
example: Providing subsidized after-school care enables more mothers to re-enter the local workforce.

def_zh: 人力；人手（不可數名詞）
def_en: the number of people working or available for work or service
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s！香港醫護、建造業及安老院輸入外勞題核心字：alleviate the manpower shortage（紓緩人手短缺）。
example: Importing trained care workers helps alleviate the acute manpower shortage in elderly homes.

def_zh: 人手不足的（醫院、學校或餐廳）
def_en: having too few staff allocated to a task or organization
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意字尾有 ed，投訴信或醫療評論中替換 not enough workers 的地道高分字！
example: Frontline nurses in severely understaffed public hospital wards face immense daily pressure.

def_zh: 工作過度的；操勞過度的
def_en: exhausted by too much work
prep_trap: 形容詞，常與 underpaid 或 understaffed 並用（overworked and underpaid 既過勞又低薪）。
example: Mandatory rest breaks protect overworked bus drivers from fatigue-related road accidents.

def_zh: 薪酬
def_en: pay
prep_trap: 不可數名詞。
example: Fair remuneration helps retain experienced teachers.

def_zh: 退休金；長者養老金
def_en: a regular payment made during a person's retirement from an investment fund to which that person or their employer has contributed
prep_trap: 可數名詞，領取退休金的長者為 pensioner（old-age pensioners），討論全民退休保障（universal retirement protection）必用。
example: Without a universal pension scheme, many grassroots seniors rely solely on modest government allowances.

def_zh: 未雨綢繆的；有遠見儲蓄的（如香港強積金 MPF）
def_en: making or indicative of timely preparation for the future
prep_trap: 形容詞，香港退休保障制度「強制性公積金」即 Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF)！
example: Early financial education helps young employees manage their Mandatory Provident Fund investments wisely.

def_zh: 養老積蓄；儲備金（為退休、買樓或進修儲起的積蓄）
def_en: a sum of money saved for the future
prep_trap: 可數名詞，討論理財及退休儲蓄時的地道生動詞組：build up a retirement nest egg。
example: Phone scammers often target retirees and wipe out the nest egg they spent decades saving.

def_zh: 有償債能力的；財務穩健不負債的
def_en: having assets in excess of liabilities; able to pay one's debts
prep_trap: 形容詞，相反詞為 insolvent（資不抵債的），名詞為 solvency。
example: Prudent budgeting is essential for keeping student union clubs financially solvent throughout the year.

def_zh: 破產
def_en: the state of being completely lacking in a particular quality or value, or legally declared unable to pay debts
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，注意中間有 p（bankruptcy），形容詞為 bankrupt（go bankrupt 破產）。
example: Impulsive spending on luxury goods can push young credit card holders to the brink of bankruptcy.

def_zh: 負債的；感激不盡的（對某人）
def_en: owing money, OR owing gratitude for a service or favor
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意中間 b 不發音（讀 /ɪnˈdetɪd/）！演講辭感謝父母或老師必背：We are deeply indebted to our teachers！
example: We are deeply indebted to our Principal and teachers for their unwavering guidance over the past six years.

def_zh: 欠款；逾期未付的款項（如欠租或欠交會費）
def_en: money that is owed and should have been paid earlier
prep_trap: 複數形式名詞，必配介詞 in（in arrears 拖欠款項 / rent arrears 欠租），Paper 3 追討欠款信件常用。
example: Members whose annual subscriptions remain in arrears for over two months will have their library privileges suspended.

def_zh: 逾期未還的（圖書）；過期未付的（帳單）；早該實行的（改革）
def_en: not having arrived, happened, or been done by the expected time
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 兩大用法：overdue library books（逾期圖書）及 long overdue reform（早該進行的改革）！
example: Reviewing the outdated school uniform policy is a reform that is long overdue.

def_zh: （青少年）違法者；不良少年（作形容詞：拖欠帳款的）
def_en: a young person tending to commit crime, particularly minor crime
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 juvenile delinquents（問題/違法青少年）。
example: Mentorship programmes pair retired police officers with juvenile delinquents to help them rebuild their lives.

def_zh: 蓄意破壞公物者
def_en: a person who deliberately destroys or damages public or private property
prep_trap: 可數名詞，動詞為 vandalize（蓄意破壞）。
example: Mindless vandals sprayed graffiti on the historic wall and smashed several park benches last night.

def_zh: 塗鴉（牆壁上的噴漆圖案或文字）
def_en: writing or drawings scribbled, scratched, or sprayed illicitly on a wall or other surface in a public place
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s！DSE 曾考辯論題：「街頭塗鴉究竟是街頭藝術（street art）還是破壞公物（vandalism）？」
example: Providing designated legal graffiti walls allows young street artists to express creativity without defacing public property.

def_zh: 損毀（公物、圖書或古蹟的）外觀；塗污
def_en: spoil the surface or appearance of something, for example by drawing or writing on it
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常指在圖書館書籍畫花或在古蹟刻字（deface library books / historical monuments）。
example: Tourists who carve their names onto historical monuments should be heavily fined for defacing cultural heritage.

def_zh: 垃圾蟲（亂拋垃圾的人）
def_en: a person who litters public places with trash
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港環境衛生與郊野公園宣傳文章極地道用字（selfish litterbugs）。
example: Installing webcams at hygiene blackspots helps authorities catch inconsiderate litterbugs red-handed.

def_zh: 黑點（如交通意外黑點或衛生黑點）
def_en: a place where a particular problem, such as traffic accidents or illegal dumping, occurs frequently
prep_trap: 可數名詞（亦分寫作 black spot），香港市政與交通題必背：hygiene blackspots（衛生黑點）及 traffic accident blackspots（交通黑點）！
example: The government launched a city-wide cleaning operation targeting over six hundred hygiene blackspots.

def_zh: 亂過馬路（不遵守交通燈號橫過馬路）
def_en: cross or walk in the street or road unlawfully or without regard for approaching traffic
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，亂過馬路的行人為 jaywalker，動詞為 jaywalk，道路安全題核心詞彙！
example: Staring at smartphones while jaywalking across busy roads has caused numerous preventable accidents.

def_zh: 交通癱瘓
def_en: severe traffic jam
prep_trap: 不可數名詞。
example: Expanding railway networks is the best way to prevent urban traffic gridlock.

def_zh: 共乘私家車；拼車（數人合乘一輛車上班以減碳及減塞車）
def_en: an arrangement between people to make a regular journey in a single vehicle, typically with each person taking turns to drive
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 carpool，環保減碳與舒緩擠塞題的實用建議。
example: Encouraging neighbours to carpool to work reduces both fuel expenses and rush-hour carbon emissions.

def_zh: 生物塑膠（由玉米澱粉或甘蔗等植物提煉的環保塑膠）
def_en: plastics derived from renewable biomass sources, such as vegetable fats and oils, corn starch, or microbiota
prep_trap: 常用複數形式 bioplastics。
example: Scientists are developing plant-based bioplastics from corn starch to replace petroleum-based packaging.

def_zh: 升級再造（將廢棄物設計成更高價值的產品）
def_en: the process of reusing discarded objects or material in such a way as to create a product of higher quality or value than the original
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，校園環保週必提活動：run an upcycling handicraft workshop！
example: Our Visual Arts Club organized an upcycling workshop to turn old denim jeans into stylish tote bags.

def_zh: 降級回收（回收後物料質素下降，如廢紙變紙皮）
def_en: the recycling of waste where the recycled material is of lower quality and functionality than the original material
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，與 upcycling 相對。
example: Unlike downcycling plastic into low-grade fibres, upcycling adds artistic and commercial value to waste.

def_zh: 零廢物的；無包裝裸買的（生活或商店模式）
def_en: the conservation of all resources by means of responsible production, consumption, reuse, and recovery of products without burning or landfilling
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，香港新興「裸買店」即 zero-waste bulk grocery stores！
example: Shopping at zero-waste grocery stores where customers bring their own jars eliminates plastic packaging.

def_zh: 極簡主義；斷捨離生活哲學
def_en: a style or technique that is characterized by extreme spareness and simplicity, or living with only essential possessions
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，極簡主義者或形容詞為 minimalist，DSE 反對過度消費主義（consumerism）的 5** 概念詞！
example: Embracing minimalism frees urban dwellers from the clutter and financial stress of impulse buying.

def_zh: 斷捨離；清理雜物（亦可清理思緒）
def_en: remove unnecessary items from an untidy or overcrowded place
prep_trap: 及物或不及物動詞，源自不可數名詞 clutter（雜物），既可指執屋捐贈舊物，亦可指整理思緒（declutter one's mind）。
example: Decluttering our bedrooms before the new school year and donating old books to charity is very rewarding.

def_zh: 雜物；凌亂堆放的東西（亦可作動詞：塞滿弄亂）
def_en: a collection of things lying about in an untidy state
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿加 s！
example: Studying at a clean, tidy desk free from clutter helps students concentrate much better.

def_zh: 囤積者（不捨得扔掉任何舊物或拾荒塞滿屋的人）
def_en: a person who hoards things, especially someone suffering from compulsive hoarding
basic_word: person who keeps too much stuff
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: Patience and psychological counselling are needed when helping elderly hoarders clear out decades of rubbish.

def_zh: 強迫性的；無法自拔的（如病態賭博、購物狂或手機成癮）
def_en: resulting from or relating to an irresistible urge, especially one that is against one's conscious wishes
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意與 impulsive（一時衝動）不同，compulsive 指「長期病態成癮無法控制」（compulsive gambling / shopping）。
example: Loot boxes in mobile games are designed like slot machines and can lead to compulsive gambling habits.

def_zh: 成癮；沉迷（網癮、毒癮、賭癮）
def_en: the fact or condition of being addicted to a particular substance, thing, or activity
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，必考介詞：addiction TO gaming / social media（切勿用 of！）；成癮者為 addict。
example: Setting daily screen-time limits is the first step toward overcoming smartphone addiction.

def_zh: 成癮者；沉迷某事物的人（如毒癮者、工作狂或購物狂）
def_en: a person who is addicted to a particular substance, typically an illegal drug, or an activity
prep_trap: 可數名詞（讀 /ˈædɪkt/，重音在首音節），常配 drug addicts 或 internet addicts。
example: Residential treatment centres help young drug addicts rebuild self-discipline and vocational skills.

def_zh: 工作狂（把工作置於健康與家庭之上的打工仔）
def_en: a person who compulsively works hard and long hours
prep_trap: 可數名詞，同類字尾有 shopaholic（購物狂）、chocoholic（朱古力迷）。
example: Hong Kong's workaholic culture often causes parents to miss precious moments of their children's childhood.

def_zh: 購物狂（沉迷瘋狂購物的消費者）
def_en: a person considered to be addicted to shopping
prep_trap: 可數名詞，討論雙十一網購節（online shopping festivals）及信用卡欠債題極好用。
example: Flash sales and credit card instalments easily turn young office workers into debt-ridden shopaholics.

def_zh: 富裕病（因過度追求物質財富而產生的空虛、焦慮與過度消費）
def_en: a psychological malaise supposedly affecting wealthy young people, symptoms of which include a lack of motivation, feelings of guilt, and a sense of isolation
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，由 affluence + influenza 合成的 5** 亮眼詞彙！
example: Despite owning the latest gadgets, many teenagers in wealthy cities suffer from boredom and affluenza.

def_zh: 倦怠感；百無聊賴的空虛無聊
def_en: a feeling of listlessness and dissatisfaction arising from a lack of occupation or excitement
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，讀 /ɒnˈwiː/。
example: Meaningful community service projects help teenagers overcome summer holiday boredom and ennui.

def_zh: 無精打采的；提不起勁的（因生病、炎熱或失眠）
def_en: of a person or their manner lacking energy or enthusiasm
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 listlessness。
example: Without air conditioning or proper ventilation, students become listless on sweltering summer afternoons.

def_zh: 酷熱難耐的；悶熱得令人流汗的（天氣）
def_en: uncomfortably hot
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 描寫香港夏天酷熱天氣或劏房沒有冷氣的 5** 詞彙（sweltering summer heat）！
example: Elderly tenants living in rooftop huts suffer terribly during the sweltering summer months.

def_zh: 烈日炎炎的；灼熱的（陽光或高溫）
def_en: very hot
prep_trap: 形容詞，必背描寫搭配：under the scorching sun（在烈日當空下），運動會或清潔工人題必用！
example: Lifeguards and street cleaners work tirelessly under the scorching sun to keep the public safe.

def_zh: 熱浪；持續酷熱天氣
def_en: a prolonged period of abnormally hot weather
prep_trap: 可數名詞，全球暖化與極端天氣（extreme weather）必提例子：prolonged summer heatwaves。
example: Global warming has made record-breaking summer heatwaves more frequent and intense across Asia.

def_zh: 潮濕的；濕熱的（香港春夏季天氣）
def_en: marked by a relatively high level of water vapor in the atmosphere
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 humidity（relative humidity 相對濕度），形容香港天氣必配 hot and humid！
example: Food spoils quickly in Hong Kong's hot and humid climate if not refrigerated properly.

def_zh: 悶熱潮濕的（令人黏笠不適的天氣）
def_en: of weather unpleasantly warm and humid
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫暴雨前或回南天悶熱天氣的生動用字。
example: Running a ten-kilometre race on a warm and muggy evening requires extra hydration.

def_zh: 惡劣的（天氣，尤指狂風暴雨）
def_en: of the weather unpleasantly cold or wet
prep_trap: 正式形容詞，Paper 3 學校通告及活動指引最愛的官方詞組：in case of inclement weather（如遇惡劣天氣）！
example: In case of inclement weather, the outdoor prize-giving ceremony will be moved to the school hall.

def_zh: 烈風；狂風（香港八號風球即 Gale or Storm Signal No. 8）
def_en: a very strong wind
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港天文台八號風球英文正是 No. 8 Gale or Storm Signal！
example: All daytime schools are suspended whenever the Observatory hoisting the No. 8 Gale or Storm Signal.

def_zh: 傾盆大雨；驟雨
def_en: a heavy fall of rain
prep_trap: 可數名詞，替換 heavy rain 的生動名詞（a sudden heavy downpour）。
example: Hikers were caught in a sudden downpour and had to seek shelter at a country park pavilion.

def_zh: 暴雨洪水；（資訊、投訴或申請的）湧至（亦可作動詞）
def_en: a severe flood, or a heavy fall of rain, OR an overwhelming amount of something
prep_trap: 可數名詞，既可指黑色暴雨洪水，亦可指海量資訊（a deluge of online information / complaints）。
example: Students need critical thinking skills to filter through the daily deluge of online information.

def_zh: 水災；淹沒（低窪地區被海水或暴雨淹浸）
def_en: flooding
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，討論鯉魚門或大澳受風暴潮水浸（coastal inundation）時的專業字。
example: Building movable flood barriers helps protect low-lying coastal villages like Tai O from seawater inundation.

def_zh: 淹沒；浸沒（於水中）
def_en: cause to be under water
prep_trap: 及物或不及物動詞，常作被動：cars were submerged in floodwater（車輛被洪水淹浸）。
example: Rising sea levels threaten to completely submerge low-lying Pacific island nations within decades.

def_zh: 蒸發；（希望、信心或資金）突然消失殆盡
def_en: turn from liquid into vapor, OR cease to exist; vanish
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，名詞為 evaporation；比喻用法極佳：Public trust quickly evaporated（公眾信任瞬間蕩然無存）。
example: Without proper follow-up support, students' initial enthusiasm for the recycling scheme quickly evaporated.

def_zh: 凝結；（將長文或報告）濃縮精簡
def_en: make something denser or more concentrated; express a piece of writing or speech in fewer words; make concise
prep_trap: 及物動詞，Paper 3 Summary Writing（撮要寫作）正是將長篇資料 condense into a 150-word summary！
collocations: condense a long article into key points
example: Making condensed mind-map notes is a highly effective way to revise history topics before exams.

def_zh: 刪節；節略（長篇小說或經典名著）
def_en: shorten a book, movie, speech, or other text without losing the sense
prep_trap: 及物動詞，DSE 推廣英文閱讀時，建議初中生先讀經典名著的「簡寫版」即 abridged versions of classics！
collocations: abridged version of a classic novel
example: Junior secondary students can build confidence by reading abridged versions of English literary classics.

def_zh: 故事梗概；劇情大綱（電影、戲劇或小說）
def_en: a brief summary or general survey of something, such as the plot of a book or film
prep_trap: 可數名詞，複數為 synopses，寫書評或影評（Book/Film Review）第一段介紹劇情大綱必備專業字！
collocations: write a synopsis of the film
example: A good book review should provide a brief synopsis of the plot without giving away the ending.

def_zh: 劇透（提前洩露電影或小說結局的內容）
def_en: a description of an important plot development in a television show, movie, or book which if previously known may reduce surprise or suspense
prep_trap: 可數名詞，影評或書評極地道詞彙：without any spoilers（不含劇透）/ spoiler alert（劇透警告）。
example: When writing a film review for the school magazine, remember to avoid major plot spoilers.

def_zh: 高潮（故事、電影、音樂會或活動的最精彩頂點）
def_en: the most intense, exciting, or important point of something; a culmination or apex
prep_trap: 可數名詞，配 reach a climax（達到高潮），形容詞為 climactic（高潮的，注意拼字中間有 c，勿與氣候的 climatic 混淆！）。
example: The talent show reached a thrilling climax when the teachers' band performed a rock song on stage.

def_zh: （戲劇、小說或事件的）結局、收場
def_en: the final part of a play, movie, or narrative in which the strands of the plot are drawn together and matters are explained or resolved
prep_trap: 單數名詞，書評或影評討論結尾收筆時的高階詞彙。
example: The detective movie kept the audience guessing right up to its surprising final denouement.

def_zh: 懸念結尾（劇集或故事在最緊張關頭結束，引人追看下一集）
def_en: an ending to an episode of a serial drama that leaves the audience in suspense
prep_trap: 可數名詞，解釋為何青少年會通宵瘋狂煲劇（binge-watch dramas）的絕佳原因：Every episode ends on a cliffhanger！
example: Streaming dramas often end every episode on a cliffhanger to tempt viewers into watching the next one immediately.

def_zh: 主角；主人翁（小說、電影或戲劇，亦可指某運動的倡導者）
def_en: the leading character or one of the major characters in a drama, movie, novel, or other fictional text
prep_trap: 可數名詞，寫書評/影評替換 main character 的 5** 必備字！反派角色則為 antagonist。
example: Readers can easily relate to the young protagonist's struggle to balance family expectations with personal dreams.

def_zh: 反派角色；對手；敵對者
def_en: a person who actively opposes or is hostile to someone or something; an adversary or villain in a story
prep_trap: 可數名詞，與主角 protagonist 相對，動詞為 antagonize（激怒/與⋯⋯為敵）。
example: What makes the superhero film memorable is its complex antagonist, whose motives are surprisingly understandable.

def_zh: 原型；典型代表
def_en: a very typical example of a certain person or thing, or an original model in literature
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意 ch 發 /k/ 音（讀 /ˈɑːkɪtaɪp/）。
example: The selfless doctor in the novel serves as the archetype of a compassionate healer.

def_zh: 誇張諷刺畫；滑稽刻板的人物描寫
def_en: a picture, description, or imitation of a person in which certain striking characteristics are exaggerated in order to create a comic or grotesque effect
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: The caricature booth at our charity fun fair was hugely popular, with art club students drawing funny portraits.

def_zh: 諷刺作品；諷刺文學（用幽默誇張手法批判社會時弊）
def_en: the use of humor, irony, exaggeration, or ridicule to expose and criticize people's stupidity or vices
prep_trap: 不可數或可數名詞，形容詞為 satirical（諷刺的，如 a satirical drama / cartoon）。
example: Our drama club wrote a clever satire poking fun at teenagers' obsession with smartphone filters.

def_zh: 惡搞作品；諧仿（模仿知名歌曲或電影以達致搞笑效果，亦可作動詞）
def_en: an imitation of the style of a particular writer, artist, or genre with deliberate exaggeration for comic effect
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港網絡文化極常見將流行曲改詞（二次創作 / parody songs），討論創意與版權時必用！
example: Creating parody songs with rewritten lyrics is a popular way for netizens to express humour on social media.

def_zh: （文學、電影、音樂或藝術的）體裁、類型、流派
def_en: a category of artistic composition, as in music or literature, characterized by similarities in form, style, or subject matter
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意法文借字發音為 /ˈʒɒnrə/，推廣閱讀或寫影評時替換 type of book/film 的 5* 必備字！
example: School libraries should purchase books across diverse genres, including graphic novels, biographies, and science fiction.

def_zh: 改編作品（如將小說改編成電影）；適應（環境或氣候變化）
def_en: a movie, television drama, or stage play that has been adapted from a written work, OR the process of adapting to new conditions
basic_word: film version of a book / adjustment
prep_trap: 作「改編電影/話劇」時為可數名詞（a film adaptation of the novel）；作「適應」時為不可數名詞（climate change adaptation）。
example: Watching the film adaptation of an English novel first can motivate reluctant students to read the original book.

def_zh: 續集（電影或小說）；後續結果
def_en: a published, broadcast, or recorded work that continues the story or develops the theme of an earlier one
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配介詞 to（a sequel to a blockbuster movie）；前傳則為 prequel。
example: While the first superhero movie was fresh and exciting, its sequel relied too heavily on computer-generated explosions.

def_zh: 賣座巨片；大熱暢銷書
def_en: a thing of great power or size, in particular a movie, book, or other product that is a great commercial success
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 Hollywood blockbuster（荷里活大片，與本地小成本電影 low-budget indie films 對比）。
example: Government film funds help local directors produce quality movies that can compete with Hollywood blockbusters.

def_zh: 首映禮；首次公演（亦可作動詞）
def_en: the first performance of a musical or theatrical work or the first showing of a movie
prep_trap: 可數名詞，活動報告或文化推廣常用 world premiere / gala premiere。
example: Our school drama club will hold the premiere of its original musical in the auditorium this Friday.

def_zh: 日間場次；下午場（話劇、音樂會或電影）
def_en: an afternoon performance in a theater or cinema
prep_trap: 可數名詞，Paper 3 購票或節目時間表常考 matinee performance（下午場，票價通常較晚間場 evening show 便宜）！
example: The theatre offers half-price tickets for students attending the Saturday afternoon matinee performance.

def_zh: 安哥；返場加演（演唱會或音樂會結束時觀眾熱烈要求加演）
def_en: a repeated or additional performance of an item at the end of a concert, as called for by an audience
prep_trap: 可數名詞，注意開頭 en 讀 /ɒŋ/，配 an encore。
example: The audience clapped so loudly that the school orchestra returned to the stage for an encore.

def_zh: 熱烈鼓掌歡迎；起立致敬喝采
def_en: a sustained and enthusiastic show of appreciation from an audience, especially by means of applause
prep_trap: 可數名詞，演講或表演報告結尾滿分詞組：receive a standing ovation（獲得全場起立鼓掌致敬）！
example: At the end of her inspiring speech, the Paralympic athlete received a two-minute standing ovation.

def_zh: 高度讚譽；喝采（亦可作動詞：盛讚）
def_en: enthusiastic and public praise
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，書評或影評必背搭配：win critical acclaim（贏得影評人一致盛讚）或 critically acclaimed（備受讚譽的）！
example: The low-budget Hong Kong film won widespread critical acclaim for its realistic portrayal of family life.

def_zh: 讚譽；榮譽；佩服（常配 kudos to somebody）
def_en: praise and honor received for an achievement
prep_trap: 不可數單數名詞（雖以 s 結尾但不是複數！），校報文章或演講讚揚籌委會時極地道：Kudos to the organizing committee！
example: Kudos must go to our backstage crew, who worked tirelessly to make the drama night a success.

def_zh: 致敬；頌詞；體現（某美德的明證）
def_en: an act, statement, or gift that is intended to show gratitude, respect, or admiration
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，必考固定片語：pay tribute to somebody（向醫護人員/老師/先賢致敬）！
example: The graduation video paid a moving tribute to the janitors and teachers who supported us every day.

def_zh: 敬意；致敬（尤指在藝術創作或紀念儀式中致敬）
def_en: special honor or respect shown publicly
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必配介詞 to：pay homage to traditional culture / pioneers。
example: The young director's new movie pays homage to classic Hong Kong martial arts films of the 1980s.

def_zh: 崇敬；敬畏（對大自然、歷史傳統或長輩）
def_en: deep respect for someone or something
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 reverent，動詞為 revere。
example: Traditional festivals teach young generations to treat ancestral customs and nature with deep reverence.

def_zh: 尊重；敬重（亦見於 self-esteem 自尊心）
def_en: respect and admiration, typically for a person
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 hold somebody in high esteem（高度敬重某人）或 boost self-esteem（提升自尊心）。
example: Dedicated teachers who care genuinely about their students' well-being are held in high esteem by parents.

def_zh: 聲望；威望；名氣（名校或專業職位的社會地位）
def_en: widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 prestigious（享負盛名的，如 a prestigious university），討論家長盲目追捧名校時必用。
example: Students should choose university subjects based on genuine interest rather than merely chasing social prestige.

def_zh: 聲望地位；身高體格
def_en: importance or reputation gained by ability or achievement, OR a person's natural height
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意與 statue（雕像）及 statute（法規）拼字極易混淆！
example: Hosting world-class cultural exhibitions enhances Hong Kong's international stature as an arts hub.

def_zh: 雕像；塑像（如李小龍銅像或天壇大佛）
def_en: a carved or cast figure of a person or animal, especially one that is life-size or larger
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港旅遊地標常提 the bronze statue of Bruce Lee 或 the Big Buddha statue。
example: Tourists love taking photos beside the bronze statue of martial arts legend Bruce Lee on the Avenue of Stars.

def_zh: 成文法；法規；章程
def_en: a written law passed by a legislative body
prep_trap: 可數名詞，形容詞為 statutory（法定的，如香港「法定最低工資」statutory minimum wage /「法定假日」statutory holidays）！
example: Reviewing the statutory minimum wage annually helps grassroots workers cope with rising inflation.

def_zh: 法定的；法例規定的（如法定侍產假、法定古蹟或法定機構）
def_en: required, permitted, or enacted by statute
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 勞工權益與公共政策必背高頻字：statutory minimum wage（法定最低工資）/ statutory body（法定機構）！
example: Extending statutory maternity and paternity leave is a vital step toward creating a family-friendly society.

def_zh: 條例；法例（香港法律的官方名稱，如《噪音管制條例》）
def_en: an authoritative order; a piece of legislation enacted by a municipal authority
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港所有法例均稱為 Ordinance（如 Waste Disposal Ordinance），寫信給政府或報章提議立法時必用！
example: The government should amend the Road Traffic Ordinance to regulate the use of electric mobility devices.

def_zh: 立法；法例（總稱，不可數名詞）
def_en: laws, considered collectively, or the process of making or enacting laws
prep_trap: DSE 極高頻文法陷阱：legislation 是不可數名詞，切勿加 s（切勿寫 legislations！應寫 introduce new legislation / a piece of legislation）！
example: While government legislation can ban single-use plastics, long-term success depends on public education.

def_zh: 立法（配 for 或 against）
def_en: make or enact laws
prep_trap: 不及物或及物動詞，常配 legislate against cyberbullying / doxxing（立法打擊網絡欺凌/起底）；立法會議員為 legislator。
example: Many parents urge the government to legislate against the sale of energy drinks to children.

def_zh: （法律的）制定、頒布生效
def_en: the process of passing legislation
prep_trap: 不可數或可數名詞，源自動詞 enact（enact a law 制定法例）。
example: Since the enactment of the indoor smoking ban, public restaurants have become much cleaner and healthier.

def_zh: 執法；執行（法例或校規）
def_en: the act of compelling observance of or compliance with a law, rule, or obligation
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自動詞 enforce，DSE 政策論證必背金句：A law is useless without strict enforcement（有法不執等於無用）！
example: Passing environmental laws is meaningless without strict enforcement and heavy penalties for offenders.

def_zh: 遵守；依從（法規、安全指引或衛生標準）
def_en: the action or fact of complying with a wish or command
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自動詞 comply（comply with），必考介詞：in compliance with fire safety regulations！
example: All food stalls at the school carnival must operate in strict compliance with hygiene guidelines.

def_zh: 違反；觸犯（法例、規章或條款，正式用語）
def_en: violate the prohibition or order of a law, treaty, or code of conduct
prep_trap: 及物動詞，後面直接接法例或校規（contravene the fire safety regulations），不加介詞，比 break 正式得多！
example: Restaurants that dump grease into public drains contravene environmental laws and face prosecution.

def_zh: 違反（合約或校規）；（資料保安）外洩缺口（亦可作動詞）
def_en: an act of breaking or failing to observe a law, agreement, or code of conduct, OR a security gap
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，DSE 必考兩大用法：in breach of school rules（違反校規）及 a personal data breach（個人資料外洩事故）！
example: Following the serious personal data breach, the company upgraded its cybersecurity systems immediately.

def_zh: 公然無視；蓄意違抗（法律、交通規則或禁令）
def_en: openly disregard a rule, law or convention
prep_trap: 及物動詞，切勿與 flaunt（炫耀財富）混淆！形容無良司機或商人「公然藐視法紀」（openly flout the law）的 5** 動詞。
example: Heavier fines are needed for taxi drivers who openly flout the law by overcharging tourists.

def_zh: 炫耀；誇耀（財富、名牌或奢華生活）
def_en: display something ostentatiously, especially in order to provoke envy or admiration
prep_trap: 及物動詞，注意與 flout（違抗法律）區分！討論社交媒體网红「炫富」（flaunt their wealth on Instagram）必用！
example: When influencers constantly flaunt luxury goods online, teenage followers may feel dissatisfied with their own lives.
