def_zh: 奢華的；揮霍鋪張的；慷慨大量的（亦可作動詞）
def_en: sumptuously rich, elaborate, or luxurious
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 a lavish banquet / lifestyle（奢華宴會/生活）。
example: Instead of holding a lavish banquet, the couple donated their wedding budget to an animal shelter.

def_zh: 富麗堂皇的；極盡奢華富裕的
def_en: ostentatiously rich and luxurious or lavish
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 opulence，常用於對比貧富懸殊（opulent shopping malls vs dilapidated tenements）。
example: The dilapidated subdivided flats stand in stark contrast to the opulent luxury malls just across the street.

def_zh: 簡樸清苦的（住宿或訓練環境，沒有豪華享受的）
def_en: showing the indifference to comfort or luxury traditionally associated with ancient Sparta
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫露營營地或訓練營設施簡樸（spartan camping facilities）卻能鍛煉青年堅毅精神時極佳。
example: Living in spartan hostel rooms during the outward bound camp taught students to appreciate home comforts.

def_zh: 簡樸無華的；嚴厲克制的；（經濟政策）緊縮節流的
def_en: severe or strict in manner, attitude, or appearance; having no comforts or luxuries
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 austerity（政府財政緊縮政策 austerity measures）。
example: During periods of fiscal deficit, governments often introduce austerity measures to cut public spending.

def_zh: 審慎的；精明謹慎的；未雨綢繆的（尤指理財或決策）
def_en: acting with or showing care and thought for the future
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 prudence，DSE 個人理財及政府財政預算案必用：prudent financial management（審慎理財）！
example: Learning prudent financial management in secondary school prevents young adults from overspending on credit cards.

def_zh: 明智審慎的；有判斷力的（運用時間、科技或資源）
def_en: having, showing, or done with good judgment or sense
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 議論文討論如何使用人工智能或手機時的 5** 詞組：the judicious use of AI / technology（明智審慎地善用科技）！
example: Rather than banning smartphones completely, parents should guide children toward the judicious use of digital devices.

def_zh: 有眼光的；具明辨是非能力的（消費者或讀者）
def_en: having or showing good judgment
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自動詞 discern（明辨），媒體素養與精明消費題必背：become discerning consumers / readers！
example: Media literacy education trains students to become discerning readers who question unverified online claims.

def_zh: 精明敏銳的；洞悉先機的
def_en: having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people and turn this to one's advantage
prep_trap: 形容詞，母音開頭配冠詞 an（an astute observer / leader）。
example: An astute student leader listens carefully to classmates' concerns before proposing changes to school rules.

def_zh: 精明的；有商業頭腦與準確判斷力的
def_en: having or showing sharp powers of judgment; astute
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 shrewd investment / shopper。
example: Shrewd shoppers compare unit prices across different supermarkets instead of being fooled by flashy packaging.

def_zh: 精明內行的；熟練掌握某事物的（尤指 tech-savvy 熟悉科技的）
def_en: shrewd and knowledgeable; having common sense and good judgment
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 必背複合詞：tech-savvy youth（熟悉科技的年輕一代）及 media-savvy consumers！
example: Tech-savvy student volunteers can teach elderly neighbours how to use video-calling apps to chat with relatives.

def_zh: 輕信他人的；容易受騙上當的
def_en: easily persuaded to believe something; credulous
prep_trap: 形容詞，字尾是 -ible，名詞為 gullibility，防騙與虛假廣告題替換 easy to cheat 的 5* 核心字！
example: Online scammers often prey on gullible teenagers by promising easy money for liking social media posts.

def_zh: 天真無邪的；涉世未深而輕信的
def_en: of a person or action showing a lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意發音為雙音節 /naɪˈiːv/，名詞為 naivety。
example: It would be naive to believe that cyberbullying will disappear simply by putting up posters.

def_zh: 輕信的；不加懷疑就相信的
def_en: having or showing too great a readiness to believe things
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意切勿與 credible（可信可靠的）混淆！credulous 指「人太易信人」（與 gullible 同義）。
example: Exaggerated weight-loss advertisements easily deceive credulous consumers who are desperate for quick results.

def_zh: 抱懷疑態度的；不輕信的（審慎查證）
def_en: not easily convinced; having doubts or reservations
prep_trap: 形容詞（美式拼作 skeptical，注意讀 /ˈskep-/），必配介詞 about/of；名詞為 scepticism，批判思考題必備！
example: Students should maintain a healthy scepticism toward viral health remedies shared on social media.

def_zh: 憤世嫉俗的；冷嘲熱諷的（認為人人皆自私的負面態度）
def_en: believing that people are motivated by self-interest; distrustful of human sincerity or integrity
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 cynicism，注意與 sceptical（理性求證的懷疑）不同，cynical 偏向「冷漠憤世、覺得做乜都無用」。
example: When charities are hit by financial scandals, the public quickly grows cynical about donating money.

def_zh: 悲觀的
def_en: tending to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen
prep_trap: 形容詞，必配介詞 about（be pessimistic about career prospects），名詞為 pessimism，與 optimistic 相對。
example: Constant exposure to negative news online can make young people overly pessimistic about their future.

def_zh: 樂觀的；抱有希望的
def_en: hopeful and confident about the future
prep_trap: 形容詞，配介詞 about，名詞為 optimism（樂觀精神）。
example: Cultivating an optimistic mindset helps examination candidates bounce back quickly from disappointing mock scores.

def_zh: 輕快樂觀的；積極向上的（音樂、氣氛或心情）
def_en: cheerful; optimistic
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫校園活動音樂或演講氣氛（an upbeat atmosphere / melody）的極佳用字。
collocations: end the speech on an upbeat note
example: Playing upbeat music during morning exercise sessions energizes students for the school day ahead.

def_zh: 心情愉快樂觀的；（經濟或旅遊市場）蓬勃向上的；有浮力的
def_en: able or tending to keep afloat, OR cheerful and optimistic, OR of an economy/market active and thriving
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意發音為 /ˈbɔɪənt/。
example: The arrival of mega international concerts kept the city's tourism and retail sectors buoyant.

def_zh: 有抗逆力的；堅韌能迅速復原的（學生心理或城市基建）
def_en: of a person or animal able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 resilience（抗逆力），DSE 青少年心理健康與氣候變化基建（climate-resilient）的雙料核心字！
example: Extracurricular sports teach teenagers to become emotionally resilient when facing setbacks and defeats.

def_zh: 堅毅果敢的（表現）；真實粗礪不加粉飾的（寫實電影）
def_en: showing courage and resolve, OR of a film/book showing unpleasant realities uncompromisingly
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自不可數名詞 grit（堅毅意志）。
example: Despite trailing at half-time, our basketball team delivered a gritty second-half performance to win.

def_zh: 堅定不移的；始終如一的（支持、決心或奉獻）
def_en: steady or resolute; not wavering
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 畢業演講辭感謝老師與父母支持必背滿分搭配：thank you for your unwavering support and dedication！
example: I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to my parents for their unwavering support throughout my DSE journey.

def_zh: 堅定不移的；忠誠可靠的（朋友或信念）
def_en: resolutely or dutifully firm and unwavering
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Even when criticized by others, the environmental pioneer remained steadfast in her mission to protect wetlands.

def_zh: 持續不斷的；不懈的（努力）；無情高壓的（競爭）
def_en: oppressively constant; incessant; never giving up
prep_trap: 形容詞，既可形容香港學業競爭無休止（relentless academic pressure），亦可形容運動員不懈訓練（relentless pursuit of excellence）。
example: Hong Kong students face relentless academic pressure from primary school all the way to university entrance exams.

def_zh: 沒完沒了的；連綿不斷的（噪音、大雨或手機通知）
def_en: of something regarded as unpleasant continuing without pause or interruption
prep_trap: 形容詞，投訴信描寫地盤噪音或樓上裝修噪音（incessant construction noise）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Incessant smartphone notifications fragment students' attention and prevent them from entering deep focus.

def_zh: 永無止境的；長期持續的（焦慮、貧困或運轉）
def_en: never ending or changing; occurring repeatedly; so frequent as to seem endless and uninterrupted
prep_trap: 形容詞，動詞為 perpetuate（使壞現象延續/固化，如 perpetuate gender stereotypes 延續性別定型）！
example: Unrealistic beauty advertisements perpetuate body anxiety among impressionable teenage girls.

def_zh: 長年存在的；反覆出現的老大難（問題，如土地不足或塞車）
def_en: lasting or existing for a long or apparently infinite time; enduring or continually recurring
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 議論文開頭點出香港長期存在的老大難問題（a perennial problem in Hong Kong）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Sky-high housing prices and long waiting lists for public flats have been a perennial problem in Hong Kong.

def_zh: 根深蒂固的；深層次的（社會矛盾、偏見或恐懼）
def_en: firmly established at a deep level; hard to change
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，與 deep-rooted 同義，討論社會深層次結構問題（deep-seated social problems / prejudices）必用。
example: Public education is required to uproot deep-seated prejudices against recovering mental health patients.

def_zh: 根深蒂固難以改變的（習慣、既得利益或觀念）
def_en: of an attitude, habit, or belief firmly established and difficult or unlikely to change; ingrained
prep_trap: 分詞形容詞，常配 entrenched habits / vested interests（既得利益）。
example: Changing deeply entrenched overtime work habits requires strong leadership from company management.

def_zh: 深植人心的；自幼養成的（習慣或文化傳統）
def_en: of a habit, belief, or attitude firmly fixed or established; difficult to change
prep_trap: 形容詞，必配介詞 in（deeply ingrained in our culture）。
example: Respecting elders is a traditional virtue deeply ingrained in Chinese family culture.

def_zh: 天生的；與生俱來的（才能或好奇心）
def_en: inborn; natural
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意雙寫 n，討論「成功靠天生才華（innate talent）還是後天努力（hard work）」的必備字！
example: Inquiry-based science experiments nurture young children's innate curiosity about how the world works.

def_zh: 固有的；內在伴隨的（風險、缺陷或價值）
def_en: existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute
prep_trap: 形容詞，必配介詞 in（the risks inherent in online investing 網上投資固有的風險）。
example: Outdoor adventure camps teach teenagers how to assess and manage the risks inherent in mountain hiking.

def_zh: 內在的；本質固有的（價值或學習動機）
def_en: belonging naturally; essential
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 教育心理學 5** 詞組：intrinsic motivation（內在自發學習動機）vs extrinsic motivation（外在物質獎罰）！
example: Teachers should spark students' intrinsic motivation to learn rather than relying solely on exam grades.

def_zh: 外在的；非本質的（如物質獎勵或外在壓力）
def_en: not part of the essential nature of someone or something; coming or operating from outside
prep_trap: 形容詞，與 intrinsic（內在的）相對，常配 extrinsic rewards / motivation（外在獎賞動機）。
example: While extrinsic rewards like prizes can motivate children initially, lasting learning requires intrinsic interest.

def_zh: 膚淺的（思想或評論）；淺水的（泳池或海灣）
def_en: of little depth; not exhibiting, requiring, or capable of serious thought
prep_trap: 形容詞，既可指淺水區（the shallow end of the pool），亦可批評人只重外貌與物質（shallow and materialistic）。
example: Judging a person's worth solely by their designer clothes is both shallow and short-sighted.

def_zh: 輕浮無聊的；不重要的；亂花錢買無用之物的（消費或投訴）
def_en: not having any serious purpose or value
prep_trap: 形容詞，批評「無聊瑣碎的投訴」（frivolous complaints）或「胡亂揮霍」（frivolous spending）的高分字。
example: Emergency ambulance services should not be wasted on callers with minor or frivolous complaints.

def_zh: 瑣碎小器的（爭執）；輕微的（罪行，如小偷小摸 petty crime）；零用現金（petty cash）
def_en: of little importance; trivial, OR of a person small-minded
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 常考三個搭配：petty arguments（為小事斤斤計較爭吵）、petty crime（輕微罪行）及 Paper 3 的 petty cash（零用金）！
example: Good teammates focus on common goals instead of wasting time on petty arguments.

def_zh: 微不足道的；區區小事的
def_en: unimportant or trivial
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 a trifling matter / sum（區區小事/微不足道的金額）。
example: Neighbors should communicate politely rather than calling the police over trifling noise disputes.

def_zh: 無關痛癢的；微不足道的
def_en: not important or significant
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 unimportant 的高階詞彙。
example: Perfectionists often waste hours worrying about inconsequential details in their slides.

def_zh: 最基本的；首要的（原則或錯誤）
def_en: of the greatest importance; fundamental
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 a cardinal rule（首要鐵律）。
example: Never sharing your bank password with strangers is the cardinal rule of online cybersecurity.

def_zh: 壓倒一切的；首要考慮的（目標或優先事項）
def_en: more important than any other considerations
prep_trap: 形容詞，只作定語，源自動詞 override（凌駕於），常配 the overriding priority。
example: During a typhoon, protecting citizens' lives is the government's overriding priority.

def_zh: 緊急迫切的；要求嚴苛的
def_en: pressing; demanding
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Emergency relief funds are reserved for families facing exigent financial hardship.

def_zh: 極其嚴重的；危急的；迫切的
def_en: extremely serious or urgent
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 必背兩個高分搭配：in dire need of help（極需援助）及 dire consequences（嚴重後果）！
example: Without immediate action to reduce carbon emissions, our planet will face dire consequences.

def_zh: 嚴重的；嚴肅莊重的（除作名詞「墳墓」外的高頻用法）
def_en: giving cause for alarm; serious
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 grave concern（嚴重關切）或 a grave threat（重大威脅）。
example: Medical experts have expressed grave concern over the rising popularity of e-cigarettes among teenagers.

def_zh: 鮮明突出的（對比）；嚴酷赤裸的（現實或警告）
def_en: severe or bare in appearance or outline; unpleasantly or sharply clear
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 議論文必背黃金搭配：stand in stark contrast to（與⋯⋯形成鮮明對比）及 serve as a stark reminder（作為嚴肅的警惕）！
example: The recent fatal industrial accident serves as a stark reminder of the importance of workplace safety.

def_zh: 顯而易見的；極其明顯的（錯誤、漏洞或不公）
def_en: amidst or shining with a harsh, dazzling light, OR highly obvious or conspicuous
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 a glaring disparity / loophole / mistake（極其明顯的差距/漏洞/錯誤）。
collocations: glaring disparity between rich and poor
example: The glaring wealth gap in our city calls for more targeted social welfare policies.

def_zh: 明目張膽的；公然無忌的（違規、謊言或歧視）
def_en: of bad behavior done openly and unashamedly
prep_trap: 形容詞，副詞為 blatantly，批評無良商人「明目張膽地違反條例」（a blatant disregard for the law）極有力！
example: Illegal parking on pedestrian pavements shows a blatant disregard for the safety of wheelchair users.

def_zh: 公然惡劣的；明目張膽的（違法或侵犯人權）
def_en: of something considered wrong or immoral conspicuously or obviously offensive
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 a flagrant violation / breach of rules。
example: Dumping construction waste into country parks is a flagrant violation of environmental laws.

def_zh: 極其惡劣的；駭人聽聞的（失誤或違規行為）
def_en: outstandingly bad; shocking
prep_trap: 形容詞，母音開頭配冠詞 an（an egregious error / abuse）。
example: Leaving hospital patients waiting in corridors for twelve hours is an egregious failure of resource planning.

def_zh: 十惡不赦的；極其殘忍可憎的（罪行）
def_en: of a person or wrongful act, especially a crime utterly odious or wicked
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意發音為 /ˈheɪnəs/，專門修飾嚴重罪行（a heinous crime）。
example: Using young children to traffic illegal drugs is a heinous crime that deserves severe punishment.

def_zh: 極其惡劣的（服務、天氣或罪行）
def_en: horrifyingly wicked, OR of a very poor quality; extremely bad or unpleasant
prep_trap: 形容詞，投訴信批評餐廳衛生或服務態度極差（atrocious service / hygiene）時極有氣勢！
example: We were shocked by the atrocious hygiene conditions and rude attitude of the waiter at the restaurant.

def_zh: 極其糟糕的；差到無底線的（表現、紀錄或環境）
def_en: extremely bad; appalling
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自 abyss（深淵），配 an abysmal safety record / service。
example: Contractors with an abysmal workplace safety record should be barred from bidding for public projects.

def_zh: 令人震驚憤慨的；惡劣得駭人的（環境或對待）
def_en: causing shock or dismay; horrific; very bad
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意雙寫 p 及雙寫 l，源自動詞 appal（We were appalled by... 我們對⋯⋯感到震驚憤慨）。
example: Volunteers were appalled by the cramped and unsanitary conditions inside the coffin homes.

def_zh: 應受譴責的；極其惡劣可恥的（行為或狀況）
def_en: deserving strong condemnation; shockingly bad in quality
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自動詞 deplore（強烈譴責）。
example: Cyberbullying a classmate to the point of depression is deplorable behaviour that schools must punish.

def_zh: 應受嚴厲譴責的；道德敗壞的
def_en: deserving censure or condemnation
prep_trap: 形容詞，字尾是 -ible，常配 morally reprehensible（道德上應受譴責的）。
example: Defrauding vulnerable elderly citizens of their life savings is a morally reprehensible act.

def_zh: 不道德的；違反專業操守的（商業、醫療或科研行為）
def_en: not morally correct
prep_trap: 形容詞，正面詞為 ethical（合乎道德的），商業操守、AI 倫理及動物測試題必用！
collocations: ethical and unethical uses of AI
example: Consumers are boycotting cosmetics brands that still engage in unethical animal testing.

def_zh: 不道德的；傷風敗俗的
def_en: not conforming to accepted standards of morality
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意雙寫 m，與 moral（道德的）相反。
example: Profiteering by raising mask prices tenfold during a pandemic is deeply immoral.

def_zh: 昧著良心的；肆無忌憚的；漫天過海不合理的（收費）
def_en: not right or reasonable; shockingly unfair
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自 conscience（良心），批評無良美容院收取「不合理天價」（unconscionable fees）的頂級詞彙。
example: It is unconscionable for beauty parlours to trick mentally disabled customers into signing huge loans.

def_zh: （價格、租金或收費）貴得離譜的、天價的
def_en: of a price or amount charged unreasonably high
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意中間沒有 h（exorbitant），DSE 討論香港天價樓租與演唱會黃牛票替換 too expensive 的 5** 詞彙！
example: Exorbitant commercial rents have forced many traditional family-owned eateries to close down.

def_zh: （價格高得）令人卻步的；禁止性的
def_en: of a price or charge excessively high; difficult or impossible to pay
prep_trap: 形容詞，副詞 prohibitively expensive（貴得令人買唔起）在議論文及投訴信極為地道高分！
example: For many grassroots families, private music lessons and overseas study tours remain prohibitively expensive.

def_zh: （價格或加幅）高昂的、急劇的；（山坡）陡峭的
def_en: of a price or demand not reasonable; excessive, OR rising or falling sharply
prep_trap: 形容詞，一詞三用：steep slopes（陡峭山坡）、a steep rise in rent（租金急升）、steep ticket prices（高昂票價）。
example: Commuters objected strongly to the bus company's proposal for a steep fare increase.

def_zh: 巨額的（罰款或帳單）；沉重龐大的
def_en: of a number or amount impressively large
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 提議重罰違例者時必配：impose a hefty fine on offenders（對違例者處以巨額罰款）！
example: Imposing a hefty fine on illegal waste dumping is the most direct way to deter offenders.

def_zh: 天文數字般的；高得驚人的（樓價、成本或數字）
def_en: of an amount, price, or scale extremely large
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 very high price 的生動高分字（astronomical property prices）。
example: Astronomical property prices in Hong Kong make it almost impossible for young people to buy flats without family help.

def_zh: 負擔得起的；價格相宜的
def_en: inexpensive; reasonably priced
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 affordability（housing affordability 置業負擔能力），民生政策題核心字。
example: School canteens must provide nutritious lunchboxes at an affordable price for all students.

def_zh: 便宜的；花費不多的（褒義，指價廉物美）
def_en: not costing a great deal; cheap
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意 cheap 常帶「劣質廉價」貶義，而 inexpensive / budget-friendly 則是正面的「價格相宜」！
example: Jogging in public parks is an inexpensive yet highly effective way for citizens to stay fit.

def_zh: 具成本效益的；抵買划算的（花的錢少但成效高）
def_en: effective or productive in relation to its cost
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，Paper 2/3 建議書（Proposal）說服校長或政府批出預算的必殺理由：a cost-effective solution！
collocations: prove cost-effective in the long run
example: Preventive health education in schools is a highly cost-effective way to reduce future hospital spending.

def_zh: 經濟實惠的；省錢省能源的；節儉的
def_en: giving good value or service in relation to the amount of money, time, or effort spent; careful not to waste
prep_trap: DSE 極高頻失分陷阱：economical = 慳錢實惠的（an economical electric car）；economic = 國家經濟上的（economic growth）！切勿混淆！
example: Taking public transport is far more economical and environmentally friendly than owning a private car.

def_zh: 經濟上的；與經濟發展相關的
def_en: relating to economics or the economy
prep_trap: 形容詞，必記與 economical 的分別：economic development / downturn（經濟發展/衰退）。
example: Developing eco-tourism in rural areas can create jobs and stimulate local economic growth.

def_zh: 賺大錢的
def_en: profitable
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Green technology is becoming a lucrative industry.

def_zh: 站得住腳的；可維持下去的（論點或局面）
def_en: able to be maintained or defended against attack or objection
prep_trap: 形容詞，其否定形式 untenable（難以為繼的 / 站不住腳的）在議論文更常用：Relying solely on landfills is no longer tenable！
example: With our landfills nearly full, relying solely on burying rubbish is an untenable waste management strategy.

def_zh: 切實可行的；能付諸實行的（計劃或措施）
def_en: able to be done or put into practice successfully
prep_trap: 形容詞，香港政府通告常配 as soon as practicable（在切實可行的範圍內盡快）。
example: Repairs to the damaged sports ground will be completed as soon as practicable.

def_zh: 行得通的；切實可操作的（計劃或折衷方案）
def_en: of a plan, system, or idea capable of producing the desired effect or result; practicable
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 a workable compromise / solution。
example: Consultation with teachers helped the Education Bureau design a workable plan for curriculum reform.

def_zh: 徒勞無功的；白費心機的
def_en: incapable of producing any useful result; pointless
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 futility，常配 a futile attempt / effort（徒勞的嘗試）。
example: Trying to ban teenagers from the internet completely is a futile exercise in the digital age.

def_zh: 毫無成果的；徒勞無功的（搜尋或談判）
def_en: failing to achieve the desired results; unproductive or useless
prep_trap: 形容詞，與 fruitful（碩果累累的）完全相反。
example: Without mutual trust, negotiations between the management and striking workers proved completely fruitless.

def_zh: 徒勞的（in vain）；愛慕虛榮的、自負的
def_en: producing no result; useless, OR having or showing an excessively high opinion of one's appearance, abilities, or worth
prep_trap: DSE 必考片語：in vain（徒勞無功：All our efforts were in vain）；作形容詞指人「愛漂亮虛榮」（名詞為 vanity）。
example: Rescue teams worked through the stormy night so the hikers' calls for help would not be in vain.

def_zh: 多餘的；過剩不必要的（如過度包裝或累贅字眼）
def_en: unnecessary, especially through being more than enough
prep_trap: 形容詞，批評禮品或網購「過度塑膠包裝」（superfluous plastic packaging）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Supermarkets should stop wrapping fruits and vegetables in layers of superfluous plastic packaging.

def_zh: 過度的；過量的（功課、壓力、打機或包裝）
def_en: more than is necessary, normal, or desirable; immoderate
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自名詞 excess（in excess of 超過），DSE 最萬用高頻字：excessive screen time / workload。
example: Excessive screen time before bed is linked to myopia, obesity, and poor sleep among children.

def_zh: 無節制的；過度的（飲食或消費）
def_en: not sensible or restrained; excessive
prep_trap: 形容詞，正面詞為 moderate（適度的）。
example: Immoderate consumption of processed meat and alcohol significantly increases the risk of chronic diseases.

def_zh: 溫和的（氣候）；有節制克制的（言行）
def_en: relating to or denoting a region or climate characterized by mild temperatures, OR showing moderation or self-restraint
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 temperance（節制）。
example: Unlike tropical regions, countries with a temperate climate enjoy four distinct seasons.

def_zh: 適度的；溫和的（運動或飲食）；（作動詞讀 /ˈmɒdəreɪt/：主持討論、緩和）
def_en: average in amount, intensity, quality, or degree
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 moderation，健康生活金句：Everything in moderation（凡事適可而止/均衡適度）！
example: Enjoying desserts occasionally in moderation is fine as long as you maintain an active lifestyle.

def_zh: 適度；節制；溫和
def_en: the avoidance of excess or extremes, especially in one's behavior or political opinions
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必考介詞搭配：in moderation（適度地：play video games in moderation 適度打機）。
example: Video games are not harmful in themselves if teenagers learn to play them in moderation.

def_zh: 克制；自我約束；限制措施
def_en: unemotional, dispassionate, or moderate behavior; self-control
prep_trap: 不可數或可數名詞，源自動詞 restrain（restrain oneself from），必配 exercise self-restraint（保持自制）。
example: Netizens should exercise self-restraint and verify facts before posting angry comments online.

def_zh: 棄權（投票時不投贊成亦不投反對票）；戒除
def_en: an instance of declining to vote for or against a proposal or motion
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，Paper 3 會議紀錄（Minutes）統計票數時常考：5 votes in favour, 1 against, and 2 abstentions。
example: The motion was passed by a majority of eight votes to two, with one abstention.

def_zh: （會議有效進行所需的）法定人數
def_en: the minimum number of members of an assembly or society that must be present at any of its meetings to make the proceedings of that meeting valid
basic_word: minimum number of members for a meeting
prep_trap: 單數名詞，Paper 3 會議紀錄或學會章程常考：reach a quorum（達到法定開會人數）。
example: Because fewer than half of the committee members attended, the meeting lacked a quorum and was postponed.

def_zh: 動議；議案（會議或辯論比賽中提出的表決提案）
def_en: a formal proposal put to a legislature or committee
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 辯論比賽（Today's motion is...）及會議紀錄（propose / second / pass a motion）必考字！
example: In today's debate, our team strongly opposes the motion that homework should be abolished.

def_zh: 不記名投票；選票；抽籤（如公屋或馬拉松抽籤）
def_en: a process of voting, in writing and typically in secret, OR a system of selecting by lot/draw
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，香港常用於 secret ballot（不記名投票選學生會）或 public ballot（抽籤分配名額）。
example: The new Student Union president was elected by all students through a fair secret ballot.

def_zh: 全體投票表決（如全校學生公投決定重大學會事項）
def_en: a general vote by the electorate on a single political question which has been referred to them for a direct decision
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: The Student Union held a campus-wide referendum to decide how to spend the surplus budget.

def_zh: 法令；政令（亦可作動詞：頒令）
def_en: an official order issued by a legal authority
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: Conservation zones were established by official decree to protect ancient woodlands from commercial logging.

def_zh: 暫停令；緩期執行（暫時禁止某活動，如休漁期或暫停填海）
def_en: a temporary prohibition of an activity
prep_trap: 可數名詞，必配介詞 on（impose a moratorium on fishing / land reclamation）。
example: An annual summer fishing moratorium in the South China Sea allows fish stocks to replenish naturally.

def_zh: 禁令；禁運（尤指禁止進口危險食品或野生動物製品）
def_en: an official ban on trade or other commercial activity with a particular country or commodity
prep_trap: 可數名詞，複數為 embargoes，必配介詞 on（impose an embargo on ivory trade）。
example: International embargoes on the ivory trade have helped curb the poaching of African elephants.

def_zh: 杯葛；聯合抵制（不環保、血汗工廠或無良企業的產品，亦可作名詞）
def_en: withdraw from commercial or social relations with a country, organization, or person as a punishment or protest
prep_trap: 及物動詞或可數名詞，DSE 消費者力量（consumer power）題必背：boycott unethical brands！
example: Ethical consumers can use their purchasing power to boycott fast-fashion brands that exploit child labour.

def_zh: 制裁；處罰（複數 sanctions）；官方批准認可（不可數）
def_en: a threatened penalty for disobeying a law or rule, OR official permission or approval for an action
prep_trap: 極奇妙的「正反同形詞」：作可數複數 sanctions 指「制裁/處罰」；作不可數名詞或動詞則指「批准認可」（sanction the proposal）！
example: Schools should impose strict disciplinary sanctions on students who engage in cyberbullying.

def_zh: 正式批准；簽署生效（國際公約、氣候協議或章程修改）
def_en: sign or give formal consent to a treaty, contract, or agreement, making it officially valid
prep_trap: 及物動詞，名詞為 ratification，環保題討論《巴黎氣候協定》（ratify the Paris Agreement）必用。
example: Over one hundred countries ratified the international treaty to reduce global greenhouse gas emissions.

def_zh: 否決（動用否決權駁回提案，亦可作可數名詞）
def_en: exercise a constitutional right to reject a decision or proposal made by a law-making body
prep_trap: 及物動詞或可數名詞（複數為 vetoes），如校長否決高風險活動提案（veto the proposal）。
example: The Principal exercised his right to veto the overnight camping trip due to typhoon warnings.

def_zh: 使無效；使作廢；抵銷（努力或正面效果）
def_en: make legally null and void; invalidate, OR make of no use or value; cancel out
prep_trap: 及物動詞，常指不良生活習慣抵銷了運動的好處（nullify the benefits of exercise）。
example: Drinking two sugary sodas after jogging will completely nullify the calorie-burning benefits of your workout.

def_zh: 抵銷（好處）；否定
def_en: nullify; make ineffective
prep_trap: 及物動詞，DSE 議論文高分動詞：Traffic congestion negates the time-saving advantage of road transport。
example: Leaving air conditioners running in empty rooms negates the school's efforts to save electricity.

def_zh: 抵銷；對抗；消弭（負面影響、壓力或副作用）
def_en: act against something in order to reduce its force or neutralize it
prep_trap: 及物動詞，DSE 提議用正面措施對抗負面影響的 5* 動詞：counteract the negative effects of sedentary work！
example: Stretching for five minutes every hour helps counteract the harmful effects of sitting all day.

def_zh: 中和（酸性或毒素）；抵銷（威脅）
def_en: make an acidic or alkaline substance chemically neutral, or render something ineffective or harmless
prep_trap: 及物動詞（英式亦拼作 neutralise）。
example: Planting more urban trees helps neutralize part of the carbon dioxide emitted by vehicles.

def_zh: 賠償；回報；補償（亦可作動詞）
def_en: compensation or reward given for loss or harm suffered or effort made
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 in recompense for（作為對⋯⋯的補償/回報）。
example: The airline offered affected passengers hotel vouchers in recompense for the twelve-hour flight delay.

def_zh: 歸還原物；賠償損失（尤指犯錯者向受害人作出的賠償）
def_en: the restoration of something lost or stolen to its proper owner, or recompense for injury or loss
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 make restitution to the victim。
example: Young vandals were ordered by the court to clean the walls and make financial restitution.

def_zh: 懲罰；報應（對罪行的嚴懲）
def_en: punishment inflicted on someone as vengeance for a wrong or criminal act
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，討論刑罰目的是「懲罰報應（retribution）」還是「更生教化（rehabilitation）」時的 5** 對比詞！
example: For juvenile offenders, the justice system should focus on education and rehabilitation rather than harsh retribution.

def_zh: 仁慈寬恕；輕判（法官或當局對悔過者的寬大處理）
def_en: mercy; lenience
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 show clemency toward a remorseful offender。
example: The judge showed clemency to the first-time teenage offender because he expressed genuine remorse.

def_zh: 寬大處理；從輕發落；仁慈
def_en: the fact or quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected; clemency
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自形容詞 lenient，常配 treat with leniency（從輕發落）。
example: While first-time mistakes should be treated with leniency, repeated bullying requires firm disciplinary action.

def_zh: 忍耐；克制；寬容包涵（公函感謝市民體諒工程不便的高階字）
def_en: patient self-control; restraint and tolerance
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，Paper 3 道歉或維修通告結尾滿分句：Thank you for your patience and forbearance（感謝閣下的耐心與體諒）！
collocations: thank you for your patience and forbearance
example: We thank all library users for their patience and forbearance during the three-week renovation period.

def_zh: 寬宏大量；大度胸襟
def_en: the fact or condition of being magnanimous; generosity
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自形容詞 magnanimous。
example: Forgiving a teammate who made a crucial error in the final match requires true magnanimity.

def_zh: 謙遜；謙虛美德（切勿與 humiliation「羞辱」混淆！）
def_en: a modest or low view of one's own importance; humbleness
prep_trap: 極重要區分：humility = 謙虛美德（形容詞為 humble）；humiliation = 當眾受辱（動詞為 humiliate）！
example: True champions accept victory with humility and treat every opponent with respect.

def_zh: 謙虛；樸素端莊
def_en: the quality or state of being unassuming or moderate in the estimation of one's abilities
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 modest（既指人「謙虛的」，亦指津貼金額「不算多但有幫助的」a modest fee/stipend！）。
example: To cover the cost of art materials, participants will only need to pay a modest fee of twenty dollars.

def_zh: 傲慢；自大目中無人
def_en: the quality of being arrogantly superior and disdainful
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 arrogant，與 humility / modesty 相反。
example: Confidence is a strength in job interviews, whereas arrogance will quickly turn employers away.

def_zh: 自負；驕傲自滿
def_en: excessive pride in oneself
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意拼字 c 後面是 ei（conceit），形容詞為 conceited（自負自大的）。
example: Despite winning numerous international piano prizes, she remains friendly, humble, and completely free from conceit.

def_zh: 自戀的；自我中心的（如沉迷自拍呃 Like）
def_en: having an excessive or erotic interest in oneself and one's physical appearance
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自名詞 narcissism（自戀），DSE 討論社交媒體自拍文化（selfie culture）必備高分字！
example: Psychologists warn that the obsession with taking filtered selfies fosters a narcissistic culture among youth.

def_zh: 自我中心的；只顧自己不理他人感受的
def_en: thinking only of oneself, without regard for the feelings or desires of others; self-centered
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 selfish / self-centered 的高分心理學詞彙。
example: Team sports teach spoiled children to overcome egocentric habits and cooperate with others.

def_zh: 只顧自己的；陶醉於自己世界而忽略身邊人的
def_en: preoccupied with one's own feelings, interests, or situation
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，批評「低頭族」只顧看手機忽略家人朋友（self-absorbed smartphone users）極貼切。
example: Staring at our phones during family dinners makes us self-absorbed and weakens family bonds.

def_zh: 冷淡疏離的；高高在上不合群的
def_en: not friendly or forthcoming; cool and distant
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 remain aloof from classmates / neighbours。
example: Although the new student seemed aloof at first, we soon realized he was simply shy.

def_zh: 冷淡不友善的；拒人於千里之外的
def_en: distant and cold in manner; unfriendly
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Introverted people are often misunderstood as standoffish when they are actually just nervous in crowds.

def_zh: 和藹可親的；平易近人的；健談友善的
def_en: friendly, good-natured, or easy to talk to
basic_word: friendly and easy to talk to
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫好校長、好導師或鄰居平易近人（an affable principal）的 5* 詞彙。
example: Our new principal is a warm and affable educator who greets students at the school gate every morning.

def_zh: 親切友好的；和煦愉快的（主人或氣氛）
def_en: friendly and cheerful
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 a genial host / atmosphere。
example: The cafe owner is a genial host who knows every regular customer in the neighbourhood by name.

def_zh: 歡樂熱鬧的；融洽盡興的（聚會或節日氣氛）
def_en: of an atmosphere or event friendly, lively, and enjoyable
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫新年盆菜宴、大排檔聚餐或聖誕派對歡樂融洽氣氛（a convivial atmosphere）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Eating hotpot together creates a warm, convivial atmosphere that brings extended families closer.

def_zh: 喧鬧活潑的；精力旺盛吵鬧的（孩童或運動場氣氛）
def_en: of a person, event, or behavior noisy, energetic, and cheerful; rowdy
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫小息時操場上跑跳玩耍的學生（boisterous children）極為生動。
example: During recess, the playground comes alive with the boisterous laughter of primary school children.

def_zh: 頑皮吵鬧難管的；精力過盛的（小孩或小狗）
def_en: uncontrollably exuberant; boisterous
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Outdoor playground games allow rambunctious young children to burn off their boundless energy safely.

def_zh: 不守規矩的；吵鬧難控制的（學生、乘客或人群）
def_en: disorderly and disruptive and not amenable to discipline or control
prep_trap: 形容詞，雖然字尾是 -ly 但屬形容詞（unruly students / passengers），課室秩序與旅遊文明題必用！
example: Airlines have the right to blacklist unruly passengers who verbally abuse cabin crew during flights.

def_zh: 吵鬧滋事的；喧嘩擾民的（深夜酒吧人群或球迷）
def_en: noisy and disorderly
prep_trap: 形容詞，投訴信投訴樓下深夜食肆或酒吧人群喧嘩（rowdy patrons）極貼切。
example: Residents living above late-night bars often complain about rowdy patrons shouting in the street after midnight.

def_zh: 刺耳喧嘩的；粗野嘈吵的（笑聲或派對）
def_en: making or constituting a disturbingly harsh and loud noise
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 raucous laughter / party。
example: Holidaymakers renting village houses should avoid holding raucous late-night parties that disturb local villagers.

def_zh: 震耳欲聾的；刺耳欲裂的（地盤打樁或改裝車噪音）
def_en: extremely loud
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，投訴信形容地盤打樁聲或非法改裝跑車聲浪的生動高分字！
example: The ear-splitting noise from the nearby piling site made it impossible for students to hear the teacher.

def_zh: 震耳欲聾的（噪音或歡呼掌聲）；（沉默）令人極度不安的
def_en: of a noise so loud as to make it impossible to hear anything else
prep_trap: 形容詞，既可負面形容噪音，亦可正面形容運動會歡呼聲（deafening cheers and applause）！
example: As the runners approached the finish line, the stadium erupted into deafening cheers.

def_zh: 刺耳嘈雜的聲音（各種噪音交織而成的混亂聲響）
def_en: a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds
prep_trap: 單數可數名詞，描寫旺角街頭車聲、喇叭聲與廣播聲交織（a cacophony of traffic horns）的 5** 文學詞彙！
example: Stepping into the quiet public library offered instant relief from the cacophony of the busy street outside.

def_zh: 持續刺耳的喧囂噪音（如地盤或繁忙茶餐廳的嘈雜聲）
def_en: a loud, unpleasant, and prolonged noise
prep_trap: 單數名詞，常配 the constant din of traffic / construction。
collocations: above the din of the canteen
example: We could barely hear each other speak above the noisy din of the crowded restaurant.

def_zh: 騷動；混亂喧鬧（突發事件引起的哄動）
def_en: a state of confused and noisy disturbance
prep_trap: 單數或不可數名詞，記敘文開頭描寫突發事件引起圍觀騷動（hear a sudden commotion）的必備字！
example: Hearing a sudden commotion in the corridor, our teacher stepped outside to see what had happened.

def_zh: 大混亂；一片喧嘩失控局面（如偶像現身或突發停電時）
def_en: wild and noisy disorder or confusion; uproar
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必背記敘文金句：Pandemonium broke out when...（當⋯⋯時，全場頓時陷入一片大混亂）！
example: Utter pandemonium broke out in the shopping mall when the pop star unexpectedly appeared on the balcony.

def_zh: 混亂；動盪；（內心的）紛亂煎熬
def_en: a state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必考搭配：emotional turmoil（內心情緒翻騰煎熬）或 economic turmoil（經濟動盪）。
example: Going through parents' divorce places adolescents in deep emotional turmoil that affects their studies.

def_zh: 劇變；大動盪（科技或社會結構帶來的重大改變）
def_en: a violent or sudden change or disruption to something
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，如 AI 對就業市場帶來的劇變（technological upheaval）。
collocations: cause upheaval in the job market
example: The rapid rise of artificial intelligence is causing major upheaval across traditional white-collar industries.

def_zh: 蛻變；徹底轉變（由毛蟲變蝴蝶，比喻青少年的成長蛻變）
def_en: a change of the form or nature of a thing or person into a completely different one
prep_trap: 可數名詞，演講辭或個人反思文章形容中學生六年來的成長蛻變（undergo a remarkable metamorphosis）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Over six years of secondary school, shy Form One children undergo a remarkable metamorphosis into confident young adults.

def_zh: 演變；漸進發展；進化
def_en: the gradual development of something, especially from a simple to a more complex form
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，動詞為 evolve（漸漸演變），與激進突變的 revolution 相對。
example: The museum exhibition traces the fascinating evolution of Hong Kong's public housing estates since the 1950s.

def_zh: 演變；逐步發展（由簡單到複雜）
def_en: develop gradually, especially from a simple to a more complex form
prep_trap: 不及物或及物動詞，必配介詞 from ... into ...（evolve from a fishing village into a financial hub）。
collocations: evolve from a fishing village into
example: In a world of rapidly evolving technology, lifelong learning is the only way to stay competitive.

def_zh: 停滯不前；蕭條（經濟或個人成長）
def_en: the state of not flowing or moving; lack of activity, growth, or development
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，與 evolution / growth 相反。
example: Investing in scientific research and education helps a city avoid long-term economic stagnation.

def_zh: 經濟衰退；不景氣
def_en: a period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity are reduced
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，必配 economic recession（經濟衰退）。
example: During an economic recession, fresh university graduates often take longer to secure full-time employment.

def_zh: 通貨膨脹（物價飛漲、錢變得唔見使）
def_en: a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，香港民生與長者生活津貼題必提：keep pace with rising inflation（追上通脹升幅）！
example: Minimum wage levels should be reviewed annually so low-income workers' salaries can keep pace with inflation.

def_zh: 通貨緊縮（物價下跌、消費意欲低迷）
def_en: reduction of the general level of prices in an economy
basic_word: falling prices in a weak economy
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，與 inflation 相反。
example: Prolonged deflation often reflects weak consumer confidence and sluggish business investment.

def_zh: 購買力（市民手中金錢能買到貨品的能力）
def_en: the financial ability to buy products and services
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，討論通脹削弱基層購買力（erode grassroots citizens' purchasing power）或旅客消費力必用！
example: Distributing electronic consumption vouchers helped boost citizens' purchasing power and supported local restaurants.

def_zh: 津貼；資助（由政府或學校補貼部分費用）
def_en: support an organization or activity financially
prep_trap: 及物動詞（英式亦拼作 subsidise），名詞為 subsidy，DSE 政策建議最常寫：The government should subsidize...！
example: Heavily subsidized public hospital services ensure that no citizen is denied medical care due to poverty.

def_zh: 須經過入息及資產審查的（社會福利或津貼）
def_en: based on an official investigation into a person's financial circumstances to determine whether they are eligible for a welfare payment
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，DSE 討論社會福利應否「全民派發（universal）」還是「設入息審查（means-tested）」的 5** 專業詞彙！
example: To ensure public money goes to those most in need, housing allowances should remain strictly means-tested.

def_zh: 救濟品；政府派錢或綜援救濟金；課堂講義
def_en: something given free to a needy person or organization, OR a printed sheet of information distributed to students
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 扶貧政策金句：Give a man a fish vs teach him to fish（Empowerment is better than mere welfare handouts）！
example: Vocational training empowers the unemployed to become self-reliant rather than relying on government handouts.

def_zh: 自力更生的；獨立自主不依賴他人的
def_en: reliant on one's own powers and resources rather than those of others
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，名詞為 self-reliance（自力更生），青少年成長與扶貧政策題必背高分字！
example: Cooking and laundry tasks at summer camps teach pampered children to become more self-reliant.

def_zh: 自給自足的（能源、食物或經濟上）
def_en: needing no outside help in satisfying one's basic needs, especially with regard to the production of food or energy
basic_word: able to supply one's own needs
prep_trap: 複合形容詞，名詞為 self-sufficiency。
example: Installing solar panels and rainwater harvesting systems makes the eco-school nearly energy self-sufficient.

def_zh: 自主的
def_en: independent
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Schools should encourage autonomous learning.

def_zh: 負有責任的；須向公眾問責交代的
def_en: of a person, organization, or institution required or expected to justify actions or decisions; responsible
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 accountability（問責性），必考介詞：hold somebody accountable TO the public FOR their actions！
example: Social media platforms should be held legally accountable if they fail to remove fraudulent advertisements.

def_zh: 負有法律責任的（配 for）；易於發生某壞事的（配 to do）
def_en: responsible by law; legally answerable, OR likely to do or to be something
prep_trap: Paper 3 通告及條款必考：Participants will be held liable for any damage to equipment（參加者須對損壞器材負責）！
collocations: liable to make mistakes when tired
example: Anyone caught dumping construction waste illegally is liable to a maximum fine of two hundred thousand dollars.

def_zh: 有罪責的；難辭其咎的；應受譴責的
def_en: deserving blame
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 morally or legally culpable（在道德或法律上難辭其咎）。
example: Contractors who use substandard steel in building projects should be held criminally culpable.

def_zh: 無可指責的；清白無辜的
def_en: innocent of wrongdoing
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Pedestrians hit by reckless drunk drivers are blameless victims who deserve full compensation.

def_zh: 無可挑剔的；完美無瑕的（品行、禮儀或英語水平）
def_en: in accordance with the highest standards; faultless
prep_trap: 形容詞，母音開頭配冠詞 an，推薦信讚揚學生操守或語文能力（impeccable manners / English）的 5** 詞彙！
example: With her impeccable English and warm smile, she was chosen as the master of ceremonies for Speech Day.

def_zh: 完美無瑕的（演出、設計或肌膚）
def_en: without any imperfections or defects; perfect
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自名詞 flaw（瑕疵/漏洞），描寫合唱團或體操表演完美無瑕（a flawless performance）極佳。
example: Beauty apps that retouch selfies to create flawless skin give teenagers unrealistic expectations about appearance.

def_zh: 瑕疵；污點（皮膚上的斑點，或紀錄上的污點）
def_en: a small mark or flaw which spoils the appearance of something
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 without a blemish on one's record（履歷毫無污點）。
example: One moment of exam cheating can leave a permanent blemish on a student's academic record.

def_zh: 損害；玷污（聲譽或國際形象）
def_en: lose or cause to lose luster, especially as a result of exposure to air or moisture; damage a good reputation
prep_trap: 及物動詞，DSE 討論黑的宰客或劣質服務如何損害香港「好客之都」聲譽（tarnish Hong Kong's reputation）的必背高分動詞！
example: Unscrupulous pharmacies that overcharge tourists severely tarnish Hong Kong's international reputation as a shopping paradise.

def_zh: 玷污；抹黑（名譽或品格）
def_en: damage the reputation of someone or something in the opinion of others
prep_trap: 及物動詞。
example: Spreading unverified gossip online can unfairly besmirch an innocent teacher's reputation.

def_zh: 污漬；（名譽或良心上的）污點（亦可作動詞）
def_en: a colored patch or dirty mark that is difficult to remove, OR a thing that damages a person's reputation
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: Leaving litter on mountain trails is a stain on our city's civic-mindedness.

def_zh: 將⋯⋯污名化；給⋯⋯貼上羞恥標籤
def_en: describe or regard as worthy of disgrace or great disapproval
prep_trap: 及物動詞（英式亦拼作 stigmatise）。
example: Society must stop stigmatizing vocational education and recognize the value of technical trades.

def_zh: 禁忌；忌諱話題（如死亡、自殺或情緒病，亦可作形容詞）
def_en: a social or religious custom prohibiting or forbidding discussion of a particular practice or topic
prep_trap: 可數名詞或形容詞，常配 break the taboo surrounding mental health / life-and-death education（打破忌諱）。
collocations: break the taboo surrounding mental illness
example: Life-and-death education in schools helps break the traditional cultural taboo surrounding discussions of grief.

def_zh: 迷信；迷信習俗
def_en: excessively credulous belief in and reverence for supernatural beings, or a widely held but unjustified belief
prep_trap: 可數或不可數名詞，形容詞為 superstitious（迷信的）。
example: Abandoning black cats and dogs out of blind superstition is both ignorant and cruel.

def_zh: 傳統習俗；風俗；（複數 Customs：海關；光顧生意）
def_en: a traditional and widely accepted way of behaving or doing something that is specific to a particular society, place, or time
prep_trap: 極易混淆一詞三義：a local custom（地方習俗，可數）；pass through Customs（過海關，大寫複數）；lose custom（流失顧客生意，不可數）！形容詞為 customary。
example: When travelling abroad, tourists should dress appropriately and respect local religious customs.

def_zh: 按傳統習俗的；慣常的
def_en: according to the customs or usual practices associated with a particular society, place, or set of circumstances
prep_trap: 形容詞，結構：It is customary for Chinese families to...（華人家庭按傳統習俗會⋯⋯）。
collocations: it is customary to give red packets
example: During Lunar New Year, it is customary for married adults to give red packets to children.

def_zh: 儀式；祭祀典禮；每天必做的習慣程序
def_en: a religious or solemn ceremony consisting of a series of actions performed according to a prescribed order
prep_trap: 可數名詞，既可指傳統節慶儀式（traditional festive rituals，如大坑舞火龍），亦可指睡前放鬆習慣（a bedtime ritual）。
example: The Tai Hang Fire Dragon Dance is a century-old ritual performed every Mid-Autumn Festival.

def_zh: 盛大巡遊慶典（如長洲飄色巡遊）；選美比賽（beauty pageant）
def_en: a public entertainment consisting of a procession of people in elaborate, colorful costumes
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港長洲太平清醮「飄色巡遊」英文正是 Piu Sik Floating Colours Pageant / Parade！
example: Thousands of spectators line the narrow streets of Cheung Chau to watch the colourful floating pageant.

def_zh: 巡遊隊伍；行列（節慶、畢業禮或宗教巡遊）
def_en: a number of people or vehicles moving forward in an orderly fashion, especially as part of a ceremony or festival
prep_trap: 可數名詞，如畢業典禮進場行列（academic procession）或太平清醮巡遊隊伍。
example: Drummers and lion dancers led a lively procession through the village to celebrate the festival.

def_zh: 節日慶典；狂歡盛會（常用於音樂節、美食節或文化日名稱）
def_en: an event marked by festivities or celebration
prep_trap: 可數名詞，Paper 2/3 為學校活動命名時的亮眼詞彙：Annual Music Fiesta / Cultural Fiesta！
example: Our Student Union is organizing a vibrant Cultural Fiesta featuring food stalls and traditional dances.

def_zh: 盛大精彩的表演盛會（如大型音樂劇或綜藝晚會）
def_en: an elaborate and spectacular entertainment or production
prep_trap: 可數名詞，宣傳海報或演講介紹學校大型綜藝匯演（a musical extravaganza）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Our fortieth anniversary concert promises to be an unforgettable musical extravaganza for parents and alumni.

def_zh: 壯觀場面；視覺盛宴；（複數 spectacles：眼鏡）
def_en: a visually striking performance or display
prep_trap: 可數名詞，形容維港煙花或無人機匯演（a dazzling visual spectacle）極佳；形容詞為 spectacular。
example: The synchronized drone show over Victoria Harbour created a dazzling visual spectacle in the night sky.

def_zh: 盛大華麗的儀式場面
def_en: elaborate display or ceremony
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，描寫傳統節慶或奧運開幕禮盛況（colourful pageantry）。
example: Tourists are fascinated by the colourful pageantry of Cantonese opera costumes and lion dances.

def_zh: （餐廳、書店或場地的）氣氛、環境格調
def_en: the character and atmosphere of a place
prep_trap: 單數或不可數名詞（亦拼作 ambiance），餐廳評論或提議改造學校閱讀角（create a cosy ambience）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Soft warm lighting and potted plants give the renovated school library a cosy, relaxing ambience.

def_zh: 氣質；氣場；獨特氛圍
def_en: the distinctive atmosphere or quality that seems to surround and be generated by a person, thing, or place
basic_word: special air or feeling around someone/place
prep_trap: 單數名詞，配 an aura of calm / mystery / confidence。
example: Experienced debaters exude an aura of calm confidence even when challenged with difficult questions.

def_zh: 氛圍；感覺（校園校報、Blog 或非正式書信極地道用字）
def_en: a person's emotional state or the atmosphere of a place as communicated to and felt by others
prep_trap: 可數名詞（常用複數 good vibes 或 a welcoming vibe），適合 Blog、校刊文章或對同學演講。
example: Decorating the student common room with beanbags and student artwork created a warm, welcoming vibe.

def_zh: 親近感；共鳴；天生的喜愛與天分
def_en: a spontaneous or natural liking or sympathy for someone or something
prep_trap: 單數名詞，必配介詞 for 或 with（have a natural affinity for animals / music 對動物/音樂有天生親近感）。
collocations: feel a close affinity with nature
example: Children who grow up with pets develop a lifelong affinity for animals and nature.

def_zh: 親情
def_en: family tie
prep_trap: 不可數名詞。
example: Festivals strengthen kinship ties.

def_zh: 夥伴情誼；團契；大學研究獎學金
def_en: friendly association, especially with people who share one's interests, OR a postgraduate research grant
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（情誼）或可數名詞（研究基金獎學金）。
example: Volunteering together on weekends offers retirees warm fellowship and a renewed sense of purpose.

def_zh: 戰友般的情誼；同甘共苦的團隊友情
def_en: the company and friendship of others with common aims
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，與 camaraderie 同義，描寫制服團隊（童軍 Scouts、紅十字會）或運動隊友極佳。
example: Overcoming tough hiking challenges together forged a lifelong bond of comradeship among the scouts.

def_zh: 悉心指導；栽培（在名師或前輩門下學習）
def_en: instruction; tuition; protection of or authority over someone
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必配介詞 under：under the tutelage of our dedicated coach/teacher（在教練/老師的悉心指導下），演講感謝師長 5** 片語！
example: Under the patient tutelage of our choir conductor, we won first prize in the Music Festival.

def_zh: 庇護；贊助支持；主辦領導（正式公函片語）
def_en: the protection, backing, or support of a particular person or organization
prep_trap: 必背正式片語：under the aegis of（在某機構的主辦/支持下，如 organized under the aegis of the Education Bureau）。
collocations: organized under the aegis of the Student Union
medical charity under the aegis of
example: The inter-school STEM competition was organized under the aegis of the Hong Kong Science Museum.

def_zh: 贊助；主辦；支持（必配 under the auspices of）
def_en: with the help, support, or protection of someone or something
prep_trap: 複數形式名詞，Paper 3 活動報告或正式演講極高級句型：held under the auspices of（在⋯⋯的主辦及贊助下舉行）！
collocations: under the auspices of the PTA
charity event under the auspices of
example: The community health fair was successfully held under the auspices of the District Council.

def_zh: 惠顧
def_en: customer support
prep_trap: 不可數名詞。
example: Thank you for your continued patronage.

def_zh: 守護管理
def_en: care
prep_trap: 不可數名詞。
example: Good stewardship of public funds is vital.

def_zh: 守護職責；保管責任（如這一代人對古蹟與大自然的守護）
def_en: the state of being a custodian; guardianship and care
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，守護者為 custodian（custodians of our cultural heritage 文化遺產的守護者）。
example: Every generation holds temporary custodianship of the Earth and must pass it unspoiled to posterity.

def_zh: 信託管理；託管職責
def_en: the office or function of a trustee; care of resources held in trust
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，校董或慈善基金信託人為 trustee（Board of Trustees 信託委員會）。
example: The scholarship endowment is managed by an independent board of trustees to ensure fairness.

def_zh: 問責制；問責性；責任感
def_en: the fact or condition of being accountable; responsibility
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 討論政府施政、慈善機構監管或 AI 決策責任時必用：public accountability！
example: Strict auditing rules ensure financial accountability among non-governmental organizations receiving public donations.

def_zh: 透明度
def_en: openness
prep_trap: 不可數名詞。
example: Greater transparency builds public trust.

def_zh: 品行端正；廉潔公正
def_en: morally correct behavior or thinking; righteousness
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 moral rectitude。
example: Judges and civil servants are expected to uphold the highest standards of moral rectitude.

def_zh: 坦率；真誠直言（不隱瞞問題，開誠布公溝通）
def_en: the quality of being open and honest in expression; frankness
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（美式拼作 candor），形容詞為 candid（坦誠的 / 抓拍自然的 a candid conversation / photo）！
example: A candid discussion between parents and teenagers helps resolve misunderstandings before they escalate.

def_zh: 坦誠直言的；（照片）自然抓拍不造作的
def_en: truthful and straightforward; frank, OR of a photograph taken informally without the subject's knowledge
prep_trap: 形容詞，一詞兩用：a candid exchange of views（坦誠交流意見）及 candid snapshots（自然抓拍的生活照）。
example: Unlike heavily edited studio portraits, candid snapshots capture the genuine joy of school sports day.

def_zh: 直截了當的；坦率果斷的（發表意見）
def_en: of a person or their manner or speech direct and outspoken; straightforward and honest
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 forthright views / manner。
example: We appreciated the guest speaker's forthright answers to students' tough questions about career stress.

def_zh: 直言不諱的；敢言的（敢於公開批評時弊或發聲）
def_en: frank in stating one's opinions, especially if they are critical or controversial
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 an outspoken critic / advocate（敢言的批評者/倡議者）。
example: She has long been an outspoken advocate for improving barrier-free transport facilities for wheelchair users.

def_zh: 大聲疾呼的；積極發聲表達意見的；（聲樂的）
def_en: expressing opinions or feelings freely or loudly, OR relating to the human voice
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配介詞 in 或 about：be vocal in opposing / supporting something（積極發聲反對/支持某事）。
example: Environmental groups have been increasingly vocal in calling for a ban on styrofoam food boxes.

def_zh: 沉默寡言的；不願吐露心事的（如受欺凌或抑鬱的青少年）
def_en: not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily
basic_word: quiet and unwilling to share feelings
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 reticence，常配介詞 about（be reticent about one's family problems），青少年心理輔導題高分字！
example: Teenage boys are often reticent about their emotional struggles because they fear appearing weak.

def_zh: 生性沉默寡言的；不苟言笑的
def_en: of a person reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little
prep_trap: 形容詞，記敘文描寫寡言卻默默付出的父親（my taciturn father）極具文學感染力！
example: Although my father is a taciturn man of few words, he shows his love by cooking for me every night.

def_zh: 內斂矜持的；慢熱害羞的；（座位）已預留的
def_en: slow to reveal emotion or opinions, OR kept specially for a particular person
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 shy 的溫和得體字（quiet and reserved students）。
collocations: priority seats reserved for the elderly
example: Drama workshops help quiet and reserved students step out of their comfort zone and express themselves.

def_zh: 拘謹放不開的；因怕出醜而不敢開口的
def_en: unable to act in a relaxed and natural way because of self-consciousness or mental restraint
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自動詞 inhibit（阻礙/抑制），相反詞為 uninhibited（無拘無束放膽表達的）。
example: Fear of making grammar mistakes often leaves local students feeling inhibited during English oral lessons.

def_zh: 缺乏自信的；羞怯退縮的
def_en: modest or shy because of a lack of self-confidence
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意與 different（不同的）拼字區分！名詞為 diffidence。
example: Encouraging words from a caring teacher can transform a diffident child into a confident learner.

def_zh: 膽怯的；羞怯的
def_en: showing a lack of courage or confidence; easily frightened
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 timidity。
example: Joining the cub scouts helped the timid primary school boy develop courage and independence.

def_zh: 大膽創新的；敢於冒險突破的；（無禮放肆的）
def_en: showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 audacity，形容大膽創新的計劃（an audacious plan / vision）極具氣勢。
example: Setting an audacious goal of zero campus food waste inspired students to rethink their eating habits.

def_zh: 無畏的；勇敢剛毅的（探險家或攀山者）
def_en: fearless; adventurous
prep_trap: 形容詞，描寫野外考察（expeditions）或極地探險家的 5** 詞彙！
example: The documentary follows a team of intrepid student explorers trekking across the Gobi Desert.

def_zh: 英勇無畏的；頑強不屈的（救援人員或努力）
def_en: possessing or showing courage or determination
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 make a valiant effort（作出頑強英勇的努力，如消防員救火或球隊逆境奮戰）。
example: Citizens applauded the valiant firefighters who risked their lives to rescue trapped residents from the blaze.

def_zh: 英勇的；英雄般的（救人行為或抗疫前線）
def_en: having the characteristics of a hero or heroine; very brave
prep_trap: 形容詞，副詞為 heroically（注意加 -ally）。
example: Passers-by praised the off-duty lifeguard for his heroic rescue of a drowning child.

def_zh: 英勇的；雖敗猶榮頑強奮戰的
def_en: of a person or their behavior brave; heroic
prep_trap: 形容詞，體育比賽報告形容落敗一方頑強到底（put up a gallant fight）極佳！
example: Although our football team lost by one goal, they put up a gallant fight against the defending champions.

def_zh: 無所畏懼的；百折不撓的
def_en: showing fearlessness and determination
prep_trap: 形容詞，與 daunting（令人卻步的）同字根。
example: With dauntless courage, the wheelchair fencer overcame her physical disability to win multiple gold medals.

def_zh: 不屈不撓的；永不言敗的（意志或精神）
def_en: impossible to subdue or defeat
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 描寫殘奧運動員（Paralympic athletes）或獅子山精神必背 5** 詞組：an indomitable spirit！
example: Paralympic athletes inspire the whole city with their indomitable spirit and refusal to give up.

def_zh: 堅定不屈的；頑強不妥協的
def_en: of a mass or structure not giving way to pressure; hard or solid; resolute
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自動詞 yield（屈服）。
example: Schools must maintain an unyielding stance against campus bullying and illegal drugs.

def_zh: 堅決果斷的；意志堅定的
def_en: admirably purposeful, determined, and unwavering
prep_trap: 形容詞，與名詞 resolution（決心 / 新年目標 New Year's resolution）同字根。
example: Faced with rising youth vaping rates, health authorities took resolute action to ban e-cigarettes.

def_zh: 果斷的（領袖）；決定性的（因素或勝利）
def_en: settling an issue; producing a definite result, OR having or showing the ability to make decisions quickly and effectively
prep_trap: 形容詞，相反詞為 indecisive（優柔寡斷的），DSE 必考兩義：a decisive leader（果斷的領袖）及 play a decisive role（起決定性作用）！
example: Quick and decisive action by the school nurse saved the student suffering from a severe peanut allergy.

def_zh: 優柔寡斷的；猶豫不決的
def_en: not settling an issue, OR not having or showing the ability to make decisions quickly and effectively
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Career counselling workshops help indecisive Form Six students clarify their strengths before submitting JUPAS choices.

def_zh: 搖擺不定；猶豫不決（在兩個選擇之間左右搖擺）
def_en: alternate or waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，注意雙寫 l，配介詞 between（vacillate between science and arts）。
example: Many students vacillate between pursuing their artistic dreams and choosing a stable business degree.

def_zh: 動搖；猶豫不決（決心或信心動搖）
def_en: shake with a quivering motion; become weaker; falter
prep_trap: 不及物動詞，注意與「豁免」waive（waive the registration fee）同音異字！
example: Despite losing the first two sets, the table tennis player's confidence never wavered.

def_zh: 豁免；免除（費用、學費或規定要求）
def_en: refrain from insisting on or using a right or claim; dispense with a fee or requirement
prep_trap: 及物動詞，Paper 3 必考高分商業及行政字：waive the registration/membership fee for needy students（豁免基層學生的報名費/會費）！名詞為 fee waiver。
collocations: apply for a tuition fee waiver
example: To encourage wide participation, the organizing committee decided to waive the entry fee for full-time students.

def_zh: 獲豁免的（亦可作動詞：豁免某人不用做某事）
def_en: free from an obligation or liability imposed on others
prep_trap: 形容詞或動詞，必考介詞：be exempt FROM paying the fee / PE lessons（獲豁免交費/不用上體育堂），名詞為 exemption！
example: Students with a doctor's certificate are exempt from running the cross-country race.

def_zh: 必須履行的；強制性的；慣例必做的
def_en: required by a legal, moral, or other rule; compulsory
prep_trap: 形容詞，與 compulsory / mandatory 同義，源自動詞 oblige（名詞為 obligation 責任義務）。
example: Attending the pre-camp safety briefing is obligatory for all students joining the kayaking trip.

def_zh: 酌情決定的；可自由支配的（如校方酌情收生學額或零用錢）
def_en: available for use at the discretion of the user
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自名詞 discretion（at the principal's discretion 由校長酌情決定），香港中學「自行分配學位」即 discretionary places！
example: Secondary schools interview primary six applicants competing for limited discretionary places every spring.

def_zh: 武斷的；隨意任性的（不按公平客觀標準的決定或校規）
def_en: based on random choice or personal whim, rather than any reason or system
prep_trap: 形容詞，批評學校或上司「武斷不講理的規定」（arbitrary rules / decisions）時極精準。
example: Students respect discipline rules when they are fair and logical rather than arbitrary.

def_zh: 變幻莫測的；反覆無常的（天氣或脾氣）
def_en: given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behavior; unpredictable
prep_trap: 形容詞，形容春季或山區天氣瞬息萬變（capricious mountain weather）極佳。
example: Hikers must pack waterproof jackets because mountain weather in spring is notoriously capricious.

def_zh: 不規律的；忽好忽壞不穩定的（作息時間、駕駛行為或表現）
def_en: not even or regular in pattern or movement; unpredictable
prep_trap: 形容詞，DSE 健康生活題討論輪班工作或熬夜導致「作息飲食不規律」（erratic sleeping and eating habits）必用！
example: Shift workers often suffer from digestive problems due to erratic meal times and disrupted sleep.

def_zh: 零星的；偶爾發生的（運動習慣或個案，不夠持之以恆）
def_en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated
prep_trap: 形容詞，強調溫習或運動必須持之以恆（consistent），而非「三分鐘熱度偶爾做一次」（sporadic efforts）！
example: Consistent daily revision is far more effective for memory retention than sporadic last-minute cramming.

def_zh: 間歇性的
def_en: stopping and starting
prep_trap: 形容詞。
example: Heavy intermittent rain delayed the tennis match.

def_zh: 按時間先後順序排列的（報告、履歷或歷史事件）
def_en: of a record of events starting with the earliest and following the order in which they occurred
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意 ch 發 /k/ 音，Paper 3 撰寫事件調查報告或進度表必配：in chronological order（按時間順序）！
example: Please list the events leading up to the laboratory accident in strict chronological order.

def_zh: 按次序的；循序漸進的（學習步驟）
def_en: forming or following in a logical order or sequence
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自名詞 sequence（次序/順序）。
example: Coding teaches children how to break complex problems down into logical, sequential steps.

def_zh: 同時發生的；同步進行的（如即時傳譯 simultaneous interpretation）
def_en: occurring, operating, or done at the same time
prep_trap: 形容詞，副詞為 simultaneously（同時地）。
example: AI-powered translation earbuds can provide nearly simultaneous interpretation for international travellers.

def_zh: 同時進行的；並行的（兩個活動或工作坊同時在不同房間舉行）
def_en: existing, happening, or done at the same time
prep_trap: 形容詞，副詞為 concurrently，Paper 3 活動流程表（Programme Rundown）常有 concurrent workshops（同時段並行工作坊）！
example: Three concurrent career workshops will be held in classrooms 3A, 3B, and 3C after the main talk.

def_zh: 同步的；協調一致的（如無人機編隊、花樣游泳或雲端同步）
def_en: caused to occur or operate at the same time or rate
prep_trap: 分詞形容詞，動詞為 synchronize。
example: A fleet of one thousand synchronized drones formed glowing Chinese characters above Victoria Harbour.

def_zh: 無縫銜接的；流暢順滑的（轉乘、數碼體驗或過渡）
def_en: smooth and continuous, with no apparent gaps or spaces between one part and the next
prep_trap: 形容詞，副詞為 seamlessly，DSE 讚揚公共交通轉乘或科技整合（seamless integration）的 5** 詞彙！
collocations: seamless transition from primary to secondary
example: Smart mobility apps allow commuters to plan a seamless journey across railways, buses, and ferries.

def_zh: 順暢無阻的（電子支付體驗）；無摩擦的
def_en: having no friction; effortlessly smooth and easy, especially in digital transactions
prep_trap: 形容詞，討論電子支付（Octopus / Apple Pay）為何令人不知不覺使多咗錢（frictionless payments encourage overspending）的精妙詞彙！
example: While frictionless mobile payments are convenient, they remove the psychological pain of handing over physical cash.

def_zh: 無所不在的（如智能手機、廣告或閉路電視）
def_en: widely or constantly encountered; common or widespread
prep_trap: 形容詞，與 ubiquitous 同義，母音開頭配冠詞 an。
example: In the digital age, omnipresent social media notifications make it difficult for students to disconnect.

def_zh: 無法逃避的；不可避免的（現實或結論）
def_en: unable to be avoided or denied
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 an inescapable conclusion / reality。
example: An ageing population is an inescapable demographic reality that Hong Kong must prepare for today.

def_zh: 即將來臨的；逼近的（通常指考試、危機或風暴）
def_en: of an event regarded as threatening or significant about to happen; forthcoming
prep_trap: 形容詞，只作定語，常配 impending public examinations / crisis（即將來臨的公開試/危機）。
example: As the impending HKDSE examinations drew nearer, the school study room became packed every afternoon.

def_zh: 逼近眼前的；隱約顯現並令人擔憂的（危機、截止日期或能源短缺）
def_en: of something unwanted or unpleasant about to happen soon and causing worry
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自動詞 loom（loom large 構成重大憂慮），常配 a looming landfill crisis / deadline！
example: With our landfills nearing capacity, Hong Kong is facing a looming waste disposal crisis.

def_zh: 即將舉行的（活動）；樂於提供協助或資訊的（作表語）
def_en: planned for or about to happen in the near future, OR willing to divulge information
prep_trap: 形容詞，Paper 3 通告開頭替換 upcoming 的正式字：our forthcoming Annual Sports Day（即將舉行的陸運會）！
example: I am writing to invite parents to attend our forthcoming Speech Day on the twentieth of November.

def_zh: 未來的；準⋯⋯；潛在的（如準大學生、潛在僱主或家長）
def_en: expected or expecting to be something particular in the future
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意切勿與 perspective（觀點角度）混淆！學校開放日（Open Day）歡迎「準學生及家長」即 prospective students and parents！
example: Our Annual School Open Day gives Primary Six prospective students and their parents a taste of secondary campus life.

def_zh: 嶄露頭角的；未來的（小小科學家、年輕藝術家或作家）
def_en: of a person beginning to develop or show signs of future success in a particular area
prep_trap: 形容詞，只作定語，原指「含苞待放的」，Paper 2/3 宣傳學校創科或藝術比賽時稱呼參賽同學為 budding scientists / artists 極為親切生動！
example: The inter-school STEM fair provides a stage for budding young scientists to showcase their inventions.

def_zh: 初創的；剛起步羽翼未豐的（新興行業、初創企業或新學會）
def_en: of a person or organization immature, inexperienced, or underdeveloped; emerging
prep_trap: 形容詞或可數名詞（原指剛學飛的幼鳥），形容本地初創企業（fledgling start-ups）或新成立的學會極貼切！
example: Government seed funding helps fledgling local tech start-ups survive their difficult first two years.

def_zh: 初生的；剛萌芽興起的（新科技或新產業，如氫能或低空經濟）
def_en: especially of a process or organization just coming into existence and beginning to display signs of future potential
prep_trap: 形容詞，形容新興產業（the nascent green hydrogen industry）。
example: Clear safety regulations are needed to guide the growth of the nascent drone delivery industry.

def_zh: 迅速發展的；蓬勃增長的（市場、人口或興趣）
def_en: beginning to grow or increase rapidly; flourishing
prep_trap: 形容詞，替換 fast-growing 的 5** 詞彙（the burgeoning silver-hair market 蓬勃發展的銀髮市場）！
example: With an ageing population, businesses are tapping into the burgeoning market for elderly healthcare products.

def_zh: 繁榮興旺的；茁壯成長的
def_en: prosperous and growing; flourishing
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自動詞 thrive（thrive on challenge 在挑戰中茁壯成長）。
example: Turning old piers into weekend craft markets can create a thriving waterfront community space.

def_zh: 蓬勃發展的；急速興旺的（行業或旅遊業）；（聲音）洪亮的
def_en: having a period of great prosperity or rapid economic growth
prep_trap: 形容詞，常配 booming e-commerce / tourism industry。
example: As more young couples choose to raise pets instead of children, the local pet care industry is booming.

def_zh: 欣欣向榮的；繁茂昌盛的（文化藝術或生態）
def_en: developing rapidly and successfully; thriving
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自動詞 flourish。
example: The West Kowloon Cultural District has transformed reclaimed land into a flourishing centre for performing arts.

def_zh: 繁榮富強的；富裕興旺的（社會或經濟）
def_en: successful in material terms; flourishing financially
prep_trap: 形容詞，名詞為 prosperity（stability and prosperity 穩定繁榮），動詞為 prosper。
example: A well-educated and healthy workforce is the foundation of a prosperous and inclusive society.

def_zh: 活力；朝氣與生機（城市或文化）
def_en: the state of being full of energy and life
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自形容詞 vibrant。
example: Organizing night bazaars and street performances helps inject new vibrancy into older districts.

def_zh: 生命力；活力；生機（個人精力或城市經濟活力）
def_en: the state of being strong and active; energy
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，與 revitalize（活化）同字根，常配 youthful vitality（青春活力）。
example: Adequate sleep and outdoor sports fill teenagers with youthful vitality and optimism.

def_zh: 精力；活力；幹勁
def_en: physical strength and good health; effort, energy, and enthusiasm
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（美式拼作 vigor），形容詞為 vigorous。
example: After a relaxing summer holiday, students returned to school with renewed vigour for the new academic year.

def_zh: 熱情活力；神采飛揚的氣勢（表演、演講或藝術創作）
def_en: vigor and spirit or enthusiasm, especially in artistic performance
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，讚賞戲劇或舞蹈表演充滿活力感染力（perform with energy and verve）的 5** 詞彙！
example: The student dancers performed their hip-hop routine with such infectious energy and verve that the crowd cheered.

def_zh: 自信瀟灑的風采；神采奕奕的表現風格
def_en: flamboyant confidence of style or manner
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意 ch 發 /ʃ/ 音（讀 /pəˈnæʃ/）。
example: The student union president hosted the talent show with humour, confidence, and panache.

def_zh: 沉著自信；泰然自若的風度（在壓力或突發狀況下依然鎮定得體）
def_en: self-confidence or assurance, especially when in a demanding situation
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，注意字尾 b 不發音（讀 /əˈplɒm/），必配 handle tough questions with aplomb！
example: Even when challenged by the judges during the Q&A session, our debate captain answered every question with aplomb.

def_zh: 平和鎮定；處變不驚的心理素質
def_en: mental calmness, composure, and evenness of temper, especially in a difficult situation
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容在公開試壓力或逆境下保持心境平靜（accept setbacks with equanimity）。
example: Practising mindfulness meditation helps students maintain inner equanimity during the stressful examination season.

def_zh: 寧靜；安詳平和（自然環境或內心世界）
def_en: the state of being calm, peaceful, and untroubled
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自形容詞 serene。
example: Listening to the gentle waves on a quiet outlying island brings a deep sense of serenity.

def_zh: 寧靜；靜謐（郊野公園或寺廟的清幽環境）
def_en: the quality or state of being tranquil; calm
prep_trap: 不可數名詞（美式單寫 l：tranquility），常配 peace and tranquillity。
collocations: enjoy the tranquillity of country parks
example: Loud music from portable speakers shatters the peace and tranquillity of country park campsites.

def_zh: 綠洲；（鬧市中的）清幽避風港
def_en: a fertile spot in a desert where water is found, OR a pleasant or peaceful area or period in the midst of a difficult, troubled, or hectic place or situation
basic_word: peaceful green refuge in a city
prep_trap: 可數名詞，複數為 oases，DSE 形容香港公園、九龍公園或圖書館為「鬧市綠洲」（an urban oasis）的滿分比喻！
collocations: oasis of calm in a bustling city
example: Hong Kong Park serves as a peaceful green oasis right in the middle of towering commercial skyscrapers.

def_zh: 避風港；安全庇護所
def_en: a place of safety or refuge
prep_trap: 可數名詞，常配 a safe haven for wildlife / distressed youth（野生動物/受困青年的安全避風港）。
example: Community youth centres serve as a welcoming safe haven for teenagers whose homes are cramped or noisy.

def_zh: 庇護；避難所（常配 seek / take refuge）
def_en: a condition of being safe or sheltered from pursuit, danger, or trouble
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必背片語：seek / take refuge from the storm（躲避風暴），難民則為可數名詞 refugee。
example: During sudden summer thunderstorms, hikers often take refuge inside country park pavilions.

def_zh: 政治或人道庇護
def_en: the protection granted by a nation to someone who has left their native country as a political refugee
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，常配 asylum seekers（尋求庇護者）。
example: Humanitarian charities provide food and legal advice to vulnerable asylum seekers living in the city.

def_zh: 外籍旅居人士；派駐海外工作的專業人士（簡稱 expat）
def_en: a person who lives outside their native country
prep_trap: 可數名詞，香港作為國際都會，討論吸引外籍專才（attract expatriates / overseas talent）必用！
example: International schools and a low tax rate help Hong Kong attract skilled expatriates from around the world.

def_zh: 移居外國的人（從本港遷出，動詞為 emigrate，名詞為 emigration）
def_en: a person who leaves their own country in order to settle permanently in another
prep_trap: 注意區分：emigrate FROM a place（移出，e- 表出）vs immigrate TO a place（移入，im- 表入）！
example: Some young professionals choose to emigrate overseas in search of larger living spaces and a slower pace of life.

def_zh: 移民外地（遷出潮，常導致人才流失 brain drain）
def_en: the act of leaving one's own country to settle permanently in another; moving abroad
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 討論香港人才流失（brain drain caused by emigration）及搶人才政策時必用。
example: Top-talent visa schemes aim to replenish the local workforce and offset the impact of recent emigration.

def_zh: 移居入境；入境事務處（Immigration Department）
def_en: the action of coming to live permanently in a foreign country
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，新來港人士為 new immigrants（可數），過關入境櫃位為 immigration counter。
example: Automated e-channels at border control points allow residents to clear immigration in just seconds.

def_zh: 移居者；外籍勞工（如外籍家庭傭工 migrant domestic workers）
def_en: a worker who moves from one region or country to another in search of work
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 討論香港三十多萬外籍家庭傭工權益時，官方標準寫法正是 migrant domestic workers！
example: Migrant domestic workers make an immense contribution by caring for children and frail seniors in Hong Kong.

def_zh: 海外僑民群體（散居世界各地的華人或港人社群）
def_en: the dispersion or spread of any people from their original homeland
prep_trap: 單數名詞，常配 the overseas Chinese diaspora（海外華人僑民社群）。
example: Lunar New Year celebrations in Chinatowns worldwide unite the global Chinese diaspora.

def_zh: 同胞
def_en: a fellow citizen or national of a country
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: When natural disasters strike, citizens generously donate money to help their affected compatriots.

def_zh: 世界主義；國際都會多元包容精神
def_en: the ideology that all human beings belong to a single community, based on a shared morality and cultural openness
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，源自形容詞 cosmopolitan。
example: Hong Kong's vibrant arts festivals and international cuisine reflect its proud spirit of cosmopolitanism.

def_zh: 多元文化主義（尊重並保存不同種族文化共融）
def_en: the presence of, or support for the presence of, several distinct cultural or ethnic groups within a society
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 multicultural（a multicultural society 多元文化社會），少數族裔共融題必備！
example: Hosting an International Food Fair at school is a joyful way to celebrate multiculturalism on campus.

def_zh: 民族自我中心的（只以自己文化標準評斷其他文化）
def_en: evaluating other peoples and cultures according to the standards of one's own culture
basic_word: judging other cultures by one's own
prep_trap: 形容詞，海外交流團（cultural exchange tours）能幫助學生擺脫狹隘的 ethnocentric mindset。
example: Participating in overseas cultural exchange programmes helps students overcome narrow ethnocentric biases.

def_zh: 思想狹隘排外的；固步自封不關心外間世界的（原指島嶼的）
def_en: ignorant of or uninterested in cultures, ideas, or peoples outside one's own experience
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意切勿與 insulation（隔熱）混淆！批評青少年只顧自己小圈子、不關心國際時事（an insular mindset）的 5** 詞彙！
example: Reading international news every day prevents students from developing an insular and narrow-minded worldview.

def_zh: 目光狹隘的；只顧地方小利益而忽略大局的
def_en: having a limited or narrow outlook or scope
prep_trap: 形容詞，注意 ch 發 /k/ 音，常與 global vision（國際視野）作對比。
example: As an international metropolis, our students must cultivate a global vision rather than a parochial mentality.

def_zh: 目光短淺的；短視近利的（政策或決定）；患近視的
def_en: nearsighted, OR lacking imagination, foresight, or intellectual insight
prep_trap: 形容詞，源自名詞 myopia（近視），DSE 議論文批評「只顧眼前利益而破壞環境」為 myopic decision（短視的決定）極具文采！
example: Sacrificing country parks for short-term commercial gain is a deeply myopic approach to land planning.

def_zh: 有遠見的；深謀遠慮的（政策或領袖）
def_en: showing a prudent awareness of future possibilities; visionary
prep_trap: 形容詞（亦加連字號 far-sighted），與 short-sighted / myopic 相反，名詞為 foresight（遠見，不可數）！
example: Building the mass transit railway decades ago was a farsighted decision that shaped modern Hong Kong.

def_zh: 遠見；先見之明
def_en: the ability to predict what will happen or be needed in the future
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，切勿與 oversight（監管/疏忽）混淆！常配 have the foresight to do something。
example: Town planners must show strategic foresight by reserving green open spaces in new housing developments.

def_zh: 事後聰明；事後回顧檢討（必配 in hindsight / with the benefit of hindsight）
def_en: understanding of a situation or event only after it has happened or developed
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，DSE 個人反思或檢討報告黃金句頭：In hindsight, we should have...（事後回看，我們當初應該⋯⋯）！
example: In hindsight, our organizing committee should have prepared a wet-weather contingency plan for the picnic.

def_zh: 回顧；回想過去（必配 in retrospect）
def_en: a survey or review of a past course of events or period of time
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，必考固定片語：in retrospect（回想起來，與 in hindsight 同義），形容詞為 retrospective。
example: In retrospect, losing that debate competition in Form Three was the best lesson I ever learned.

def_zh: 內省；自我反省與審視內心
def_en: the examination or observation of one's own mental and emotional processes
prep_trap: 不可數名詞，形容詞為 introspective，寫日記（journaling）或獨處能促進 quiet introspection。
example: Keeping a personal diary encourages quiet introspection and helps teenagers understand their own emotions.

def_zh: 頓悟；恍然大悟的一刻（記敘文主角醒覺轉折點）
def_en: a moment of sudden and great revelation or realization
prep_trap: 可數名詞，記敘文（Short Story）描寫主角經歷某事件後「突然大徹大悟」（have a sudden epiphany）的 5** 奪星字！
example: Seeing the elderly volunteer smile despite his poverty gave me a life-changing epiphany about true happiness.

def_zh: 頓悟；令人大開眼界的新發現；被揭露的驚人真相
def_en: a surprising and previously unknown fact, especially one that is made known in a dramatic way
prep_trap: 可數名詞，源自動詞 reveal，常配 an eye-opening revelation。
example: Visiting a recycling plant came as a shocking revelation to students who thought all plastic bins were recycled.

def_zh: 令人大開眼界的經歷；發人深省的事（可數名詞）
def_en: an event, experience, or fact that is unexpectedly enlightening or surprising
prep_trap: 可數名詞，前面配 an（The poverty simulation camp was a real eye-opener for us！），遊學團或義工報告結尾必背！
example: Spending a day in a wheelchair was a real eye-opener that showed us the daily struggles of disabled citizens.

def_zh: 警鐘；當頭棒喝的警告（促使社會或個人猛然醒覺的事件）
def_en: a thing that alerts people to an unsatisfactory situation and prompts them to remedy it
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 議論文評論意外事故、極端天氣或身體亮紅燈時必背：serve as a timely wake-up call！
example: The record-breaking black rainstorm should serve as an urgent wake-up call regarding climate change.

def_zh: 分水嶺
def_en: turning point
prep_trap: 可數名詞。
example: The policy marked a watershed moment.

def_zh: 轉捩點（人生、比賽或歷史的關鍵轉折）
def_en: a time at which a decisive change in a situation occurs, especially one with beneficial results
prep_trap: 可數名詞，記敘文與演講辭極高頻詞組：mark a major turning point in my life。
collocations: major turning point in my life
example: Joining the voluntary service team in Form Four proved to be a major turning point in my personal growth.

def_zh: 十字路口；人生或發展的關鍵抉擇時刻（雖有 s 但配 a crossroads）
def_en: a point at which a crucial decision must be made that will have far-reaching consequences
prep_trap: 必考文法：crossroads 單複數同形，必配 stand AT a crossroads（正處於人生或發展的十字路口）！
example: After receiving their DSE results, Form Six graduates stand at an important crossroads in their lives.

def_zh: 關鍵時刻；重要關頭（必配 at this critical juncture）
def_en: a particular point in events or time
prep_trap: 單數名詞，DSE 議論文呼籲政府或社會把握當下關鍵時刻採取行動的 5** 片語：At this critical juncture, we must...！
example: At this critical juncture, Hong Kong must invest heavily in green technology to remain competitive.

def_zh: 懸崖峭壁；（比喻災難或破產的）危險邊緣
def_en: a very steep rock face or cliff, especially a tall one, OR the verge of a dangerous situation
prep_trap: 單數名詞，常配 stand on the precipice of climate catastrophe（處於氣候災難的懸崖邊緣）。
example: Scientists warn that humanity stands on the precipice of irreversible ecological damage if emissions continue to rise.

def_zh: 邊緣（常指絕種、破產或崩潰的危險邊緣）
def_en: an extreme edge of land before a steep slope, OR a point at which something, typically something unwelcome, is about to happen
prep_trap: 單數名詞，必配介詞 on ... of：on the brink of extinction / collapse / bankruptcy（瀕臨絕種/崩潰/破產邊緣）！
example: Conservation breeding programmes have successfully pulled the black-faced spoonbill back from the brink of extinction.

def_zh: 邊緣；瀕臨某狀態（必配 on the verge of）
def_en: an edge or border, OR the point at which something is about to happen
prep_trap: 單數名詞，必考片語：on the verge of tears / collapse / extinction（快要哭出來 / 瀕臨崩潰 / 瀕臨絕種）。
collocations: on the verge of giving up
example: When I was on the verge of giving up on mathematics, my teacher stayed after school to tutor me.

def_zh: 門檻（如公屋入息門檻或大學收生門檻）；新時代的開端
def_en: a strip of wood or stone forming the bottom of a doorway, OR the level or point at which something starts to happen or take effect
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 兩大必考用法：lower the income threshold（放寬入息申請門檻）及 on the threshold of adulthood（踏入成年的門檻）！
collocations: on the threshold of a new era
example: Raising the income threshold for welfare allowances helps more working-poor families receive financial support.

def_zh: 天花板；最高上限（如資助上限或職場無形晉升障礙 glass ceiling）
def_en: the upper interior surface of a room, OR an upper limit set on prices, wages, or expenditure
prep_trap: 可數名詞，DSE 必考兩大用法：set a price/rent ceiling（設定價格/租金上限）及 break the glass ceiling（打破女性職場晉升的玻璃天花板）！
example: More female executives are breaking the glass ceiling and taking up top leadership roles in finance.

def_zh: 上限（收費、人數或碳排放上限，亦可作動詞：設定上限）
def_en: an upper limit imposed on spending or other activities
prep_trap: 可數名詞或及物動詞，必配介詞 on（put a cap on tuition fees / class size 設定學費/每班人數上限）。
collocations: put a cap on working hours
